### 14.8 Delivery label

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Sending… | Touch only, client-side, while a send is in flight |
| Sent | Saved, waiting for an agent to fetch it |
| Delivered | An agent fetched it; in a group, any member |
| Not delivered | Failed, shown in red with a menu: Try Again (only while it is the newest message), Edit and Send, Delete |

- **Desktop:** 9.5 px `--label-3` under every message you sent, 5 px in from the trailing edge.
- **Touch:** caption2 `--label-2`, only under your latest message and under failed messages. This is the better rule.
- **Retries:** after 0, 2, 5 and 15 s, under the same id, only while the message is the newest.

## 15. Patterns

| Pattern | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Run grouping | Name above the first message of a run, avatar beside the last, a spacer in between (touch rules; better than desktop's avatar-on-every-message) | [08 §3.4.3](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md) |
| Three-rule auto-scroll | At the bottom means within 2 px. Stick only while at the bottom; your own message always scrolls; incoming messages scroll only when you were following; nothing moves while you read. Save `{messageId, offset, isAtBottom}` at the end of a gesture, on hide and on quit | [03 §2.14](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md) |
| Paging | Open on the newest page (100 on desktop, 50 on touch) or from the saved reading message. A top sentinel loads the previous page. Rows are keyed by id; pin the first shown row so new messages extend the list | [03 §2.14](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md) |
| Unread | One flag per conversation (not a count). Set by a new agent message while the conversation is not viewed. Cleared by selection, focus, any input in the pane, composer focus or typing, scrolling, sending. The badge counts conversations | [07 §2.5](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md) |
| Status precedence | Working > failed > all ready > idle, as one tested function. The tooltip lists "{Name}: {detail}" per member | [07 §2.4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md) |
| Optimistic send | Show the message at once; retry after 0, 2, 5 and 15 s under the same id, only while it is the newest; on failure offer Try Again, Edit and Send, Delete | [07 §2.9](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md) |
| Reserved layout | Reaction overhang on every row; media sized before loading; wells at fixed heights; composer heights stable; call timer width reserved | 03, 05 |
| Commit, then publish | Snapshot, write everything, restore on any failure, then update the screen and restart the agent | [05 §2.5](analysis/05-bots-groups-profiles.md) |
| Delayed progress | Background checks never flash a spinner: show it only after 300 ms, and keep it in layout at opacity 0 | [06 §2.2](analysis/06-settings-harness-usage-activity.md) |
| Refresh on return | Re-check external state (sign-ins, permissions, installs) when the app regains focus | [06 §2.2](analysis/06-settings-harness-usage-activity.md) |
| Sequential modals | Open the next sheet only after the previous popover or sheet has closed | [05 §2.3](analysis/05-bots-groups-profiles.md), [08 §5](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md) |
| Links, not live state | A shared live resource (browser tab, computer, app) is posted as a link plus a snapshot taken when shared; the live view opens on click | [09 §7.2](analysis/09-companion-apps-and-website.md) |
| Effects as a side channel | Expiring, rate-limited, claimed once, foreground only, with a still fallback | [03 §2.18](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md) |
| Typing never re-renders history | The draft is read only inside the composer; prove it with a render-count test | [03 §2.14](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md) |

## 16. Content design

Noodle's copy rules come from its `ui-copy` skill, its docs and its strings. Full inventory and changelog-derived decisions: [analysis/10](analysis/10-copy-content-accessibility.md).

- **Functional labels only.**
  - No persistent instructional hints, shortcut legends or explanatory footers.
  - Optional guidance goes in tooltips or documentation.
  - A disabled control explains itself through its placeholder or tooltip.
- **Ellipsis.** End a label with "…" (the single character, never three dots) only when the command needs more input before it can run: "Rename…", "Edit…", "Add Tools…", "Choose Image…", "Settings…". Do not use it:
  - for "New Bot" or "New Group", even though they open a form;
  - for "Remove", "Delete Plan" or "Quit", where a confirmation is not more input;
  - for "Invite", whose sheet only shows a code;
  - on links to System Settings or web pages;
  - on menu toggles.
- **Row actions.** Keep a row to its main controls. Secondary actions and per-item switches go into its "…" menu: switches as checkmark items above a divider, the destructive action last. Buttons inside rows are link-style.
- **Destructive confirmations.**
  - The title names the object ("Delete Bot?", "Remove "Notion"?").
  - The message states what happens and what is kept ("The bots in the group will not be deleted.", "Your sign-in is kept.", "Its workspace, memory and messages are kept.").
  - The confirm button is the verb ("Delete Bot", "Remove Tool"); Cancel is the default action.
- **Errors.** Plain sentences that say what to do: "Choose a key with Command (⌘), Control (⌃) or Option (⌥).", "The microphone isn't responding. Reconnect it or choose another…", "Enter a valid HTTPS server URL.". Validation messages name the fix: "Use X instead".
- **Status words.** Plain states: "Ready", "Signed in", "Sign-in required", "Needs attention", "Reconnecting", "Checking…", "Not installed", "Agents paused", "Unavailable".
- **Capitalisation.**
  - *Title Case:* commands, buttons, menu items, tabs, window and sheet titles, empty-state titles ("Change Background…", "Show in Main Window", "No Usage").
  - *Sentence case:* settings switch labels ("Keep Mac awake while agents work"), captions, explanations, sentence tooltips, placeholders, status text, bot descriptions.
  - *Lowercase:* inline status tags ("restricted", "unrestricted", "apps").
  - Noodle's Mac and iPhone disagree in places ("Preview web links" against "Preview Web Links"): apply one rule on every platform.
  - In OpenCompany, follow its own sentence-case voice (section 19).
- **Spelling and typography.** British English ("colour", "licence", "cancelled", "recognise"), with a few American slips to avoid ("customize", "license"). Curly quotes and apostrophes. Never three dots. Mostly uncontracted ("cannot", "does not": about 238 literals, against about 15 contractions).
- **Tone in the chrome.** Second person, with Noodle named in the third person. Never "we", never an apology. Exclamation marks almost never appear: the only two are a sample bubble and the starter greeting, which is written in the user's voice.
- **Naming.**
  - Bot (a user-facing agent), Group (several bots with a shared goal), Harness (the agent runtime: Codex, Claude Code…), Backstory (private role prompt), Description (public), Noodlet (a small app a bot builds), Computer, Browser, Applet, Hub.
  - "Kick" means recovering a failed bot, not removing anyone.
  - Archive keeps everything but stops a bot or group from running or receiving messages.
- **Demo content.**
  - Personas have a first name, an illustrated portrait with a role prop, a one-line public description and a private backstory.
  - The starter team is a Personal Assistant, a Full-Stack Developer and a Researcher in a group called "Team", greeted with "Welcome to the team! Please introduce yourselves, and tell me what you are best at and how you can help me."
  - Generated names are "Real" (110 first names) or "Playful" (descriptor plus companion, such as "Clever Otter").
- **Agent-facing conventions.**
  - Reactions double as work signals: 👀 received, ⏳ working, ✅ done. Outdated work reactions are removed.
  - Reactions and system notices are "not a new request". Bots must not send routine acknowledgements or create reply loops.
  - On a heartbeat with nothing to do, a bot finishes silently. After a recovery it never announces the restart.
  - Effects are rare and never replace a reply.

### 16.1 Four registers

| Register | Where | Rules | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| App chrome | Labels, menus, settings, dialogs, errors | Functional and terse; states the consequence and what is kept | "Saving restarts the bot. Its workspace and history stay unchanged." |
| Bot messages | Default agents, demos | Outcome first ("Done.", "Sorted:", "Found it."); exact figures with units and the comparison that matters; bold for the one thing to notice; options as a numbered list of bold names plus one sentence each; end with one decision or commitment ("Shall I?"); name teammates ("Sol has the running total…"); no emoji in the body | "B is winning, and clearly: **9.4% against 5.9%**. With a thousand visitors on each side, that is not noise." |
| User docs | Help, READMEs | Task-led headings ("Give an agent a job"); imperative; UI names in bold; paths with `→`; limits stated plainly; nothing about code | "Turning unrestricted access off does not undo completed actions…" |
| Marketing | Website, films | Short declarative headlines ending in a full stop; contractions allowed | "Private by default." "Signed in, so they don't have to ask." |

### 16.2 More rules, with examples

| Rule | Examples |
|---|---|
| **Confirmation is asymmetric.** Confirm only what destroys data or widens access. Narrowing access, archiving and reversible changes apply at once | "Allow Unrestricted Access for {name}?" / "Allow Unrestricted Access". Turning it off applies with no prompt |
| **Dialog anatomy.** The title is a question naming the object. The body says what is lost, what is kept and any side effect, plus "This cannot be undone." only when true. The confirming button repeats the verb and the noun. Names go in curly quotes | "Delete Bot?" / "“{name}”, its workspace, and its direct conversation will be permanently deleted. It will also be removed from every group. This cannot be undone." / "Delete Bot", "Cancel" |
| **Three-part errors.** What happened to whom; what to do, with the exact place to do it; what is kept. Use one word for survival: "kept" | "Grok Build's usage limit has been reached. Once usage is available again, right-click the bot and choose Kick to resume. Unfinished work is preserved." |
| **Empty states.** A Title Case title and at most one sentence; no illustration; a button only when it is the only way forward. With nothing selected, the detail pane stays empty | "No Usage" / "No tokens were used in this period."; "Set Up Your First Bot" only when there are no bots |
| **Placeholders.** The composer reads "Message {name}"; searches read "Search" or "Search tools"; long-text prompts end in "…"; optional fields say "Optional"; examples start with "e.g." | "Briefly describe what this bot does…", "e.g. Notion — Work" |
| **Tooltips.** On icon-only buttons, the command name in Title Case plus the live shortcut in parentheses, generated from the active binding. Explanations are full sentences. Never put essential information only in a tooltip | "Record Voice Message (⇧⌘D)" |
| **Explain on click.** Column headings and status tags are buttons that open a 360 px popover: a headline, what it allows, the default, and what turning it off does and does not undo | Settings, Bots: "Heartbeat", "Unrestricted", "Apps", "Archived" |
| **Progress text.** An "-ing" verb plus "…" for progress; an "-ing" phrase with no ellipsis or full stop for a bot's activity detail | "Checking…", "Restarting runtime…"; "Checking for new messages" |
| **Generated paths.** Build "Settings → Harness" from the live navigation labels, with one separator everywhere. Noodle hard-codes them, and a rename left "Settings → Chat" and "Settings › Harnesses" in its errors | |
| **One word, one meaning.** Noodle uses "Profile" for both a bot's card and a harness sign-in account, and "Kick" needs a gloss. Choose distinct words ("Accounts", "Recover") | |
| **Persona descriptions.** Sentence case, no final full stop, eight words or fewer, written as "Role: scope" or a verb phrase. Backstories are second person: one identity sentence plus one or two working principles | "Analyst: sign-ups, funnels and what actually worked"; "You read the numbers and say plainly what they mean. You never call a result before the sample supports it." |

### 16.3 Direction of travel (from 59 releases in five weeks)

Noodle's changelog moves consistently in eight directions ([10 §3.6](analysis/10-copy-content-accessibility.md)):

1. **Plain names replace technical ones.**
   - MCP connections → Tools;
   - Autonomous → Unrestricted;
   - Chat → Conversation;
   - "Apple Intelligence" for the on-device harness.
2. **Explanations move behind a click.** Footers, notes and badges are deleted; explanations live in popovers.
3. **Fewer steps and controls.**
   - Flows advance by themselves.
   - Pickers lose their Done buttons and close on an outside click.
   - Redundant buttons and needless settings go.
4. **Confirmation is asymmetric** (16.2).
5. **Platform and Messages parity.**
   - the ellipsis rule;
   - link-style row buttons;
   - a subdued destructive red;
   - a Messages-style unread dot and badge;
   - a received sound.
6. **Layout is stable.** Messages do not jump when a reaction lands; the composer does not change height on the first character.
7. **State is honest.** "Delivered" means a bot fetched the message. Failures come with recovery steps. Nothing is ever invented on the person's behalf.
8. **Release notes describe what people now see** ("X now does Y instead of Z"), one entry per visible change.

### 16.4 Localisation

Noodle has none: every string is an English literal, with hand-built plurals ("1 hour" against "{n} hours"), concatenated sentences and capitalised nouns. A web build should start with a message catalogue (ICU) from the first commit:

- `Intl.PluralRules` (or ICU plural selects) for every count;
- `Intl.ListFormat` for name lists, which also settles the serial comma per locale;
- `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `RelativeTimeFormat` and `NumberFormat` for times, durations, token counts, costs and file sizes;
- whole sentences per message, with named arguments;
- logical CSS properties, so bubbles and the sidebar mirror for right-to-left languages;
- a glossary that marks product nouns and harness names as untranslatable.

## 17. Accessibility

Gaps a web build must close are marked **Fix**. Full audit: [analysis/10](analysis/10-copy-content-accessibility.md).

**What Noodle does well.**

- **Icon controls carry names.** Icon-only controls nearly always have a label and a tooltip (172 accessibility labels across the suite), including contextual ones ("Remove {name} from group", "{name}, unrestricted access").
- **Sidebar rows read as one element.** The label is "Unread, {title}, {preview}" and the runtime status is the value; the decorative unread dot is hidden.
- **Custom controls keep native semantics.**
  - The gradient effort track is a standard slider named "Reasoning Effort", with the effort as its value.
  - Reaction badges read "{emoji}, {names}".
  - The welcome wordmark is a header named "Noodle".
- **Decoration is hidden from assistive technology:** the effects layer, and icons inside tiles that already say the same thing.
- **Mobile replaces gestures with named actions.** VoiceOver gets "Copy" and "React" instead of long press, plus the escape action.
- **Settings status labels pair symbol, text and colour.**
- **Media has text alternatives:** transcripts for voice messages and calls.
- **Reduced Motion is honoured almost everywhere**, with still equivalents (10.3).
- **Accessibility names double as test selectors** in Noodle's hidden-window tests.

**Gaps a web build must close** are marked **Fix**.

| Area | Noodle | Web requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Status dots | Colour only; the text is in a tooltip and the row's VoiceOver value | **Fix:** pair the dot with text ("Chloe: working") through `aria-describedby` and the tooltip; consider a shape change for failed (WCAG 1.4.1) |
| Who is speaking in groups | Avatar only on the Mac | **Fix:** the name above the first message of each run (WCAG 1.3.1) |
| Message semantics | No combined element; VoiceOver reads the avatar button, then the text | **Fix:** the list is `role="log"` (polite); each message is an article named with the sender and time, with the delivery state as text; announce each new message once, never per streamed token (WCAG 4.1.3) |
| Headings and landmarks | The conversation title is not a heading | **Fix:** the title is a heading; the sidebar, conversation and composer are labelled landmarks |
| Names | Tooltip and label disagree ("Try Another Name" vs "Generate Another Name"); the disabled Send is a bare image; the backstory editor has no programmatic label | **Fix:** one catalogue entry feeds both the `aria-label` and the tooltip (WCAG 2.5.3); a disabled Send stays a button with `aria-disabled`; every field has a label tied to it |
| Reduced transparency, increased contrast, forced colours | Not read (left to the system) | **Fix:** `prefers-reduced-transparency` and `prefers-contrast: more` swap in opaque tokens (8.4); `forced-colors: active` keeps bubble borders and focus rings |
| Contrast over wallpapers | Dim, forced dark, veil, shade, with wallpapers assumed to be dark | Keep the full stack, and *guarantee* 4.5:1 for text (3:1 for UI parts) with the scrim and plates. Test every preset and a bright photo (WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.11) |
| Animated wallpapers and effects | Stop under Reduce Motion only | **Fix:** a visible pause control for anything that can animate longer than 5 s (WCAG 2.2.2) |
| Reactions | Right-click (desktop) or long press (touch) only | **Fix:** a visible "React" button, the ContextMenu key or Shift+F10, and long press; your own reactions marked `aria-pressed` |
| Annotations | Keyboard shortcut only, by policy | **Fix:** a pointer path (a toolbar or menu item) alongside the shortcut |
| Shortcuts | Eleven rebindable commands with conflict checks; no single-key shortcuts | Keep rebinding and conflict checks. Never use single-character shortcuts (WCAG 2.1.4) or browser-reserved combinations: ⇧⌘R / Ctrl+Shift+R (hard reload), ⇧⌘A / Ctrl+Shift+A (tab search), ⇧⌘D / Ctrl+Shift+D (bookmark all tabs), ⇧⌘C / Ctrl+Shift+C (inspect), ⌘N / Ctrl+N, ⌘T, ⌘W |
| Drag-out of attachments | Drag, plus Copy and Save in the context menu | Keep a non-drag path to the same result (WCAG 2.5.7) |
| Targets | Badges 28, mention chips 22, recording buttons 30 × 36, chip remove buttons small | **Fix:** at least 24 × 24 everywhere (WCAG 2.5.8) and 44 on touch, using padding or pseudo-elements |
| Text size | About 95 fixed point sizes on the Mac: 9.5 px delivery status, 10 px captions | **Fix:** rem-based sizes; nothing people must read below 12 px; reflow at 320 px and work at 200 % zoom (WCAG 1.4.4, 1.4.10) |
| Focus | Tab and Shift+Tab move between list and composer; arrows move through the list; the composer relies on the caret | Visible `:focus-visible` rings, never hidden under the floating composer (use `scroll-padding-bottom`, WCAG 2.4.11); focus returns to the trigger or the composer after a dialog |
| Live status | System | `role="status"` for "Checking…", "Connecting…" and "Restarting…"; `aria-invalid` plus `aria-describedby` for validation |
| Tooltips and popovers | Hover tooltips; explanations in click-opened popovers | Hoverable, dismissible with Escape, persistent while hovered (WCAG 1.4.13); anything needed on touch goes in a click-opened popover |
| Writing aids | Writing Tools disabled in the composer | Do not disable browser spellcheck or grammar in the composer |
| Images | Avatars beside names | `alt=""` for an avatar next to its name; the name otherwise; descriptive alt text on screenshots |
| Process | The pull-request checklist has no accessibility items | Add keyboard path, screen-reader names, reduced motion, contrast over wallpapers and 200 % zoom to the checklist; query by role and name in component tests; run axe on fixture states |

```css
  --font-mono: var(--font-mono);
  --text-meta: var(--text-meta);
  --text-message: var(--text-message);
  --text-row-title: var(--text-row-title);
  --ease-apple: cubic-bezier(.42, 0, .58, 1);
}
```

Gradients and multi-layer backgrounds (bubbles over wallpapers, avatar gradients) stay as custom properties used through `bg-(image:--avatar-grad-0)` or a small component class, because Tailwind colour utilities cannot hold gradients.

### 18.3 Springs (motion)

```ts
export const spring = {
  press:  { type: 'spring', visualDuration: 0.25, bounce: 0 },
  snappy: { type: 'spring', visualDuration: 0.2,  bounce: 0.15 },
  lift:   { type: 'spring', visualDuration: 0.35, bounce: 0.25 },
  morph:  { type: 'spring', visualDuration: 0.4,  bounce: 0.35 },
  brand:  { type: 'spring', visualDuration: 0.7,  bounce: 0.1 },
} as const;
```

## 19. Applying this to OpenCompany

OpenCompany already has a strict token system ([11 §7](analysis/11-opencompany-current-state.md), `docs-internal/theme_system.md`). Adopt Noodle's values through it rather than beside it.

| Noodle token or value | OpenCompany today | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Row title 13.5 / 600; preview 12.5 | `--text-row` 13.5; `--text-meta` 12.5 | Reuse as they are |
| Conversation title 22 / 600 | `--text-title` 22 | Reuse |
| Bubble radius 16; composer 18 | `--radius-panel` 16; `--radius-draft` 18; `--radius-composer` 22 | Reuse the panel radius for bubbles. The pill field is half its height |
| Card 12; row 10 | `--radius-card` 12; `--radius-row` 10 | Reuse |
| Status colours | `status-{working,ready,paused,attention,waiting}-{dot,fill,border,ink}` | Reuse. Keep OpenCompany's vocabulary ("Needs you" = waiting) |
| SF Pro | Geist Variable, plus the system mono stack | Keep Geist. Raise message text to 14 to 15 px, because Geist at 12.5 px is smaller than SF at 12.5 pt |
| Accent and link | shadcn `--primary` (`#2563eb` light, `#3b82f6` dark) and the action-role tokens; there is no separate link token | Map both `--accent` and `--link` to `--primary`. Add a distinct link token only if a separate "system affordance" blue is wanted |
| Glass, materials | Only `--blur-scrim` (6 px) behind dialogs | **Add** a glass tier to `themes/base.css` (blur, saturate) and `light.css` / `dark.css` (background, edge, shadow), bridged in `index.css` |
| Wallpaper stack | none | **Add** `--wallpaper-dim`, `--chat-veil`, `--shade-*` and `--fade-band`. The wallpapered subtree takes the dark token set (`data-appearance="dark"`), not a new theme |
| Bubble tokens | Owner bubble `bg-bg-elevated`; replies bubble-less | **Add** `--bubble-out`, `--bubble-out-ink`, `--bubble-in-glass` (used only over wallpapers, RFC decision D1) |
| Reactions | none | **Add** `--reaction-mine`, `--reaction-other`, `--reaction-ring` |
| Avatar gradients | `AVATAR_CLASS` maps node roles to fills | **Add** `--avatar-grad-0` to `-5` in theme files, defined with hex and `color-mix()` |
| Motion | `--dur-*` and `--ease-*` through `lib/motion.ts` | **Add** `--dur-switch` 160, `--dur-wallpaper` 350, `--dur-select` 120 and spring presets; route every Web Animation through `lib/motion.ts` |
| Icons | lucide-react | Use 11.2 |
| Copy | Sentence case, second person, no decorative emoji | Keep OpenCompany's voice: sentence-case labels ("New employee", "Change background…") with Noodle's ellipsis, row-action and confirmation rules. Reactions per RFC decision D2 |

**Rules that still apply** (CLAUDE.md section 7):

- compose shadcn primitives;
- use `ActionButton` intents for action buttons;
- use token-only Tailwind classes;
- keep opacity arithmetic out of call sites: every tint above is a named token in the theme files;
- use no palette names in components;
- provide a pointer-operable alternative for every functional drag.

**Light and dark.** Home stays light and dark only. The ten stylized skins keep painting `.chat-msg-*` in Dev's console chat, and none of the new glass or wallpaper tokens needs a per-skin value.

doc:docs-internal/research/noodle/RFC-CR.title: RFC: One adaptive UI for browser, desktop and mobile
doc:docs-internal/research/noodle/RFC-CR.content:
# RFC: One adaptive UI for browser, desktop and mobile

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | Draft for discussion. Not accepted; nothing here is built. |
| Date | 2026-10-08 |
| Companion | [RFC.md](RFC.md) (the Noodle-style team chat for Home) and [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md). This RFC decides *where* that UI runs and how it adapts; build both together so Home is not redesigned twice |
| Inspiration | Noodle ships one design across a Mac app and an iPhone client of a server it calls a Hub ([analysis/08](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md), [analysis/09](analysis/09-companion-apps-and-website.md)) |
| Audience | OpenCompany maintainers |

## 1. Recommendation

Build **one adaptive React UI** and run it in **three thin shells**:

| Shell | Technology | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Browser | The existing Vite SPA, made an installable PWA | Exists, needs the PWA layer |
| Desktop | The existing Electron app, with a small typed native bridge | Exists, needs the bridge |
| Mobile (iOS, Android) | A Capacitor app that bundles the same build | New |

The phone is a **client of an OpenCompany server**, never a server itself. The Python backend, Temporal and the bun sidecar cannot run on a phone. The server is the desktop app on your computer, a VM from `company deploy`, or a Docker host. This is exactly Noodle's model: Noodle Mobile is a client of a Noodle Hub.

```
             one React UI (adaptive design system + features)
                 |                    |                     |
        +--------v-------+   +--------v---------+   +-------v-----------+
        | Browser (PWA)  |   | Desktop          |   | Mobile            |
        | service worker |   | Electron 44      |   | Capacitor         |
        | Web Push       |   | preload bridge   |   | native plugins    |
        +--------+-------+   +--------+---------+   +-------+-----------+
                 |                    |   embeds a local     |
                 |                    |   server             |
                 +--------------------v----------------------+
                             OpenCompany server
                     (FastAPI + WebSocket + Temporal + workers)
```

We are not choosing React Native, Flutter or Tauri. They would mean a second UI (or a second desktop shell) for little gain; section 4 explains why, and when to revisit.

## 2. Principles

1. **One UI, many shells.** Features are written once. Shells contribute capabilities (notifications, windows, push, share), never screens.
2. **Adapt to capability, not to platform name.**
   - Layout follows window size and container size.
   - Interaction follows input modality (pointer, hover, touch).
   - Native features follow detected capabilities.
   - Components never test `isElectron` or `isIOS`.
3. **Brand-consistent visuals, platform-native behaviour.** One look everywhere. Each platform keeps its own behaviour: shortcuts, back gestures, title bars, notification style, materials, haptics. This is the approach of Linear, Slack, Figma, Notion and Noodle itself.
4. **The phone is a remote control for your company.** It reads, approves, talks and watches. Building workflows stays on large screens.
5. **Native where it changes the experience; web everywhere else.** Native means push, share-to-app, the keyboard, haptics, secure storage, windows, OS materials and deep links. Everything else is the shared web UI.
6. **Correct under bad networks.** Sends are idempotent with client ids. Streams resync after gaps. Lists are cached for instant start. The app never assumes the socket is alive.
7. **Budgets are design constraints.** Performance, accessibility and battery budgets are set per form factor before building, not measured afterwards.

## 3. Where OpenCompany stands (verified 2026-10-08)

| Area | Today | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Shells | One SPA (`client/`) served by the backend; Electron 44.3 (`desktop/package.json`) loads it from `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (`desktop/src/main/index.ts:141-178`) | Two of three shells already share one bundle |
| Native bridge | The main Electron window has no preload; only the setup window has one (`desktop/src/main/index.ts:85-101`, `:142-156`). No notifications, badge, global shortcut, deep links or OS materials | The desktop app is a browser window around the SPA; native polish is unclaimed |
| Window chrome | Default frame, `backgroundColor: "#12141f"`, menu bar auto-hidden off macOS | No title bar integration, no Mica or vibrancy |
| PWA | No manifest, no service worker, no `theme-color`; viewport meta is `width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0` only (`client/index.html:6`) | Not installable; no safe-area or keyboard handling |
| Responsiveness | 15 responsive class prefixes across 8 files in `client/src/features`. Home has a fixed 260 px sidebar, 52 px header and 460 px dock | Home is desktop-only today |
| Navigation | No router; Home is an in-memory view switch (`useHomeStore.view`) | No URLs to deep-link into; no back-button or swipe-back semantics |
| Server address | A build-time `VITE_PYTHON_SERVICE_URL`, or same-origin (`client/src/config/api.ts`); the WebSocket URL comes from `window.location` (`client/src/contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx:783-796`); 40 `fetch` calls across 20 files | A bundled mobile app needs a runtime server address and one API client |
| Auth | JWT in an HttpOnly cookie; no token revocation, with `User.is_active` the only lever (CLAUDE.md, Authentication) | Cookies do not cross from an app origin to your server; there are no device sessions |
| WebSocket origin policy | Non-http(s) origins are refused unconditionally, even if listed in `CORS_ORIGINS` (`server/services/authz/ws_session.py:49-89`) | `capacitor://localhost` (the iOS app origin) cannot connect |
| Sync | Chat protocol v2: per-run `seq`, `hub_epoch` resync, idempotent `client_message_id` (`docs-internal/chat_protocol.md`) | Already right for flaky mobile networks |
| Helpful pieces | `react-virtuoso`, `qrcode.react` (pairing codes), `idb-keyval`, TanStack Query persistence, the React Compiler, a three.js orb with a static fallback | Much of the client groundwork exists |
| Fonts | `index.html` loads a large Google Fonts stylesheet for every stylized theme on every page load (`client/index.html:66-79`), while Home uses bundled Geist | Wasteful on mobile; breaks offline and a strict CSP |

## 4. Options and decision

| Option | UI reuse | Native feel | Push and share | Effort | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Responsive web plus PWA only | 100 % | Fair; installable on desktop, Android and iOS 16.4+ | Web Push only (iOS needs the app on the Home Screen); no share-to-app on iOS | S | **Do first.** Cheapest step, and every later shell builds on it |
| **Capacitor** (the same build in native iOS and Android shells) | about 95 % | Good with keyboard, haptics, status bar, splash and back-button plugins | Full: APNs and FCM, share extensions | M | **Recommended for the app stores** |
| React Native or Expo, sharing core logic | 0 % of UI, about 60 % of logic | Best | Full | XL: a second UI for chat, markdown, generated UI, approvals and Canvas | Revisit only if mobile becomes the primary product and the WebView measurably fails its budgets |
| Tauri 2 (desktop and mobile) | about 95 % | Good | Mobile plugins less mature | L: rewrite the desktop host contract in Rust | Not now. The desktop app bundles Python, uv and bun anyway, so Tauri's smaller binary barely matters |
| Flutter or fully native | 0 % | Best | Full | XXL | No |

**Decision.** Ship the PWA layer, keep Electron, and add Capacitor for mobile. To keep the React Native door open, put all logic in a platform-agnostic `core` layer (section 5.1).

## 5. Target architecture

### 5.1 Layers

```
shells/      web (Vite entry, service worker) | desktop (Electron main + preload) | mobile (Capacitor iOS/Android)
ui/          design system (tokens, shadcn primitives, adaptive components) + features (home, chat, editor, settings)
platform/    one adapter interface with capability flags; web | desktop | mobile implementations
core/        wire types (zod), connection (server address, auth, transport, resync), TanStack Query hooks,
             Zustand stores, domain logic (status precedence, delivery labels), i18n catalogue
```

Layering rules:

- `core` imports nothing from React DOM, the browser or a shell.
- `ui` reaches native features only through `platform` (`usePlatform()`).
- Each shell is the only place that imports Electron, Capacitor or service-worker APIs.

Start inside `client/src/`: `client/src/core/`, `client/src/platform/`, a `client/src/app/shell` entry per target. Add a standalone `mobile/` package beside `desktop/` (Capacitor project; like `desktop/`, it is not a root workspace member). Split folders into packages only when a second consumer actually exists.

### 5.2 The platform adapter

```ts
export interface Platform {
  kind: 'web' | 'desktop' | 'mobile';           // telemetry and diagnostics only; never branch UI on it
  os: 'macos' | 'windows' | 'linux' | 'ios' | 'android' | 'unknown';
  capabilities: {
    notifications: boolean; push: boolean; badge: boolean; haptics: boolean;
    shareTarget: boolean; nativeMaterials: boolean; multiWindow: boolean;
    globalShortcuts: boolean; secureStorage: boolean; biometrics: boolean;
  };
  notify(n: { title: string; body: string; route: string; tag?: string }): Promise<void>;
  setBadge(count: number): Promise<void>;
  haptic(kind: 'selection' | 'light' | 'medium' | 'success' | 'warning'): void;
  share(data: { title?: string; text?: string; url?: string; files?: File[] }): Promise<void>;
  openExternal(url: string): Promise<void>;
  openWindow(route: string, opts?: { floating?: boolean }): Promise<void>;   // desktop pop-outs
  secureStore: { get(k: string): Promise<string | null>; set(k: string, v: string): Promise<void>; remove(k: string): Promise<void> };
  onDeepLink(handler: (route: string) => void): () => void;
  onResume(handler: () => void): () => void;                                    // foreground: resync
  keepAwake(on: boolean): Promise<void>;
}
```

**Implementations**

| Shell | Built on |
|---|---|
| Web | Notification API plus a service worker, the Badging API, the Web Share API, and `visibilitychange` |
| Desktop | A preload exposing a typed `window.opencompanyDesktop` through `contextBridge` (keep `contextIsolation` and `sandbox` on) |
| Mobile | Capacitor plugins: App, Keyboard, Haptics, Share, Push Notifications, Status Bar, Splash Screen, a secure-storage plugin |

Missing capabilities degrade quietly: if `haptic` is unavailable it does nothing, and `openWindow` falls back to in-app navigation.

### 5.3 Connection, identity and pairing

**1. Runtime server address.**

- Replace the build-time base URL with a `connection` module in `core`: the server URL, an auth state, and a WebSocket factory.
- Route all 40 `fetch` calls through one API client that adds the base URL, credentials and auth.
- The browser and desktop default to same-origin, as today. Mobile reads the address from pairing.

**2. Pairing by QR code.**

- On a signed-in screen, Settings › Devices › Add Device shows a QR code (`qrcode.react` is already a dependency). It encodes the server URL and a single-use invitation that expires after about 10 minutes, like Noodle's 15-minute Hub invitations.
- The phone scans it, proves possession over HTTPS, and receives a device-bound refresh token.
- The token is stored in the Keychain or Keystore through secure storage, never in `localStorage`.

**3. Token auth beside cookies.**

- Keep the HttpOnly cookie for same-origin browser and desktop use.
- Add bearer access tokens (short-lived) for app origins.
- Add a single-use WebSocket ticket from an authenticated `POST`, used as `wss://…/ws/status?ticket=…` with a TTL of 60 s or less. Browsers cannot set headers on a WebSocket, and a long-lived token in a URL ends up in logs.

**4. Device sessions and revocation.**

- A `device_sessions` record holds a name, platform, created time, last-seen time and revoked time.
- Settings › Devices lists them, with Revoke.
- This closes today's "no token revocation" gap for every client, not just phones.

**5. Origin policy.** Extend `ws_session.py` and CORS with an explicit allow-list of app origins: `capacitor://localhost` on iOS and `https://localhost` on Android, by default. Admit them only with login on and a valid device token. An `Origin` header is not a security boundary for native apps; the token is.

**6. Login is required for remote access.** Any server reachable from another device must have login on, TLS, and the device-token flow. Multi-user data isolation is not required for one owner with several devices.

**7. Version skew.**

- App-store clients lag the server by days or weeks.
- The server returns `protocol_version` (the chat protocol already does) plus a minimum supported client version. A client outside the range shows "Update OpenCompany" rather than failing strangely.
- Protocol changes stay additive for at least one release, and CI tests the N−1 client against the N server.

**8. Reachability.** This is decision D4. The options:

- **A deployed VM.** `company deploy` already gives HTTPS and login.
- **The desktop app as a hub, through a tunnel** (Tailscale, or Cloudflare Tunnel).
- **A LAN-only mode**, with TLS caveats.

Never bind the desktop backend to `0.0.0.0` by default.

### 5.4 Notifications and push

| Shell | Mechanism | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Browser (tab open) | In-page sound plus the title badge; the Notification API when the tab is hidden | Today's broadcasts are enough |
| Browser (installed PWA, closed) | Web Push with VAPID keys generated by each server | Self-hostable, no vendor. iOS requires the PWA on the Home Screen (16.4+) |
| Desktop | Native notifications through the preload, a dock or taskbar badge (`app.setBadgeCount` on macOS and Linux, `setOverlayIcon` on Windows), and a click handler that deep-links to the conversation | Windows needs the AppUserModelID that electron-builder sets for NSIS installs |
| Mobile | APNs (iOS) and FCM (Android) | A shipped app's push credentials belong to the publisher, so a self-hosted server cannot hold them. See below |

**The mobile push relay.**

- Run a tiny OpenCompany relay that forwards *opaque wake-ups* (a conversation id, a badge count, a collapse key) to APNs and FCM.
- The app then fetches the message over its authenticated connection, so message text never passes through Apple, Google or the relay. This is the privacy model Noodle Mobile uses ([analysis/08](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md) §3.15).
- Owners who do not want a relay can bring their own keys (a self-built app) or use the PWA's Web Push.

**Notification content and actions.**

- Collapse to one notification per conversation, and clear it when the conversation is read on any device.
- Approval notifications carry Approve and Reject actions.
- Inline reply is possible on desktop, Android and iOS. It is an improvement over Noodle, which has none.

### 5.5 Navigation and URLs

Introduce URL routes for Home. TanStack Router is the recommendation, for its typed routes and search params alongside TanStack Query; React Router 7 is equivalent.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | Conversation list (phone) or last conversation (desktop) |
| `/e/:employeeId` | Conversation |
| `/e/:employeeId?m=:messageId` | Reveal a message (notifications) |
| `/e/:employeeId/workspace/:tab` | Workspace: browser, board or device |
| `/hire` | Hire flow |
| `/settings/:page` | Settings, including `devices` |
| `/dev/...` | The workflow editor (Dev mode) |

What routes provide:

- browser back and forward;
- Android back and predictive back;
- iOS swipe-back;
- deep links: `opencompany://` on desktop, universal and app links on mobile;
- notification targets;
- shareable links;
- restore after the app is killed.

The current `useHomeStore.view` becomes derived from the route rather than stored beside it.

### 5.6 Offline and sync

| Concern | Approach |
|---|---|
| Fast start and offline reading | Persist the conversation list and the latest page of each recent conversation to IndexedDB, extending today's TanStack persistence. The service worker caches the app shell |
| Sending offline | An outbox of pending messages with `client_message_id`. Retry after 0, 2, 5 and 15 s while the message is still the newest (Noodle's rule), then show Not delivered with Try again, Edit and Delete |
| Coming back | On resume or reconnect, refetch summaries, resubscribe to live runs, and drop stale stream events by `seq` and `hub_epoch` (chat protocol v2) |
| Background on mobile | The OS suspends sockets. Push wakes the user, not the socket; the app resyncs when it comes to the foreground. No background polling |
| Conflicts | The server is authoritative. Drafts are per conversation and per device, never synced |

### 5.7 Security

- Electron keeps `contextIsolation`, `sandbox` and no `nodeIntegration`. The preload exposes narrow, typed functions, with no IPC passthrough.
- Mobile ships bundled assets, not a remote URL (Capacitor `server.url` is for development only). A strict CSP allows only the paired server for `connect-src`.
- Tokens are stored in secure storage. Biometric unlock is an optional Settings toggle. Certificate pinning is optional for VM deployments.
- Pairing invitations are single-use and short-lived. Every device session can be revoked.
- Canvas and workspace HTML keep their sandbox rules on every shell, and are never `allow-same-origin`.

### 5.8 Build and release

| Target | Build | Distribution | Updates |
|---|---|---|---|
| Browser | `vite build` (as today), plus a service worker generated at build time | Served by every server | Ships with the server; the service worker shows "A new version is available. Reload" |
| Desktop | Unchanged, plus the preload bundle | NSIS, DMG and AppImage (as today) | Existing auto-update |
| Mobile | `vite build --mode mobile`, then `cap sync`, then Xcode or Gradle | TestFlight and Play internal testing, then the stores | Store releases. No over-the-air code pushes until store rules and signing are settled |

The mobile build excludes the editor, React Flow, three.js and the stylized-theme fonts. Code-split them so they never load on phones.

## 6. Adaptive design system

### 6.1 Window size classes

These are Material 3's size classes, which are platform-neutral and cover tablets and desktop windows. Components inside a layout use container queries (Tailwind v4 `@container` with `@sm:`, `@md:`), so the chat pane adapts to its own width, whether it sits in the main column, the dock or a pop-out window.

| Class | Width (CSS px) | Home layout |
|---|---|---|
| Compact | below 600 | Stack navigation: the list, then the conversation, then the workspace (a full-screen sheet). A bottom-anchored composer, and a header with back, avatar and name |
| Medium | 600 to 839 | Two panes: a 320 px list and the conversation. The workspace opens as a sheet over the conversation |
| Expanded | 840 to 1199 | A collapsible sidebar (resizable 260 to 380) and the conversation. The workspace is a dock that overlays when opened |
| Large and extra-large | 1200 and up | Sidebar, conversation and persistent workspace dock, as today |

```
Compact (phone)          Medium (tablet / narrow window)     Large (desktop)
+------------------+     +--------+-------------------+      +--------+----------------+-----------+
| < (av) Chloe  .. |     | Search | (av) Chloe     .. |      | Search | (av) Chloe  .. | Workspace |
|                  |     | Pinned |                   |      | Pinned |                | Browser   |
|  conversation    |     | Chloe  |  conversation     |      | Chloe  | conversation   | Canvas    |
|                  |     | Kai    |                   |      | Kai    |                | Device    |
| (+)( Message  ↑) |     |        | (+)( Message   ↑) |      |        | (+)( Message ↑)|           |
+------------------+     +--------+-------------------+      +--------+----------------+-----------+
```

### 6.2 Input modality and density

| Media query | Changes |
|---|---|
| `(pointer: coarse)` | Touch density: controls 44 to 48 px (the Noodle iOS composer is 48); body text 16 to 17 px; gaps of 12 or more; no hover-only affordances |
| `(pointer: fine)` | Desktop density: controls 32 to 36 px (the Noodle Mac composer is 36); 14 to 15 px body; 13.5 and 12.5 px list text |
| `(hover: none)` | Hover action bars become a visible "…" button plus long press; tooltips are not used to carry information |
| `(prefers-reduced-motion)`, `(prefers-reduced-transparency)`, `(prefers-contrast: more)`, `(forced-colors: active)` | As in [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md) sections 8.4, 10.3 and 17 |

Express density as tokens, not per-component media queries:

- `--control-h`, `--row-h`, `--gap`, `--text-body` and `--hit-min` take two value sets.
- The sets switch on `[data-density="touch"]` (set from `(pointer: coarse)`, or forced in the mobile shell).

### 6.3 Component adaptation

The API stays the same; the presentation changes.

| Component | Pointer, expanded | Touch, compact |
|---|---|---|
| Dialog | Centred `Dialog` | Bottom sheet (shadcn `Drawer`, built on vaul) with a drag handle and snap points |
| Popover or picker | `Popover` | Bottom sheet |
| Context menu | Right-click plus a "…" button | Long press (350 ms) opens a lift overlay with the reaction bar and actions (Noodle iOS); the "…" button stays |
| Tooltip | Hover and focus | Not used for information; a long-press hint where useful |
| Sidebar | Resizable column | The root screen of the stack |
| Workspace dock | Docked and resizable | A full-screen route with a close button |
| Composer | 36 px pill; Enter sends | 48 px pill above the keyboard; the field grows upward over the transcript; Return inserts a newline on phones unless the owner changes it (mobile convention) |
| Tables in messages | Inline grid | A card that opens a sortable sheet (Noodle iOS) |
| Row actions | Hover toolbar | Swipe actions (Pin, Mark read), always duplicated in the "…" menu |
| Settings | Left navigation plus a page | A list that pushes pages |

### 6.4 Platform conventions

| Platform | Conventions to honour |
|---|---|
| macOS (desktop) | `titleBarStyle: 'hiddenInset'` with `trafficLightPosition` placing the traffic lights in the sidebar, as Noodle does; `vibrancy: 'sidebar'` behind a transparent sidebar; ⌘ shortcuts; app menu items (Settings… ⌘,); a Dock badge |
| Windows 11 (desktop) | `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` with `titleBarOverlay` (native caption buttons, the app header drawn into the title bar using the `titlebar-area-*` CSS env variables); `backgroundMaterial: 'mica'` (or `'acrylic'` for flyouts) behind transparent regions (verify on the target builds); Ctrl shortcuts; taskbar overlay badge; toast notifications |
| Linux (desktop) | Standard frame, no materials; CSS fallbacks |
| Browser | Native browser chrome. Never take reserved shortcuts (Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Shift+R and others; see [RFC.md](RFC.md) 7.4). ⌘K or Ctrl+K for search. An install prompt only after real engagement |
| iOS | Safe areas (`viewport-fit=cover`, `env(safe-area-inset-*)`); swipe-back; light haptics on selection and send; a share extension ("Send to an employee"); the keyboard accessory pinned to the composer; Dynamic Type respected through the WebView text zoom; no hover affordances |
| Android | Predictive back through the Capacitor App back-button handler; edge-to-edge with insets; notification channels (Messages, Approvals, Status); haptics; `interactive-widget=resizes-content` for keyboard resizing; a share target intent |

### 6.5 Materials and depth per platform

This answers "how do we get Noodle's depth": use real OS materials where the shell has them, CSS where it does not, and opaque surfaces where blur is costly or unwanted.

| Shell | Sidebar and chrome | Floating controls (composer, toolbar) | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS desktop | Native vibrancy (real blur of the desktop and wallpaper) | CSS glass ([DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md) 8.2) | Fills; translucent plates over wallpapers |
| Windows 11 desktop | Mica (the tinted desktop wallpaper, very cheap) | CSS glass | same |
| Browser | CSS glass where `backdrop-filter` is supported and the device is capable; solid otherwise | CSS glass | same |
| iOS | Solid tinted surfaces, or a light CSS blur on the composer only | CSS glass, small surfaces | same |
| Android (mid and low tier) | Solid surfaces (blur is expensive in WebViews) | Solid with a hairline and a shadow | same |
| Any, with reduced transparency | Opaque tokens | Opaque | Opaque |

### 6.6 Tokens as the cross-platform source

- **Source of truth.** Move token values to DTCG JSON (the W3C Design Tokens Community Group format) under `client/src/themes/tokens/`.
- **Generation.** Generate from that JSON, with Style Dictionary or a small script:
  - the existing per-theme CSS files, keeping the hex plus `color-mix()` convention and the `@theme inline` bridge;
  - a small `shell-tokens.json` for native shells: the window background (Electron's `backgroundColor`), the status bar and splash colours, the PWA `theme_color` and `background_color`, and the notification accent.
- **Appearance.** Use `color-scheme` plus `light-dark()` for system appearance. Forced dark over wallpapers stays a subtree token set ([RFC.md](RFC.md) 7.9).
- **Density.** The density token families of 6.2, generated as two value sets.

### 6.7 Type, motion and icons

- **Type.**
  - Use rem-based sizes and respect user font scaling (browser zoom, iOS text size, Android font scale).
  - Desktop body is 14 to 15 px; touch body is 16 to 17 px.
  - Headings use `clamp()` for fluid sizing.
  - Ship only Geist for Home. Load stylized-theme fonts on demand, in Dev mode only, and self-host them for the mobile build.
- **Motion.**
  - Use the View Transitions API for navigation: a push or pop slide on compact, a 160 ms cross-fade between conversations on desktop.
  - Springs go through `lib/motion.ts`.
  - Respect reduced motion; target 60 fps on a mid-range Android phone.
- **Icons.**
  - Use lucide everywhere, at a 2.25 stroke at small sizes.
  - Use platform-appropriate glyphs for share (an iOS square-and-arrow, an Android share node) and for back (an iOS chevron, an Android arrow) through the adapter's `os`.

### 6.8 Accessibility

- WCAG 2.2 AA on every shell (the requirements list is in [RFC.md](RFC.md) 7.16 and [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md) 17).
- Test with each platform's screen reader: VoiceOver (macOS and iOS), TalkBack, NVDA, Narrator.
- Touch targets are at least 44 px; pointer targets at least 24 px.
- Focus is managed on route changes: move focus to the screen heading, and restore it on back.

### 6.9 Budgets (per form factor)

| Budget | Compact (mobile) | Desktop and browser |
|---|---|---|
| JavaScript on first view (Home) | ≤ 200 KB gzip; no editor, React Flow or three.js | ≤ 400 KB gzip; the editor loads lazily |
| Largest Contentful Paint (cold, mid-tier device on 4G) | ≤ 2.5 s, cached shell ≤ 1 s | ≤ 1.5 s from the local server |
| Interaction to Next Paint | ≤ 200 ms | ≤ 100 ms |
| Scrolling a 1,000-message transcript | 60 fps (virtualised with `react-virtuoso`, already a dependency) | same |
| Idle battery | No timers, polling or animation while the app is hidden (the existing `data-page-hidden` pause, extended to video wallpapers and the orb) | same |
| Accessibility | axe clean on fixture states; Lighthouse accessibility ≥ 95 | same |

## 7. What runs where

| Capability | Phone | Tablet | Desktop app | Browser |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Team list, conversations, reactions, voice messages | Full | Full | Full | Full |
| Approvals (Approve, Reject, Undo) | Full, plus notification actions | Full | Full | Full |
| Hire an employee | Full (a guided, mobile-first flow) | Full | Full | Full |
| Workspace: live browser, board, device | View, plus Take control on tablets | Full | Full | Full |
| Employee settings, connectors | Common settings; OAuth through the system browser with a deep-link return | Full | Full | Full |
| Workflow editor (Dev mode) | Not offered (a link that opens on desktop) | Landscape, pointer recommended | Full | Full |
| Credentials with API keys | Paste and save | Full | Full | Full |
| Notifications when closed | Push | Push | Native, while running | Web Push (installed PWA) |
| Pop-out and floating windows | - | - | Yes | Same-origin windows |

## 8. Quality

- **Playwright projects:**
  - Chromium, WebKit and Firefox at desktop sizes;
  - Pixel 8 and iPhone 15 emulation at compact sizes;
  - an iPad at medium size.
  - Visual regression per size class and appearance, using the scenario fixtures from [RFC.md](RFC.md) 8.7.
- **Desktop.** The existing Electron end-to-end smoke tests, plus preload bridge tests (notification, badge, deep link).
- **Mobile.**
  - CI builds both apps (macOS runners for iOS).
  - Maestro (or Appium) smoke flows: pair, open a conversation, send, receive a push, approve.
  - Real devices before each store release.
- **Protocol.** N−1 client against N server compatibility tests, and the minimum-version gate.
- **Release trains.**
  - Server and web ship together.
  - Desktop ships with its auto-updater.
  - Mobile ships through TestFlight and Play internal testing.
  - The protocol stays additive for at least one release.

## 9. Roadmap

This roadmap interleaves with [RFC.md](RFC.md) phases. Build the Noodle-style Home adaptively from its first phase.

| Phase | Scope | Size | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| X0 Adaptive foundation (with RFC phases 0 to 1) | Size classes; container queries; density tokens; modality variants; viewport meta (`viewport-fit=cover`, `interactive-widget=resizes-content`); safe areas and keyboard handling; URL routes for Home; the `core/connection` module and API client; platform adapter with the web implementation; theme fonts loaded on demand | M | Home is fully usable at 360 px wide in WebKit and Chromium emulation; no hover-only actions; back and forward work; no regressions at 1440 px |
| X1 Installable web | Manifest and icons (generated from the brand geometry); `theme-color`; service worker (app-shell cache, offline page, update prompt); Web Push with VAPID; notification click opens the deep link | S to M | Lighthouse "installable"; push arrives on desktop Chrome and on an installed iOS PWA; offline start shows cached conversations |
| X2 Desktop native polish | Typed preload bridge; native notifications and badge; `opencompany://` deep links; ⌃⌥Space-style global quick switcher; pop-out and floating conversation windows; title bar overlay (Windows) and inset traffic lights (macOS); Mica and vibrancy behind transparent regions | M | Notifications deep-link correctly; the badge equals unread conversations; materials verified on Windows 11 and macOS; no `nodeIntegration` |
| X3 Remote clients (server) | Device sessions and revocation UI; QR pairing; bearer tokens and WebSocket tickets; origin allow-list for app schemes (login required); protocol-version gate; CORS for app origins; reachability path per D4 | M to L | A second device pairs, works and is revoked in under a minute; no cookie-dependent path on mobile; security review signed off |
| X4 Mobile apps | Capacitor project (`mobile/`); push relay plus APNs and FCM; share extension and intent; haptics; keyboard and status bar; optional biometric lock; store pipelines | L | TestFlight and Play internal builds pass the smoke flows; push carries no message text; a cold start with a cached shell paints in about 1 s on a mid-tier phone |
| X5 Parity and polish | Offline outbox; tablet two-pane polish; notification inline reply and approval actions; widgets and live activities (optional) | M | The outbox survives an app kill; inline reply works on iOS and Android |

Recommended order: X0, then X1, then X2 (cheap and visible), then X3, then X4. X3 is the real gate for phones, because it is mostly security work.

## 10. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| WebView performance on low-end Android | Budgets in CI; virtualisation; no blur on Android low tier; the editor and three.js never shipped to phones |
| App Store minimum-functionality review (guideline 4.2) for WebView apps | Real native value: push, share extension, offline, haptics, biometric lock. Bundled assets, not a remote website |
| Push needs publisher credentials | An opaque-wake relay; bring-your-own-keys documented; Web Push as the vendor-free path |
| Exposing a home server | Login and TLS required; device tokens; tunnels rather than open ports; revocation |
| Three shells to maintain | The adapter boundary; one bundle; shell code kept small; a CI matrix per shell |
| Version skew with store apps | A minimum-version gate; additive protocol; N−1 tests |
| Electron material APIs vary by OS build | Feature detection with CSS fallbacks; materials are polish, never required |
| Router migration touches every Home entry point | Do it in X0, together with the Noodle-style Home work, behind routes that mirror today's views |

## 11. Decisions for the owner

| # | Decision | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Mobile scope | Home only; Home plus a read-only editor | Home only |
| C2 | Distribution | PWA only; PWA plus the app stores | PWA first (X1); the stores at X4 |
| C3 | Mobile push | An OpenCompany-run opaque relay; bring your own keys; Web Push only | Relay, with bring-your-own-keys documented |
| C4 | Reachability | VM (`company deploy`) only; the desktop app as a hub through a tunnel; LAN mode | VM plus a tunnel option. No open LAN by default |
| C5 | Router | TanStack Router; React Router 7; a minimal hand-written URL sync | TanStack Router |
| C6 | Desktop runtime | Keep Electron; move to Tauri | Keep Electron |
| C7 | Phone send key | Return inserts a newline (mobile convention); Return sends (desktop convention) | Return inserts a newline on phones, with a visible send button |

## 12. Open questions

- **Q1.** Should a phone pair with several servers, as Noodle Mobile joins several Hubs, with a server switcher in the list header?
- **Q2.** Should the desktop app expose itself to paired phones only while it is running, or should a headless always-on mode exist?
- **Q3.** Should Live Activities (iOS) or ongoing notifications (Android) show an employee's long-running work?
- **Q4.** How does the Android device-mirroring workspace (scrcpy over WebCodecs) behave on a phone viewing a phone? It is probably view-only.
