doc:docs-internal/research/noodle/RFC.md.content:
# RFC: A Noodle-style team chat for OpenCompany Home

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | Draft for discussion. Not accepted; nothing here is built. |
| Date | 2026-10-08 |
| Studied | [pdparchitect/noodle](https://github.com/pdparchitect/noodle) 0.50.0, commit `702339e3153025c9fe9582783caff7a19b48ff97` (2026-10-07), Apache-2.0 |
| Companion documents | [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md) (Noodle's design system, translated to web tokens and components) and [analysis/](analysis/) (eleven evidence notes with permalinks into Noodle's source) |
| OpenCompany baseline | Home (Normal mode) and the shared chat as recorded in [analysis/11](analysis/11-opencompany-current-state.md) on 2026-10-08; chat semantics per [chat protocol v2](../../chat_protocol.md) |
| Audience | OpenCompany maintainers deciding whether, and in what order, to build this |

## 1. Summary

Noodle is a native macOS and iOS app that presents AI agents as contacts in a messaging app. Each agent ("bot") has a face, a name, a private backstory and a status dot. It lives in a sidebar of conversations with previews, times and unread markers. Its conversation sits on a wallpaper the owner chose, and several bots can share one conversation. The product works because of dozens of small, consistently applied rules, for example:

- every row reserves room for a reaction badge;
- an empty composer and a one-line composer are the same height;
- state is always derived from facts in a fixed priority order;
- copy never explains itself on screen;
- legibility over any wallpaper is guaranteed by a four-layer recipe.

OpenCompany's Home already has the skeleton of this experience: a team sidebar, a shared chat and a Workspace dock with Browser, Canvas and Mobile tabs. On agent features its chat is richer than Noodle's: streamed runs, steps, generated UI, approvals, branches and citations. What it lacks is the "team you message" layer:

- previews, times and unread state in the sidebar;
- search;
- a conversation identity header;
- grouped message runs;
- personal appearance (avatars, wallpapers);
- reactions;
- rich input (voice messages, annotations, screen capture);
- conversations with several employees.

This RFC proposes adopting Noodle's interaction model in seven phases, ordered so that each ships value on its own:

| Phase | Theme | Server work |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Foundations: tokens, primitives, fixtures | none |
| 1 | Conversation surface | none (client only) |
| 2 | Sidebar, read state, attention | conversation summaries, read marks, search |
| 3 | Identity and appearance | per-conversation appearance store |
| 4 | Reactions and effects | reactions table, agent tools |
| 5 | Rich media | voice message metadata, link unfurls |
| 6 | Group conversations | new conversation model (behind decision D6) |
| 7 | Optional: activity, usage, keybindings, pop-out windows, calls | varies |

Ten decisions need the owner before work starts; they are collected in section 10. The most consequential are:

- **D1:** whether replies get bubbles, which revisits the 2026-10-03 choice of bubble-less replies.
- **D2:** emoji or icon reactions, given the design system's "no decorative emoji" rule.
- **D5:** whether owners may keep sending while an employee works.
- **D6:** how groups map onto workflows.

## 2. Motivation

1. **The owner's first question is "who needs me?".** Noodle answers it from the sidebar alone. Each row shows a status dot (working blue, failed red, ready green, idle grey), the last message's time, a two-line preview, and a blue unread dot ([01 §2.4](analysis/01-app-shell-and-navigation.md)). OpenCompany's sidebar shows a name, a role, a status pip and a pending-drafts badge, but no last message, time or unread state. The server does not store those at all ([11 §8](analysis/11-opencompany-current-state.md)).
2. **The chat should feel calm under load.** Agents produce long, frequent, structured output. Noodle's transcript is built so that nothing moves unless the person moved it:
   - reaction space is reserved on every row;
   - media boxes are sized before they load;
   - the composer never jumps on the first keystroke;
   - the reading position is anchored by message identity, not pixels ([03 §2.14](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)).
   These rules are cheap to adopt and directly reduce the jitter streamed agent output causes.
3. **Personal identity makes a team.** Illustrated avatars and per-conversation wallpapers turn a list of automations into a cast ([05 §2.11-2.12](analysis/05-bots-groups-profiles.md)). OpenCompany offers a photo or an initial on a role colour only.
4. **Some work is naturally multi-agent.** Noodle's group conversation ("Launch week": four bots, one goal line, one thread) is its signature screen ([03 §2.2](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)). OpenCompany's teams delegate behind a lead and never speak in the thread ([11 §8](analysis/11-opencompany-current-state.md)).
5. **Noodle's source is a specification.** Its 110k lines of Swift, 50 releases and a 144 KB changelog record the exact values and the reasons behind them. Reading the code gave us rules, not impressions; this RFC copies rules, not pixels.

## 3. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**

- G1. A Home conversation list that answers "who replied, who is working, who needs me" without opening anything.
- G2. A conversation surface with Noodle's calm: an identity header, grouped runs, a reserved layout, legibility over personal wallpapers, and a composer that never jumps.
- G3. A light acknowledgement channel (reactions) for owners and employees, including status signals from employees ("seen", "working", "done").
- G4. Personal identity: an avatar editor for employees, and appearance for conversations.
- G5. Rich input: voice messages, annotations (text quotes and screen regions) and screen capture.
- G6. Multi-employee conversations, gated by decision D6.
- G7. Keep every existing OpenCompany strength:
  - AG-UI streaming;
  - steps;
  - generated UI;
  - approvals with Undo;
  - edit and regenerate branches;
  - ratings;
  - citations;
  - follow-ups;
  - the Workspace dock.

**Non-goals**

- Native clients. Noodle Mobile, Computer, Browser, Applet and Hub stay out of scope as apps. OpenCompany's equivalents are the web app, the Electron shell, the Workspace dock (Browser, Canvas, Mobile) and messaging channels.
- Sharing employees with other people (Noodle Hub). This needs multi-user data isolation, which `AUTH_MODE=multi` does not provide ([11 §8](analysis/11-opencompany-current-state.md)).
- Replacing OpenCompany's approval cards with Noodle's approval by policy ([07 §2.4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)).
- Copying Noodle's brand: its name, wordmark, icon tile, illustrated cast, scenario content or the website's launch photograph. Apache-2.0 §6 grants no trademark rights, and `stage-launch.jpg` has no stated licence ([09 §11](analysis/09-companion-apps-and-website.md)).
- Voice calls before phase 7.

## 4. Background: Noodle in one page

**Product model** ([07 §2.2](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)):

- **Bot.** A name (1 to 100 characters), a public description (shown to other bots) and a private backstory (never shown).
- **Harness and model.** Codex, Claude Code, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, Muse, FX or Apple Intelligence, plus a model and a reasoning effort.
- **Bot resources.** A workspace folder, up to 16 shared folders, tools (MCP connections, Calendar, Reminders), computers and browsers.
- **Conversations.** Each bot has exactly one direct conversation. A group conversation has 1 to n bots, a name and a description (the goal).
- **Messages.** Append-only, authored by the user, an agent or the system. Each has a delivery state (Sent until a bot fetches it, then Delivered), reactions, attachments and an optional call record.

**Runtime** ([07 §2.1, §2.4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)):

- **Bot process.** Each bot runs as its own harness process, with one snapshot `offline | starting | ready | working | failed` plus a human-readable detail and a typed failure.
- **Posting.** Bots post complete messages through a `messenger` CLI, and the app polls once per second. Nothing streams into the chat; harness output streams into a separate per-bot Activity log.
- **Groups.** Every bot is woken by every message, and only prompt text discourages reply loops.

**Surfaces** ([01 §2.1](analysis/01-app-shell-and-navigation.md)):

- one main window: a split view of the sidebar and the conversation, over a full-bleed wallpaper;
- optional separate and always-on-top floating conversation windows;
- a system-wide "Choose Conversation" grid (⌃⌥Space);
- per-bot Activity HUD panels;
- a Usage window with token and cost charts;
- an 11-tab Settings window;
- four companion apps.

**The rules that make it work** (details in [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md)):

1. **Legibility recipe for wallpapers.** A 25 % black scrim, forced dark appearance, a 28 % chat veil, a 64 pt header shade and a 64 pt top fade mask on the transcript ([03 §2.1-2.3](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)).
2. **Reserved reaction clearance.** 12 pt on the Mac and 16 pt on iOS, on every row, so reacting never moves the conversation ([03 §2.10](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md), [08 §3.4.3](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md)).
3. **Fixed composer height.** Empty and one-line drafts are the same height; the field grows to six lines, then scrolls. On iOS the growth overlays the transcript instead of pushing it ([03 §2.15](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md), [08 §3.4.7](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md)).
4. **Three-rule auto-scroll.**
   - Stick to the bottom only while at the bottom (2 pt tolerance).
   - Always scroll to your own message.
   - Follow incoming messages only if already following.
   - Save the reading position by message identity at the end of a gesture ([03 §2.14](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)).
5. **Status from facts in priority order.** For conversations, working beats failed, which beats all-ready; anything else is idle. For harnesses there is a 10-step derivation. Colours follow one rule: green is usable, orange needs action, neutral is pending, red is reserved for errors and badges ([07 §2.4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md), [06 §2.2](analysis/06-settings-harness-usage-activity.md)).
6. **Content rules.**
   - Functional labels only, with no persistent hints.
   - "…" only when a command needs more input.
   - Destructive actions go last, behind a confirmation that states the consequence and what is kept, with Cancel as the default ([10](analysis/10-copy-content-accessibility.md), [06 §2.2](analysis/06-settings-harness-usage-activity.md)).
7. **Commit, then publish.** Bot edits are transactional and roll back on any failure ([05 §2.5](analysis/05-bots-groups-profiles.md)).
8. **Performance is a design property.**
   - Typing never re-renders the transcript, and a render-probe test proves it.
   - Markdown and link detection are cached.
   - Previews load only for visible rows, after a 300 ms dwell ([03 §2.14](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)).

**Where it falls short.** Each of these is an explicit improvement target here:

- no timestamps or day separators in the transcript;
- no jump-to-latest control;
- no working indicator in the chat;
- reactions reachable only by right-click;
- 12.5 pt message text with no maximum bubble width;
- per-second file polling with O(n) rewrites;
- unbounded group fan-out;
- a single overwritten error slot.

Sources: [03 §4](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md) and [07 §4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md).

## 5. Design principles adopted

Each principle is stated as it applies to OpenCompany, with the Noodle evidence it rests on.

- **P1. Employees are contacts.** Every employee has a face, a name, a status and one canonical conversation, and the sidebar is a conversation list ordered by recent activity, not a roster. *Evidence:* the sidebar rows, ordering and sections ([01 §2.4](analysis/01-app-shell-and-navigation.md)).
- **P2. The chrome recedes; the team and the place carry identity.** Components use system-neutral tokens. Personality comes from avatars, wallpapers and the employees' own words. *Evidence:* Noodle defines no custom colour assets and uses system semantics everywhere ([02](analysis/02-visual-language-and-tokens.md)).
- **P3. Nothing moves unless the person moved it.**
  - Reserve space for things that may appear: reactions, media, the delivery label, call timers.
  - Never change layout from geometry callbacks.
  - Keep heights fixed where lists change.
  *Evidence:* [03 §2.10, §2.14](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md) and [05 §2.15](analysis/05-bots-groups-profiles.md).
- **P4. Legible over anything.** Any user-chosen backdrop gets the full legibility recipe, never a partial one. *Evidence:* [03 §2.3](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md).
- **P5. State from facts.** The server sends facts (phase, failure kind, counts). The client derives labels and colours through one tested function per surface and never stores display text as state. *Evidence:* [06 §2.4](analysis/06-settings-harness-usage-activity.md) and [07 §2.4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md).
- **P6. Say less.** Functional labels, tooltips for guidance, no shortcut legends on screen, and destructive confirmations that state consequences. *Evidence:* [10](analysis/10-copy-content-accessibility.md).
- **P7. Activity is not conversation.** Tool calls, logs and reasoning stay out of the message flow, in disclosures and in an activity surface. This matches OpenCompany's existing steps disclosure and Live work card. *Evidence:* [07 §2.4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md).
- **P8. Keyboard first, never keyboard only.** Every shortcut has a visible path, and every gesture (long press, swipe, right-click, drag) has a pointer-operable equivalent. This tightens Noodle, whose reactions and annotations are keyboard- or right-click-only, and satisfies OpenCompany's WCAG 2.5.7 rule. *Evidence:* [03 §4](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md) and [04 §2.2](analysis/04-rich-media-voice-annotations.md).

## 6. Concept mapping and proposal

Status codes are taken from [11 Mapping table](analysis/11-opencompany-current-state.md): **exists**, **partial** or **missing**.

| Noodle concept | OpenCompany today | Proposal | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bot | Employee (one saved workflow) - exists | Keep. A bot is an employee; no second, lighter agent type in this RFC | - |
| Direct conversation | The chat session whose id is the workflow id - exists | Keep. Introduce a server-side *conversation summary* over sessions (section 8.2) | 2 |
| Group | Teams delegate behind a lead - partial | A new conversation kind with several employees (D6) | 6 |
| Sidebar sections, search, previews, times, unread | One "AI employees" list, no metadata - partial | Pinned, Employees and Groups sections; server search; previews; times; unread dots | 2 |
| Status dot | Status pip with working pulse - exists | Keep server-derived statuses; add the cut-out ring and the group precedence (7.7) | 0, 2 |
| Conversation header | Left-aligned identity in the Home header - partial | A centred "conversation start" hero at the top of the transcript; the compact identity stays in the header | 1 |
| Bubbles | Owner bubble; bubble-less replies - partial | Run grouping. Reply backing per D1 | 1 |
| Delivery label | "Sending…", then the time - partial | Sent, Queued, Delivered under the latest owner message only (D7) | 1 |
| Reactions | Good/Bad ratings - missing | A semantic set of 12, rendered per D2, told to the employee as a note | 4 |
| Wallpaper | Orb layer behind the main column - missing | Per-conversation presets, images and video with the legibility recipe | 3 |
| Avatars | Photo or initial - partial | Gradient plus symbol defaults, the photo kept, generated portraits optional | 3 |
| Composer | Card with "+" (file picker), dictation, slash, chips, Send/Stop - exists | Keep the capabilities. Adopt the geometry rules, a "+" menu and long-paste-to-file | 1 |
| Voice messages | Dictation only - partial | Record, waveform, transcript, player | 5 |
| Annotations, capture | Clipboard paste only - missing | Text-quote and region annotations; `getDisplayMedia` capture | 5 |
| Link previews | Source chips only - partial | Server-side unfurl cards for public URLs | 5 |
| Effects | none - missing | An agent tool for confetti and fireworks, rate-limited, played once | 4 |
| Activity window | Steps disclosure, Live work card - partial | An Activity drawer per employee (optional) | 7 |
| Usage window | Billing tab - partial | Tokens and cost by employee, model and day (optional) | 7 |
| Companions | Workspace dock: Browser, Canvas, Mobile - exists | Keep. Adopt Noodle's card rule: a link plus a snapshot, never live state | 5 |
| Floating windows | none - missing | Electron pop-out windows (optional) | 7 |
| Hub, Mobile app | Deploy targets and messaging channels - partial | Out of scope | - |

## 7. Proposed experience

Values below are the target for OpenCompany. Where they differ from Noodle's, the reason is given. Full specifications are in [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md).

### 7.1 Layout and navigation

```
+--------------------+-----------------------------------------------+------------------+
| Sidebar 300 px     | Conversation column                           | Workspace dock   |
| (resizable         |  wallpaper layer (z-0, this column only)      | (unchanged:      |
|  260-380, persisted|  header shade 64 px + Home header (52 px)     |  Browser,        |
|  as today)         |  transcript (masked top fade)                 |  Canvas, Mobile) |
|  [Search ⌘K]       |   conversation-start hero                     |                  |
|  Pinned            |   runs of messages                            |                  |
|  Employees         |  composer (overlaid at the bottom)            |                  |
|  Groups (phase 6)  |                                               |                  |
|  profile row       |                                               |                  |
+--------------------+-----------------------------------------------+------------------+
```

- **Wallpaper scope.** The wallpaper sits behind the conversation column only (decision D3). Noodle also runs it under the sidebar, which then needs translucent sidebar glass; that is a later option.
- **Routes.** Home stays a single view switch (`useHomeStore.view`). Add `?m=<message id>` deep links to reveal a message, used by notifications. Keep the selected conversation in the store, not the URL, as today.
- **New menu.** "New employee" becomes a "+" menu with "New employee" and, from phase 6, "New group". This matches Noodle's Create menu ([01 §2.3](analysis/01-app-shell-and-navigation.md)).
- **Keyboard.**
  - ⌘K (or Ctrl+K) focuses the sidebar search. ⌘F is the browser's find-in-page, so we do not take it.
  - Up and Down move the selection while focus stays in the list.
  - Tab moves from the list to the composer, and Shift+Tab moves back.
  - Switching conversations cross-fades the transcript over 160 ms ease-out (View Transitions), skipped under reduced motion.

### 7.2 Sidebar

**Rows** follow Noodle's Mac row ([01 §2.4](analysis/01-app-shell-and-navigation.md)):

- **Geometry.** 66 px high, 42 px avatar, 10 px gap.
- **Status dot.** 10 px with a 2 px ring cut out of the avatar.
- **Title line.** The title at `--text-row` (13.5 px, semibold), with the time at 11.5 px in faint ink on the same line.
- **Preview.** Two lines at `--text-meta` (12.5 px, muted).
- **Unread dot.** An 8 px accent dot in the leading inset.
- **Selected row.** Uses `bg-active`.
- **Pending drafts.** The existing pending-drafts badge stays, after the time.

OpenCompany's Home tokens already include 13.5 and 12.5 px steps, so this needs no new type tokens.

- **Preview text.**
  - The last message, as plain text: Markdown stripped, tables replaced with "Sent a table", attachment-only messages shown as "Sent N attachments", and a recording as "Voice message".
  - "No messages yet" when empty.
  - Noodle leaks Markdown into list rows on iOS; we strip it everywhere ([08 §5](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md)).
- **Time.** "8:02" today; "Sep 20" earlier this year; "Sep 20, 2025" otherwise. This improves on Noodle, which always prints the year. Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the user's locale.
- **Ordering.**
  - Pinned first, in pin order.
  - Then by the last message's time, newest first.
  - Renames and settings edits do not reorder. Noodle's rename bump is a pitfall ([07 §4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)).
- **Search.** Live and server-side, over the title, the description, member names and message bodies, case- and diacritic-insensitive. Noodle filters every body on the client, which does not scale. Empty results show "No results for "…"".
- **Context menu** (new shadcn `context-menu` primitive, plus a "…" button on hover and focus so the menu also has a pointer path):
  - Open in Workspace;
  - Pin / Unpin;
  - Change background…;
  - Edit…;
  - Show activity (phase 7);
  - a separator;
  - New session (D4);
  - Delete employee, as today, last.
  Noodle's order and rules are in [01 §2.4](analysis/01-app-shell-and-navigation.md).
- **Empty states.** No employees: today's hire view. A search with no match: the system-style empty result. Nothing else: no text.

### 7.3 Conversation pane

**Conversation-start hero.** A centred block that is the first row of the transcript and scrolls away with it ([03 §2.2](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)):

- an 80 px avatar (a new `xl` size on Home's `Avatar`), which opens the profile card;
- the name at `--text-title` (22 px, semibold);
- for groups, the goal line (13 px, muted, at most 460 px wide) and the member names (12.5 px, muted).

It is shown only when the oldest message is loaded. Today's Home header identity stays as the compact persistent header.

**Transcript rules.** These follow Noodle iOS, which handles groups better than the Mac ([03 §4](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md), [08 §3.4.3](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md)).

- **Runs.** A run is consecutive messages by the same author, with no gap over 5 minutes. The 5-minute gap is our addition.
  - In a group, the author's name sits above the first message of a run, and the 28 px avatar beside the last.
  - Other messages in the run keep a 28 px spacer so bubbles align.
  - In a direct conversation, no avatar is shown beside replies; the hero and header carry identity. This is an alternative to Noodle's Mac, which puts an avatar on every bot message.
- **Spacing.** 12 px between rows: a 10 px gap plus a 2 px clearance, where the clearance plus the gap is the reaction overhang. 3 px between parts of one message.
- **Width.**
  - Prose is capped at `min(100% − 120 px, 720 px)`. Noodle has no cap, which yields 730 px lines on wide windows.
  - Owner messages align right, replies left, and system notices sit centred in an 80 px inset.
- **Times and days.**
  - Day separators ("Today", "Yesterday", "Mon 6 Oct").
  - The exact time on hover and focus of any message.
  - The existing "Sending…, then the time" label under the latest owner message.
  - Noodle has no transcript times at all, which is a known gap.
- **Delivery label.** Under the latest owner message only, plus any message that failed ([08 §3.4.5](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md)). The labels map onto existing chat-protocol facts (decision D7):

  | Label | Meaning |
  |---|---|
  | Sending… | Client-side only |
  | Sent | Saved |
  | Queued | `delivery: queued`, because the employee is paused |
  | Delivered | The run was claimed by the workflow |
  | Not delivered | Failed, with a red mark offering Try Again, Edit and Send, and Delete |

  The retry policy uses Noodle iOS's bounded, idempotent pauses of 0, 2, 5 and 15 s, under the same `client_message_id`, only while the message is still the newest ([07 §2.9](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)).
- **Bubbles.**
  - Owner bubble: today's `rounded-draft` shape, filled with the bubble-out token. With a wallpaper, it becomes translucent glass tinted with the accent.
  - Reply backing per decision D1. The recommended rule: keep bubble-less replies on plain backgrounds, as chosen on 2026-10-03, and give replies a translucent plate (the bubble-in glass token, radius 16) whenever a wallpaper is set, because unbacked text over a photograph fails contrast.
  - The `.chat-msg-user` and `.chat-msg-bot` theme hooks stay.
- **Markdown.** Keep OpenCompany's GFM rendering: headings, lists, code, tables, citations. Noodle deliberately renders inline-only so agent prose reads as chat ([03 §2.6](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)); we do not, because generated reports benefit from structure. One exception: tables longer than 8 rows fold to 6, with a "{n} more rows" control opening a reader that offers sorting and Copy as CSV, as Noodle's table bubbles do ([03 §2.7](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)).
- **Long messages.** Over 1,200 characters or 12 lines, a message folds to 8 lines with "Read more". It expands in place on mobile and opens a reader dialog on desktop ([03 §2.6](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)).
- **Reserved layout.**
  - Every row reserves the reaction overhang.
  - Images reserve their box from server-provided pixel sizes: fit within 300 × 240, minimum 120.
  - The pending-attachment strip and the composer report their height, and the transcript's bottom spacer follows it.
- **Working indicator.** OpenCompany already shows streamed text, steps and a live ring. Keep them. Noodle's lack of any in-chat indicator is a gap, not a model.
- **System notices.** Centred capsules: 11.5 px medium, muted ink, on the glass surface, radius 14. Uses:
  - group membership changes;
  - new session started (D4);
  - restart dividers, as today.

### 7.4 Composer

Keep every current capability: "+", paste and drop, dictation, slash commands, the Web and Ask first chips, Send, Stop and Resume (chat protocol v2). Change the geometry and the entry points ([03 §2.15](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md), [08 §3.4.7](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md)):

- **Field.** A pill: minimum height 36 px on desktop and 48 px on phones, radius half the height. The empty and one-line heights are identical. The field grows to 6 lines, then scrolls; on phones the growth overlays the transcript instead of pushing it.
- **"+".** A 36 px (or 48 px) circular glass button that opens a menu: "Attach File…", "Choose Photo…", a separator, then "Capture Screen…" (phase 5). Phones get a morphing panel with Camera, Photos and Files ([08 §3.4.7](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md)).
- **Mic and Send.** The mic sits inside the pill and swaps to Send as soon as there is text or a pending file. Send is disabled, not hidden, while the draft is empty.
- **Placeholder.** "Message {name}". When disabled, the placeholder states the reason ("{Name} is paused", "Turn on Talk to message {name}"), so no extra hint line is needed.
- **Keys.**
  - Enter sends, unless an IME composition is active (`isComposing` or `keyCode` 229).
  - Shift+Enter and Alt+Enter insert a newline.
  - Escape closes menus.
  - Recording a voice message (phase 5) gets a configurable shortcut. Noodle's own bindings cannot be copied into a browser:

    | Noodle binding | Browser action it collides with |
    |---|---|
    | ⇧⌘D, Ctrl+Shift+D | Bookmark all tabs |
    | ⇧⌘A, Ctrl+Shift+A | Tab search |
    | ⇧⌘R, Ctrl+Shift+R | Hard reload |
    | ⇧⌘C, Ctrl+Shift+C | Element inspector |
    | ⌘N, Ctrl+N | New window (reserved) |

    The Electron shell can use Noodle's set unchanged ([10 §4.2](analysis/10-copy-content-accessibility.md)).
- **Long paste.** Text over 1,200 characters or 12 lines becomes a "Pasted Text.txt" attachment and leaves the draft untouched ([03 §2.15](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)).
- **Drafts** are kept per conversation in the existing `composerStore` and persisted per viewer. Whitespace-only drafts are discarded.
- **While a run is live** (decision D5):
  - Today a second send is refused with `run_in_progress`.
  - Noodle always lets people send; messages queue, or interrupt the bot when they look like a stop or a correction ([07 §2.4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)).
  - Recommended: allow queued follow-ups, delivered when the run ends, shown as "Queued", with Stop available as today.
- **@mentions** (phase 6). Typing `@` after whitespace or one of `([{,:` opens a list of employees: participants first, then the others. Choosing one inserts the plain name. The slash-menu component is the pattern. Port Noodle's trigger rule exactly ([03 §2.16](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)).

### 7.5 Reactions

- **Semantic set.** Twelve keys, in Noodle's order: love, like, dislike, laugh, celebrate, question, seen, working, done, thanks, fire, idea ([03 §2.10](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)).
- **Storage.** Keys, never codepoints, so rendering is a design decision (D2):
  - **Option A:** emoji, as Noodle has them.
  - **Option B:** lucide icons, recommended given the design system's "no decorative emoji" rule: Heart, ThumbsUp, ThumbsDown, Laugh, PartyPopper, CircleHelp, Eye, Hourglass, CircleCheck, HandHeart, Flame, Lightbulb.
- **Who reacts.**
  - The owner reacts through a hover or focus "React" button, the message context menu (desktop) or a long press (touch).
  - Employees react through a `react_to_message` tool. This gives them a quiet way to signal seen, working and done, the same convention Noodle's bot skill teaches ([07 §2.7](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)).
- **Badge.**
  - Overlapping badges hang 12 px above the first bubble's top-right corner, 5 px outside it, each overlapping the previous by 6 px.
  - Each badge is a minimum of 28 × 28 px. When it shows a count it gets 7 px side padding.
  - The owner's own reactions use the accent tint.
  - Clicking opens a popover listing who reacted, with Change and Remove.
  - No layout shift, because the overhang is reserved.
- **Reaching the employee.** An owner reaction becomes a `[reaction]` note on the employee's next turn, following the existing `[feedback]` precedent (`services/chat/notes.py`). Reactions never start a run by themselves.
- **Ratings.** Good and Bad stay as they are. They are ratings with a learning purpose, and Like and Dislike do not replace them (open question Q3).

### 7.6 Attachments, cards and link previews

- **Card family.** Keep the current attachment display and the document cards, and adopt Noodle's card sizes and rules ([03 §2.17](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md), [09 §7.3](analysis/09-companion-apps-and-website.md)):
  - images fit 300 × 240 with a minimum of 120, radius 13;
  - documents are 280 wide with a 165 px thumbnail area;
  - link cards are 280 × 220;
  - app and noodlet cards are 304 wide with a 150 px thumbnail.
  - Selected: scale 1.01 plus an accent glow, over 120 ms.
- **Companion cards.** Browser pages, devices and Canvas items shared into the chat are a link plus a snapshot taken when shared, never live state. Clicking opens the live view in the Workspace dock ([09 §7.2](analysis/09-companion-apps-and-website.md)). Only the server may mint these card types: an employee can post only resources assigned to it.
- **Link previews** (phase 5):
  - The server unfurls the first public `http(s)` URL in a message: at most 2,048 characters, no credentials, no private, loopback, link-local or `.local` hosts, with a DNS-resolution check.
  - Results are cached for 7 days and failures for the session.
  - The client asks only after the card has been in view for 300 ms, with a 10 s deadline.
  - No preview is shown when an attachment already carries the same URL ([03 §2.11](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)).
- **Context menu.** Copy, Copy as CSV (tables), Save…, Open; then "Use as background" and "Use as photo" for images, each confirmed ([03 §2.12](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)). Every drag-out has the Save… path as its pointer equivalent (WCAG 2.5.7).

### 7.7 Status, attention and notifications

- **Status vocabulary.** Keep the server-derived employee statuses (working, ready, paused, attention, waiting or "Needs you") and their `--status-*` tokens.
- **Group dot precedence.** Needs you, then attention, then working, then ready, then paused/idle. This deliberately differs from Noodle's working > failed > ready > idle: in OpenCompany "Needs you" is an owner action, and actionable comes first. Write it as one tested function, as Noodle does ([07 §2.4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)).
- **Dot rendering.** Cut out of the avatar with a CSS mask so it reads on any wallpaper. Sizes: 10/2 px (dot/ring) on 42 px list avatars; 7/1.5 px on 20 px header avatars; `max(8, 0.24 × size)` on large avatars ([03 §2.2](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md), [08 §3.16](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md)).
- **Unread.**
  - A per-conversation flag, set by a new employee-authored message while the conversation is not being viewed.
  - "Viewed" means selected, with the page visible and focused.
  - Cleared by selection, focus, pointer or key input, scrolling, composer focus or input, and sending.
  - Read marks are monotonic per principal on the server, so tabs and devices agree ([07 §2.5](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)).
- **Notifications.**
  - When the tab is hidden or unfocused: a Web Notification per new employee message. The title is the employee's name, the body is the plain-text preview, and in groups the group name is added. Clicking reveals the message.
  - When visible but on another conversation: the message-received sound from the existing sound packs.
  - The Electron shell uses native notifications.
  - No message text goes through any third-party push service. If remote push is ever added, the service worker fetches the text from our own server, as Noodle Mobile does ([08 §3.15](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md)).
- **Tab title badge.** The number of unread conversations, not messages.

### 7.8 Employee identity

- **Avatar editor.** A dialog, 440 px wide ([05 §2.11](analysis/05-bots-groups-profiles.md)):
  - a 104 px preview;
  - "Image": Choose File… (the existing upload path) and Create Image… (optional, through a configured image model);
  - "Colour": six gradient swatches;
  - "Symbol": a 6-column grid of 12 lucide glyphs mapped from Noodle's set (Sparkles, Zap, Brain, Hammer, Terminal, Search, Package, Paintbrush, BadgeCheck, Bug, WandSparkles, Cog).
  - New hires get a gradient-and-symbol avatar by default instead of an initial.
- **Profile card.** A 320 px popover opened from avatars ([05 §2.9](analysis/05-bots-groups-profiles.md)):
  - an 88 px avatar and the name;
  - a status capsule: the employee's self-set one-line status, at most 60 characters, or the state label;
  - the public description (role and summary);
  - an action row: Message, Open Workspace, Edit, Usage (phase 7).
  - It dismisses on an outside click; an editor never does.
- **Public description vs backstory.** OpenCompany's hire-written instruction already plays the role of Noodle's private backstory. It stays private; only the role and summary show.

### 7.9 Conversation appearance (wallpaper)

- **Sources** ([05 §2.12](analysis/05-bots-groups-profiles.md)):
  - Default;
  - four presets (Sunset, Ocean, Forest, Dusk), each three hex stops plus a blurred ellipse, exact values in [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md);
  - an uploaded image (up to 50 MB, re-encoded to 2560 px JPEG);
  - an uploaded video (MP4 or WebM, up to 200 MB in phase 3, muted, looping);
  - "Use as background" from a chat image.
- **Rendering.**
  - A non-default background adds a black 25 % scrim and switches the conversation column's subtree to the dark token set (`data-appearance="dark"`) with a 350 ms cross-fade.
  - The new image is decoded before the cross-fade, so the pane never flashes empty.
  - Video pauses when hidden, under `prefers-reduced-motion` (the poster shows), and under `prefers-reduced-transparency`, which also switches surfaces to opaque fills.
- **Storage.** Appearance is the owner's, not the employee's. Keep it out of the employee's workspace, where agents can read files (Noodle: "kept out of message delivery and the agent workspace"). Decision D10.
- **Editor.** A 520 px dialog: a 210 px live preview with two sample bubbles, five swatches, "Choose Background…" and Apply. Opening it from Edit applies only on Save.

### 7.10 Rich media (phase 5)

All four specifications are in [04](analysis/04-rich-media-voice-annotations.md), which includes a web translation for each.

**Voice messages.** Recording replaces the pill with a recording bar:

- discard (Escape);
- a red dot;
- a live scrolling waveform: 2.5 px bars every 5 px, a fixed dB window from −60 to −12, 50 ms buckets;
- the time;
- stop and send (Return).

The recording is sent as an audio attachment that carries its transcript (through the existing `transcribe_audio`), its duration (at most 600 s) and a 100-point waveform. It is played by a 270 px card with a 60-bar waveform; clicking the waveform seeks. A partial transcript is never sent silently: if transcription fails, the owner gets "Retry Transcription" and "Send Audio Only".

**Annotations.**

- *Text quote:* select text in a message, then use the context menu item "Annotate…" or a configurable shortcut.
- *Region:* a toolbar button or a configurable shortcut. Noodle's ⇧⌘A and ⇧⌘R collide with browser tab search and hard reload, so they are not the web defaults. The pointer path is something Noodle omits on purpose ("Annotating is by keyboard shortcut only"); we add it to satisfy P8.
- A crosshair overlay over a frozen snapshot of the pane, with an orange selection (14 % fill, 3 px stroke).
- Anything under 4 × 4 px becomes a 16 × 16 marker.
- A comment popover: "What should change?", ⌘↩ saves.
- The result is a draft attachment, orange-marked PNG or quoted text, sent with the next message.

**Screen capture.**

- "Capture Screen…" in the "+" menu opens a dialog driven by `getDisplayMedia`.
- It shows a live preview, Capture (Return) and freeze-and-annotate.
- The capture is added to the draft.
- The browser's own picker replaces Noodle's thumbnail grid.

**Voice calls** are phase 7. They need a realtime audio path (WebRTC) that does not exist ([04 §2.4](analysis/04-rich-media-voice-annotations.md)).

### 7.11 Group conversations (phase 6, behind D6)

**User experience** ([05 §2.7](analysis/05-bots-groups-profiles.md), [03 §2.2](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md)):

- "New group": a name, a goal ("Shared with every employee in this group so they understand its purpose"), a member well with search-and-add, and confirm-on-remove.
- A composite avatar of the first three members.
- The hero shows the goal and the member names.
- Runs show names and avatars.
- `@name` completion in the composer.
- System notices for membership changes.

**Model.** Option A, recommended, is a conversation entity with participant employees. An owner message is delivered to each participant's talk line with the conversation id, the roster (names and public descriptions) and its recent history. Each employee decides whether to reply. A reply is posted into the group thread with author identity.

**Guards.** Noodle has none and relies on prompts ([07 §4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)). We add server-enforced guards:

- a budget of employee messages per owner message;
- a per-employee rate limit;
- a quiet period after N consecutive employee messages;
- `@mentions` raise the priority of the named employees.

**Teams.** Existing teams (a lead plus specialists through Task Manager) stay as delegation inside one workflow. They are not groups.

### 7.12 Effects (phase 4)

- An employee tool `celebrate(kind: confetti | fireworks)`. Confetti is for an everyday win; fireworks for a rare milestone.
- An effect is not a message: it does not wake anyone, mark anything unread or reorder the list.
- Server rules: at most one per conversation every 2 s; it expires after 30 s; it is claimed atomically by the visible conversation, so it never replays.
- The client plays a 4 s `<canvas>` overlay, seeded from the effect id.
- Under reduced motion, a still badge shows instead.
- Exact particle formulas are in [03 §2.18](analysis/03-conversation-surface.md).

### 7.13 Activity and usage (phase 7, optional)

- **Activity drawer** per employee, a web translation of Noodle's Activity HUD ([06 §2.8](analysis/06-settings-harness-usage-activity.md)):
  - a monospaced, selectable log of run events: steps, tool calls, output deltas coalesced by stream id;
  - bounded to 500 entries and 256 KB;
  - follow-latest only within 4 px of the bottom, with a floating "Follow latest" button.
  It reuses `chatRunStore` events, so it needs no new server stream.
- **Usage view** ([06 §2.7](analysis/06-settings-harness-usage-activity.md)):
  - periods of 7 days, 30 days and 12 months;
  - group by employee, model or provider;
  - measure tokens or cost;
  - a summary strip of six stats, a stacked bar chart with stable name-ordered hues (seven colours plus "Other") and a breakdown table.
  It reads the existing token and API usage metrics.

### 7.14 Settings additions

Home Settings gains pages only where this RFC adds settings:

- **Conversation:**
  - message received sound;
  - preview web links;
  - attachment layout (Wrap, Vertical, Stack);
  - show descriptions in the @ menu (phase 6).
- **Keybindings** (phase 7): Noodle's recorder, validation and reserved-shortcut rules ([06 §2.10](analysis/06-settings-harness-usage-activity.md)). Extend the reserved list with the browser's own shortcuts (7.4) and with any single-character shortcut (WCAG 2.1.4).

Noodle's row anatomy, status label vocabulary and footer action bar become the pattern for every new settings row ([06 §2.2](analysis/06-settings-harness-usage-activity.md)).

### 7.15 Mobile and responsive

Noodle Mobile uses one layout everywhere and stretches it on iPad; the agent flagged this as a pitfall ([08 §5](analysis/08-mobile-ios.md)). Target layouts by width:

| Width | Layout |
|---|---|
| Below 768 px | Stack navigation: the list, then the conversation. Dialogs become bottom sheets. Composer controls are 48 px. The composer bottom sits `max(8 px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) − 6 px)` from the edge, and 8 px above the on-screen keyboard (`visualViewport`). |
| 768 to 1023 px | Two panes: a 320 px list plus the conversation. The Workspace dock becomes a sheet. |
| 1024 px and up | The three-column layout of 7.1. |

Touch:

- every target is at least 44 px;
- long press (350 ms) opens a lift overlay with the 12-reaction bar and Copy;
- every swipe action (Pin) is also in the context menu.

### 7.16 Keyboard and accessibility

Noodle does well on naming icon controls, Reduce Motion and keyboard operation. It has these gaps ([10 §3.7](analysis/10-copy-content-accessibility.md)):

- status dots that rely on colour alone;
- no sender names in group messages;
- no combined message element for VoiceOver;
- an unlabelled backstory editor;
- tooltips and accessibility names that disagree;
- no handling of reduced transparency, increased contrast or differentiate-without-colour.

Requirements for this work, all acceptance criteria of the phase that introduces the surface:

- **Transcript semantics.**
  - The message list is `role="log"` (polite). Each message is an article whose accessible name includes the sender and time ("Chloe, 07:58"), with the delivery state as text.
  - New employee messages are announced once each, never per streamed token.
  - Group runs print the sender's name (7.3).
- **Status never by colour alone.** The status dot pairs with a text description ("Chloe: working") through `aria-describedby` and its tooltip. Progress text ("Checking…") lives in `role="status"`.
- **Headings and landmarks.** The conversation title is a heading; the sidebar, conversation and composer are labelled landmarks.
- **Names.** Every icon-only control is a real button whose `aria-label` equals its tooltip text, from one source. A disabled Send stays a button with `aria-disabled`.
- **Message actions.** Every message is focusable; its actions open with Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key, by right-click, and from the hover or focus button. Reactions, annotations and capture each have a visible control besides any shortcut.
- **Motion and pause.**
  - Reduced motion turns off cross-fades, the waveform scroll, the effects (a still badge instead) and the wordmark animation.
  - Any animated wallpaper or effect that can run longer than five seconds also gets a visible pause control (WCAG 2.2.2).
- **Transparency and contrast.**
  - `prefers-reduced-transparency` and `prefers-contrast: more` replace glass and blur with opaque tokens.
  - `forced-colors: active` keeps bubble borders and focus rings.
  - Text over any wallpaper meets 4.5:1. That is guaranteed by the scrim and the dark tokens, never assumed from the image, and checked by fixtures on every preset and a bright photo.
- **Text and targets.**
  - Text is in rem, with nothing below 12 px.
  - The page reflows at 320 px and works at 200 % zoom.
  - Pointer targets are at least 24 × 24 px (WCAG 2.5.8), and 44 px on touch.
- **Focus.** Focus rings stay visible and are never hidden under the floating composer (`scroll-padding-bottom`, WCAG 2.4.11). Focus returns to the composer or the trigger after a dialog closes.
- **Process.**
  - Component tests query by role and name, so a missing name fails a test, as Noodle's hidden-window tests do.
  - axe runs on the fixture states.
  - The pull-request checklist gains keyboard, screen reader, motion, contrast over wallpapers and zoom.

### 7.17 Content design

Adopt Noodle's copy rules ([10 §3.3, §4.1](analysis/10-copy-content-accessibility.md), [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md) section 16):

- **Labels.** Functional only: no persistent hints, shortcut legends or explanatory footers on the conversation surface or in lists. Optional guidance goes behind a click: a heading or status tag that opens a popover saying what it allows, the default, and what turning it off does and does not undo.
- **Ellipsis.** "…" (one character) only when the command needs more input. Never on confirmations, on new-item commands that open a form, or on links.
- **Confirmation is asymmetric.** Confirm destruction and anything that widens access. Narrowing access, archiving and reversible changes apply at once.
- **Dialogs.**
  - The title is a question naming the object.
  - The body says what is lost, what is kept and any side effect, plus "This cannot be undone." only when true.
  - The confirming button repeats the verb and the noun, and Cancel takes initial focus.
- **Errors** have three parts: what happened, what to do and where, and what is kept. Never "we", never an apology.
- **Disabled controls** explain themselves through their placeholder ("{Name} is paused").
- **Settings paths in messages** ("Settings → Connectors") are generated from the live navigation labels, so a rename cannot leave stale text behind. Noodle's errors still say "Settings → Chat" five releases after that tab was renamed.
- **Employee voice.** The hire-written instructions should give employees Noodle's demo voice:
  - outcome first;
  - exact figures;
  - one next step;
  - teammates named;
  - no emoji in message bodies;
  - silence instead of acknowledging system events;
  - a status line of at most 60 characters.

These rules match OpenCompany's existing design-system voice (sentence case, second person) with two differences:

1. Noodle writes commands in Title Case ("Change Background…"); OpenCompany keeps sentence case ("Change background…").
2. Emoji are a conflict to resolve (D2).

## 8. Technical design

### 8.1 Frontend architecture

All new code lives in the existing feature folders and follows CLAUDE.md section 7:

- shadcn primitives;
- `ActionButton` intents;
- token-only Tailwind;
- no opacity arithmetic;
- lucide icons;
- Zustand slice selectors;
- TanStack Query for server data.

```
client/src/features/home/
  sidebar/HomeSidebar.tsx        -> ConversationList (sections, search, rows), ConversationRow, NewMenu
  header/HomeHeader.tsx          -> unchanged identity + a 64 px HeaderShade when a wallpaper is set
  employee/EmployeeChat.tsx      -> passes ConversationStart (hero) through the ChatPane `top` slot (where the orb sits)
  appearance/                    -> NEW: Wallpaper (layers + crossfade), WallpaperEditor, AvatarEditor, ProfileCard
  data/conversations.ts          -> NEW: useConversationsQuery, useMarkRead, useSetPinned, useSearchConversations
client/src/features/chat/
  thread/ChatThread.tsx          -> run grouping, day separators, reserved clearance, top fade mask
  turns/UserTurn.tsx, AssistantTurn.tsx -> bubble tokens, wallpaper plate, delivery label, React button
  turns/ReactionBadges.tsx       -> NEW
  turns/MessageContextMenu.tsx   -> NEW (shadcn context-menu)
  composer/Composer.tsx          -> pill geometry, "+" menu, long-paste rule, queued sends (D5)
  composer/MentionMenu.tsx       -> NEW in phase 6 (pattern: SlashMenu)
  media/                         -> NEW in phase 5: VoiceRecorderBar, VoicePlayer, AnnotationOverlay, CaptureDialog
  effects/EffectsCanvas.tsx      -> NEW in phase 4
client/src/components/ui/context-menu.tsx -> NEW (bun x shadcn@latest add context-menu)
```

**State ownership**

| Data | Owner | Fresh by |
|---|---|---|
| Conversation summaries (title, preview, last activity, unread, pinned, appearance) | TanStack Query `['conversations']` | `chat.updated` (debounced 300 ms), `conversation.read`, `conversation.appearance` broadcasts |
| Messages, reactions | Existing thread queries (`get_chat_messages`) | `chat.updated` |
| Run events | Existing `chatRunStore` | `chat_run_event` |
| Employee runtime status | Existing employee queries and `employee_lifecycle` | unchanged |
| Selection, search text, sidebar width, drafts, viewports, wallpaper editor open | Zustand (`useHomeStore`, `composerStore`) with slice selectors; drafts and viewports persisted per viewer | local |
| Effects queue | Small Zustand slice keyed by conversation | `chat_effect` (phase 4) |

**Rules carried over from Noodle and locked by tests**

1. Typing in the composer causes zero commits in transcript rows. A React Profiler or render-count test, Noodle's `TranscriptRenderProbe` equivalent.
2. Adding a reaction does not change a row's height (layout test).
3. Prepending older pages keeps the top visible message in place (scroll test).
4. The conversation-status precedence function has a table test.
5. The delivery-label function maps every protocol state.

### 8.2 Data model changes (server)

Proposals, to be refined in each phase's design. Names follow the snake_case conventions.

| Change | Phase | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conversation summary | 2 | Computed per session: `{id, kind: "direct", employee_ids, title, last_message: {uid, role, author_id, preview, created_at} \| null, last_activity_at, unread, pinned, appearance}` | Direct conversations are today's sessions. `preview` is plain text computed server-side by the rules in 7.2 |
| Read marks | 2 | `chat_read_marks(session_id, principal_id, up_to_uid, updated_at)`, monotonic | Unread = the latest employee-authored message is newer than the mark. Per principal even before multi-user isolation exists (D8) |
| Pins | 2 | `conversation_pins(principal_id, session_id, pinned_at)` | Ordered by `pinned_at` |
| Search | 2 | SQLite FTS5 over `chat_messages.message` plus titles and descriptions | Server-side; returns conversation ids with a snippet |
| Appearance | 3 | `conversation_appearance(session_id, principal_id, background_json, updated_at)` plus media under `<DATA_DIR>/appearance/` | Not in the employee workspace (D10). Served through a dedicated route that reuses `services/media/preview.py` inline rules |
| Avatar appearance | 3 | `employee_avatar {symbol, colour_index, image_ref?}` on the employee's metadata | The existing photo path stays |
| Reactions | 4 | `chat_reactions(message_uid, author_kind, author_id, key, created_at)`, unique `(message_uid, author_kind, author_id, key)` | `key` is one of the 12 semantic keys. Delivered to the employee as `[reaction]` notes (`chat_notes`) |
| Effects | 4 | `chat_effects(id, session_id, author_id, kind, created_at, expires_at, consumed_at)` | Claimed atomically |
| Voice message metadata | 5 | On the attachment: `{voice: {duration_s, waveform[≤100], transcript?, locale?}}` | Audio stored as an `AudioRef` (media transport rules) |
| Link unfurls | 5 | `link_previews(url_hash, title, site, image_ref, fetched_at, failed)` | Seven-day cache; server fetch with SSRF guards |
| Group conversations | 6 | `conversations(id, kind, title, description, created_at, archived_at)`, `conversation_members(conversation_id, workflow_id, position)`, and `chat_messages.author_id` | D6. Message author identity is the prerequisite |
| Queued follow-ups | 2 or 3 | Admit an owner message while a run holds the lane, with `delivery: "queued_behind_run"` | D5. Needs a chat protocol change and a `protocol_version` bump |

### 8.3 Wire protocol changes

All new requests are WebSocket message types in snake_case; all new broadcasts are typed CloudEvents factories. Identity-only broadcasts are followed by an authorized refetch (the house pattern). `docs-internal/chat_protocol.md` changes in the same commit as any chat shape change. Draft shapes are in Appendix B.

| Message | Kind | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `list_conversations {}` returns `{conversations: [...]}` | request | 2 |
| `mark_conversation_read {session_id, up_to_uid}` | request | 2 |
| `set_conversation_pinned {session_id, pinned}` | request | 2 |
| `search_conversations {query, limit?}` returns `{results: [{session_id, snippet, message_uid}]}` | request | 2 |
| `com.opencompany.chat.read` (data `{session_id}`) | broadcast | 2 |
| `set_conversation_appearance {session_id, background}` and the upload route `POST /api/appearance/{session_id}` | request + HTTP | 3 |
| `com.opencompany.chat.appearance` (data `{session_id}`) | broadcast | 3 |
| `set_chat_reaction {session_id, message_id, key, present}` | request | 4 |
| `claim_chat_effect {session_id}` returns `{effect \| null}` | request | 4 |
| `com.opencompany.chat.effect` (data `{session_id, effect_id, kind, expires_at}`) | broadcast | 4 |
| `get_link_preview {url}` returns `{title, site, image_url} \| {failed: true}` | request | 5 |
| Group creation, update and membership requests (`create_conversation`, `update_conversation`) | request | 6 |

Every handler applies the existing chat access rules: refuse the internal socket, and allow only the conversation's owner ([11 Constraints](analysis/11-opencompany-current-state.md)).

### 8.4 Tokens and theming

New tokens go into `client/src/themes/base.css`, `light.css` and `dark.css`, bridged in `client/src/index.css`, with hex and `color-mix()` values defined in theme files and none at call sites. Home stays light and dark only. The wallpaper's forced-dark subtree reuses the dark token set rather than adding a third appearance. Token groups, with full values in [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md) Tokens:

- **Glass surfaces:** `--glass-bg`, `--glass-bg-strong`, `--glass-edge`, `--glass-shadow`, `--blur-glass` (20-24 px), `--saturate-glass` (160-180 %).
- **Wallpaper:** `--wallpaper-scrim` (black 25 %), `--chat-veil`, `--header-shade-top`, `--header-shade-mid`, `--fade-band` (64 px).
- **Bubbles:**
  - `--bubble-out` and `--bubble-out-ink`;
  - `--bubble-in` (plain) and `--bubble-in-glass` (wallpaper);
  - `--bubble-radius` (Home's `--radius-panel`, 16), `--bubble-pad-x` and `--bubble-pad-y`.
- **Reactions:** `--reaction-mine`, `--reaction-other`, `--reaction-ring`.
- **Avatar gradients:** `--avatar-grad-0` to `--avatar-grad-5` (two stops each).
- **Wallpaper presets:** `--wallpaper-sunset-1` to `-3` and the same for ocean, forest and dusk.
- **Annotation mark:** `--annotation-mark` (`#ff8c00`) and its halo.
- **Motion:** additions to the `--dur-*` and `--ease-*` set; all Web Animations go through `lib/motion.ts`.
  - `--dur-switch` 160 ms, `--dur-wallpaper` 350 ms, `--dur-select` 120 ms;
  - `--spring-lift` (350 ms, bounce 0.25) and `--spring-morph` (400 ms, slight overshoot).

The ten stylized skins keep painting `.chat-msg-*` in Dev's console chat. They do not reach Home.

### 8.5 Rendering and performance

- **Transcript.**
  - Keep the bounded window: the newest page, plus prepending through an `IntersectionObserver` sentinel.
  - Rows use `content-visibility: auto` with a measured intrinsic size.
  - Move to `react-virtuoso` only if real conversations exceed a few thousand rows.
- **Glass costs GPU time.**
  - Limit `backdrop-filter` to small surfaces: bubbles over a wallpaper, the composer, the header shade and badges.
  - Never blur the whole column.
  - Pause video wallpapers when hidden and while a dialog is open.
  - The existing `data-page-hidden` pause already stops CSS animations.
- **Decode before swap.** `img.decode()` (or the video's `canplay`) before cross-fading a wallpaper.
- **Lazy media.** Link previews and thumbnails load only after 300 ms in view; reserved sizes come from server metadata.
- **Markdown cache.** Keyed by message uid and revision.
- **No polling.** Everything above is pushed or refetched on a broadcast, which also removes the existing undocumented 5 s poll in `EmployeeAccess.tsx` noted in [11 §9](analysis/11-opencompany-current-state.md).

### 8.6 Security and privacy

- **Link unfurls** are a new outbound fetch:
  - public hosts only, with a DNS-resolution check against private ranges;
  - a size cap;
  - an image re-encode;
  - no cookies;
  - a timeout.
  This needs its own review before phase 5.
- **Wallpapers and avatars.** Uploads use the existing streamed upload limits and content sniffing. Video is served inline only for `video/*` types; SVG is never inline (`NEVER_INLINE`).
- **Reactions and effects** are rate-limited on the server. Employee-posted cards are validated against the employee's assigned resources.
- **Voice.** The audio stays in the workspace as an `AudioRef`; transcription uses the configured speech provider.
- **Groups.** One employee never sees another employee's private instructions. The roster carries only names and public descriptions, as in Noodle ([05 §2.3](analysis/05-bots-groups-profiles.md)).

### 8.7 Testing

- **Scenario fixtures.** Port Noodle's scenario format, a strict JSON schema of agents, conversations, messages, reactions, backgrounds, a presentation state and a timeline ([07 §2.10, §3.4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)):
  - validate with a `.strict()` zod schema, so unknown keys fail;
  - run fixtures through a fake WebSocket transport injected into the provider, never by mocking hooks;
  - extend the existing `client/src/features/chat/__fixtures__/` rather than starting a parallel folder.
- **Visual regression.** Playwright screenshots of fixture states:
  - each wallpaper preset and a bright photo, in both appearances;
  - a group conversation;
  - a long table;
  - reaction stacks;
  - the composer at 1, 6 and 10 lines;
  - the phone breakpoint with the keyboard open.
- **Behaviour tests.** The render-count, layout-shift, scroll-anchor, precedence and delivery-label tests of 8.1, plus the IME Enter rule and the long-paste rule.
- **Server tests.**
  - read-mark monotonicity;
  - reaction idempotence;
  - effect claim atomicity;
  - group guard budgets;
  - the broadcast factories (`test_status_broadcasts.py` stays green).

## 9. Rollout plan

Each phase is shippable alone. Sizes are relative: S is days, M is about a week, L is two to three weeks, and XL is over a month.

| Phase | Scope | Size | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 Foundations | Tokens (8.4); shadcn `context-menu`; `Avatar` sizes `xl` and the cut-out status dot; gradient-and-symbol avatar component; motion tokens; scenario fixture harness with a fake transport; render-count test harness | M | Tokens exist in light and dark; the fixture harness renders a seeded Home; render-count, precedence and delivery-label tests in place |
| 1 Conversation surface | Hero; run grouping; day separators and hover times; reserved clearance; the delivery label; long-message fold; table fold; prose width cap; composer pill geometry; the "+" menu; long paste to file; message context menu (Copy, Save, Use as photo) | M | Typing re-renders no rows; reacting is impossible to test yet, but layout tests cover the reserved space; the composer's empty and one-line heights are equal; Lighthouse accessibility passes |
| 2 Sidebar and attention | `list_conversations`; read marks; pins; FTS search; previews and times; unread dots; title badge; notifications and sound; ordering by last message; context menu; ⌘K search | L | Opening a conversation clears unread in every tab; search finds message text; previews never show Markdown; no new polling |
| 3 Identity and appearance | Wallpaper presets, upload and video; the legibility recipe; forced-dark subtree; wallpaper editor; avatar editor; profile card | M | Contrast passes on every preset and on a bright-photo fixture; reduced transparency renders opaque; video pauses when hidden |
| 4 Reactions and effects | Reactions data, UI, keyboard path and `[reaction]` notes; employee `react_to_message` tool; effects tool, canvas and still badge | M | A reaction never moves a row; an employee "working, then done" sequence shows as reactions; an effect plays once, in the foreground only |
| 5 Rich media | Voice messages (record, waveform, transcript, player); annotations (text and region); screen capture; link unfurls with SSRF guards; companion cards with snapshots | L | Failed transcription offers retry and audio-only; an annotation reaches the employee with its quote or region; the unfurl security review is signed off |
| 6 Groups | Conversation entity; author identity; fan-out with guards; @mentions; group sheets; composite avatar | XL | D6 decided; guard budgets enforced in tests; a four-employee fixture conversation renders and replays |
| 7 Optional | Activity drawer; usage view; keybindings editor; Electron pop-out windows; voice calls | L each | Decided per item |

Phases 1 and 3 change the look of a screen the owner approved on 2026-10-03, so each needs the owner's sign-off on fixture screenshots before merge.

## 10. Decisions required

| # | Decision | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Reply backing | (a) Keep bubble-less replies everywhere (the 2026-10-03 choice); (b) Noodle bubbles everywhere; (c) bubble-less on plain backgrounds, a translucent plate when a wallpaper is set | (c). It respects the owner's choice and fixes legibility over wallpapers |
| D2 | Reaction glyphs | (a) Emoji, as in Noodle; (b) a fixed lucide icon set over semantic keys | (b). The design system forbids decorative emoji; keys keep the agent contract independent of the glyphs |
| D3 | Wallpaper scope | (a) Conversation column only; (b) the whole window with a translucent sidebar | (a) first; (b) is a later visual project |
| D4 | Conversation lifetime | (a) Today: Reset and New conversation clear the thread; (b) Noodle: the transcript persists, and "New session" resets context only, with a notice in the thread | (b), as a separate design with workflow-control owners; (a) stays until then |
| D5 | Sending while an employee works | (a) Refuse (today); (b) queue behind the run; (c) queue, with interrupt for stop or correction messages | (b) now; (c) later |
| D6 | Group model | (a) A new conversation entity over several employee workflows; (b) make team specialists visible in the lead's thread | (a). It matches peers working toward a goal; (b) conflates delegation with conversation |
| D7 | Meaning of "Delivered" | Saved; admitted; claimed by the workflow | Sent = saved; Queued = paused; Delivered = run claimed |
| D8 | Read-state owner | Per session; per principal | Per principal, even before isolation |
| D9 | Markdown | (a) Keep GFM blocks; (b) Noodle's inline-only rendering | (a) |
| D10 | Where wallpaper media lives | In the employee workspace; in an appearance store outside it | Outside it |

## 11. Alternatives considered

- **Do nothing; keep the 2026-10-03 Home.** It is coherent, but it does not solve G1 (who needs me) or G4. The sidebar metadata in phase 2 is valuable even without any visual change.
- **Port Noodle's look wholesale** (SF Pro, 12.5 px text, Liquid Glass everywhere, bubbles everywhere). This would conflict with OpenCompany's token system, Geist typography and the owner's chat decision. Web glass is also costlier than native. We copy the rules, not the skin.
- **A separate "Team" screen beside Home.** Two places to talk to the same employee would split attention and state; Noodle's single conversation list is the lesson.
- **Client-side unread from `localStorage`.** It is simple, but tabs and devices disagree, and it is lost on a reset. Noodle's own Hub moved to server-side, message-id read marks for that reason ([07 §2.5](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)).
- **File polling, as Noodle does.** Already ruled out by OpenCompany's push architecture.
- **Typing indicators from the employee's status.** Noodle shows that runtime phase is per bot, not per conversation, so a working bot would light up every conversation it belongs to. OpenCompany's runs are per session, which already solves this. Show "working" only from the session's own run.

## 12. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| `backdrop-filter` cost on large or animated backgrounds (video), especially on low-end GPUs | Blur only small surfaces; pause video when hidden or a dialog is open; opaque fallback under reduced transparency and on a GPU-tier heuristic |
| Legibility over arbitrary photos | The full recipe always applies (scrim, forced dark, veil, shade, fade); fixture screenshots include a bright photo |
| Scope creep from Noodle's breadth (companions, Hub, calls) | Non-goals are explicit; phase 7 is optional, item by item |
| LLM spend in groups (every employee woken by every message) | Server-side budgets, rate limits and mention priority (7.11); show per-group usage |
| Reworking a recently approved design | Owner sign-off per phase on fixture screenshots; D1 keeps the approved default |
| Cross-browser features (View Transitions, `field-sizing`, `scrollend`, `content-visibility`) | Progressive enhancement with the documented fallbacks |
| Noodle screenshots that predate its code | The analysis treats code as current; this RFC follows the code |
| Docs drift in OpenCompany (`normal_mode.md` is behind the code) | Update `normal_mode.md` and `chat_protocol.md` in the same commits as each phase |

## 13. Open questions

- **Q1.** Should an employee's self-set one-line status (Noodle's `status`, at most 60 characters) become a tool, shown in the profile card and on mobile pinned rows?
- **Q2.** Should the Choose Conversation quick switcher (⌃⌥Space in Noodle) exist as a system-wide shortcut in the Electron shell, or only in the app, merged with the ⌘K search?
- **Q3.** Should Like and Dislike reactions write ratings (`set_chat_feedback`), or stay separate signals?
- **Q4.** Should "Create Image…" for avatars and wallpapers use a configured image model, and which provider pays for it?
- **Q5.** What do groups do with employees that are paused or not running (Noodle: archived bots stay members but receive nothing)?
- **Q6.** Can an employee start a conversation on its own (heartbeats)? Noodle wakes idle bots every 30 minutes by default ([07 §2.4](analysis/07-state-model-and-runtime-ui.md)).
- **Q7.** Is per-conversation appearance synced across the owner's devices (server-side, as proposed) or local, as in Noodle?

## Appendix B: draft wire shapes

# Noodle: app shell and navigation

Noodle's macOS shell is one main window (a two-column `NavigationSplitView`: a translucent conversation sidebar over a full-bleed per-conversation wallpaper, and a chat detail), surrounded by a deliberately small set of auxiliary surfaces: per-conversation windows, always-on-top floating panels, a system-wide "Choose Conversation" grid summoned with ⌃⌥Space, dark HUD-style panels for activity logs and live Hub views, a Usage window and an 11-tab Settings window. Navigation is a single selection (`selectedConversationID`) filtered by an optional "space" and a search string; everything else (sheets, alerts, takeovers such as the first-run welcome) is driven by optional store fields. The chrome leans entirely on system behaviour: a unified toolbar with no title and no background, Liquid Glass toolbar buttons, a 64 pt header shade that keeps the toolbar readable over any wallpaper, and system semantic colours. First run is a full-window "wordmark writes itself" animation that lifts into a four-tile account picker and ends by creating a three-bot starter team in a "Team" group. Shortcuts are user-rebindable through a validated registry, notifications are shown only when the user is not looking at Noodle, and there are no notification actions or inline reply.

Permalink base for every `path:line` citation below: https://github.com/pdparchitect/noodle/blob/702339e3153025c9fe9582783caff7a19b48ff97/

### 2.2 Window chrome

**Main window.** `WindowConfiguration` sets `titleVisibility = .hidden`, `titlebarAppearsTransparent = true`, `backgroundColor = .windowBackgroundColor`, `minSize = 980 × 670`, `isReleasedWhenClosed = false` (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:303-323`). The scene uses `.windowToolbarStyle(.unified(showsTitle: false))` and `.windowResizability(.contentMinSize)`, and the split view applies `.toolbarBackgroundVisibility(.hidden, for: .windowToolbar)` (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:113-119,460`), so the toolbar has no bar of its own: the wallpaper runs under the traffic lights and the toolbar buttons float on it as glass. The wallpaper is a `.background` of the whole `NavigationSplitView` with `.ignoresSafeArea()`, so it sits behind both columns (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:431-441`).

Measured in `screenshot-chloe.png`: traffic lights ≈14 pt in diameter, centres at x ≈ 22.5, 45.5, 68.5 pt and y ≈ 23 pt, inside the sidebar column; toolbar glass buttons ≈37 pt circles centred on the same y; the Create pill ≈44 × 37 pt with a pull-down chevron; the gap between Hide Sidebar and Create ≈15 pt (`ToolbarSpacer(.fixed)`); both sit right-aligned in the sidebar column, the Create pill ending ≈7.5 pt before the column edge; the detail column's first button starts ≈8 pt after the sidebar edge. The toolbar band is therefore ≈46-52 pt tall (inferred from button centres; the code sets no height).

**Header shade.** One 64 pt band over the wallpaper, under both columns, so the toolbar stays legible on bright images (`Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/NoodleWallpaper/ConversationWindowHeaderShade.swift:26-52`):

```swift
Rectangle().fill(.ultraThinMaterial)
  .overlay { LinearGradient(stops: [.init(color: .black.opacity(dark ? 0.24 : 0.06), location: 0),
                                    .init(color: .black.opacity(dark ? 0.10 : 0.03), location: 0.5),
                                    .init(color: .clear, location: 1)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom) }
  .mask { LinearGradient(stops: [.init(color: .black, location: 0), .init(color: .black.opacity(0.88), location: 0.55),
                                 .init(color: .clear, location: 1)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom) }
  .frame(height: 64)
  .shadow(color: .black.opacity(dark ? 0.24 : 0.06), radius: 14, y: 5)
```

The transcript itself is masked by `ConversationContentTopFade`: transparent at 0, white 12 % at 45 % of 64 pt, opaque at 64 pt (`Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/NoodleWallpaper/ConversationWindowHeaderShade.swift:3-22`, applied at `Sources/Noodle/ChatView.swift:180-185`). The welcome and Connect takeovers omit the shade ("Flat: there is no title bar content", `Sources/Noodle/WelcomeView.swift:15-19`) but keep an invisible 1 × 1 principal toolbar item so the window keeps its toolbar shape (`Sources/Noodle/WelcomeView.swift:21-26`).

**Wallpaper behaviour that affects the chrome.** A non-default wallpaper forces the whole window into dark appearance (`window.appearance = .darkAqua`), cross-fading the window and its chrome over 0.35 s ease-in-out unless Reduce Motion is on; the wallpaper itself gets a 25 % black scrim and cross-fades over 0.35 s after its replacement image has loaded, so a switch never flashes the plain canvas (`Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/NoodleWallpaper/ConversationBackgroundView.swift:40,43-61,92,128-151`). The detail column adds `textBackgroundColor` at 28 % over the wallpaper (`Sources/Noodle/ChatView.swift:62`; the empty detail uses the same tint, `Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:419`).

**Split view.** `NavigationSplitView(columnVisibility:)` with `.navigationSplitViewStyle(.balanced)` and sidebar width `min 280, ideal 326, max 380` (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:405-427`). The screenshot's sidebar is ≈311 pt. The sidebar list hides its own background and draws a tint `Color.black.opacity(dark ? 0.24 : 0.04)` (`Sources/Noodle/SidebarView.swift:28,35`); in the group screenshot the wallpaper shows through the sidebar heavily blurred, so the native sidebar material sits under that tint. Column visibility is view state (`@State`, default `.all`), not persisted (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:329`).

**Sidebar collapse.** While the sidebar is visible the sidebar column removes the system sidebar toggle and declares its own "Hide Sidebar" button (`sidebar.leading`) followed by the Create menu; hiding animates `columnVisibility = .detailOnly` with SwiftUI's default animation. When hidden, the system toggle returns to the window toolbar and Create moves to the window toolbar's `.navigation` placement (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:363-400,407-410,461-464`; `CHANGELOG.md:613`). A comment records a layout trap: `.navigationSplitViewColumnWidth` must come after `.toolbar(removing:)` or the width is lost (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:409-410`). Shift-Tab from the composer re-opens a hidden sidebar and focuses the list (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:413-416`).

**Other window chrome.** Conversation windows: transparent title bar, no toolbar background, principal title = 20 pt status avatar (7 pt dot, 1.5 pt cut-out ring) + `.headline` name, spacing 7, one line, tail truncation, no glass behind it (`.sharedBackgroundVisibility(.hidden)`) (`Sources/Noodle/ConversationWindow.swift:68-71,128-143`). Floating panels: `[.titled, .closable, .resizable, .fullSizeContentView, .nonactivatingPanel]`, minimise and zoom buttons hidden, native title hidden, clear background, `NSVisualEffectView` `.hudWindow` blur of what is behind instead of the wallpaper (`Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:181-201,236-245`). HUD panels (activity, live views, previews) share `AnnotationPreviewFrame`: dark aqua, `.hudWindow` material, corner radius 18, 1 pt border white 22 %, all three traffic lights hidden, a 36 pt header with an `xmark.circle.fill` close button (18 × 18, 10 pt from the left), a 13 pt semibold title 8 pt after it (middle truncation), an 11 pt medium secondary kind label 14 pt from the right, and the content inset 5 pt left, right and bottom with an inner radius of 13; dragging the header moves the window (`Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/AgentActivityWindow.swift:302-372`).

**Focus guard.** `WindowFocusGuard` swallows the first physical click on a non-key titled window and only focuses it, so a click into a background Noodle window never also presses whatever was under the pointer; title-bar drags, resizing and window buttons keep native behaviour (`Shared/SettingsUI/Sources/NoodleSettingsUI/WindowFocusGuard.swift:53-92`).

### 2.4 Sidebar

**Sections and order.** One `List(selection:)` in `.sidebar` style with three sections, each rendered only when non-empty: "Pinned", "Bots", "Groups" (`Sources/Noodle/SidebarView.swift:20-24,64-75`). Pinned rows are removed from Bots and Groups and appear in the order they were pinned (a newly pinned item is appended) (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:495-509,529-531`). Bots and Groups are ordered by `updatedAt`, newest first; the store re-sorts after every send and reloads sorted from disk (`Sources/NoodleCore/WorkspaceRepository.swift:809-813`, `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:1468-1471`). There is no explicit animation when a reply moves a row to the top (no `withAnimation` anywhere in the store). There is no per-row drag, no reordering and no drop target per row.

**Row anatomy** (`Sources/Noodle/SidebarView.swift:141-199`, measured values from the 2x screenshot in brackets):

| Part | Value |
|---|---|
| Row content | `HStack(spacing: 10)`, `.frame(height: 66)`, insets top 2, leading 14, bottom 2, trailing 10, so a 70 pt pitch [measured 69-70] |
| Avatar | `ConversationAvatar` 42 pt [42]; group with 2+ members: up to 3 avatars at 62 % size on a `.quaternary` disc, offsets (-0.18s, -0.14s), (0.18s, -0.14s), (0, 0.19s), each with a 2 pt window-background ring; one-member group: 86 % avatar offset (-0.06s, -0.06s) over an 88 % disc offset (0.06s, 0.06s) (`Sources/Noodle/Components.swift:6-61`) |
