| Title | 13.5 pt semibold, 1 line; bot name for a direct chat, group name for a group, first non-empty line, capped at 100 characters with "…" (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:2181-2187`, `Sources/NoodleCore/ConversationName.swift:34-39`) |
| Timestamp | 11.5 pt, `.tertiary`, trailing; same baseline row as the title, `HStack(spacing: 6)` with `Spacer(minLength: 4)` |
| Preview | 12.5 pt, `.secondary`, `lineLimit(2)`, `VStack(spacing: 2)` under the title [line pitch ≈15.5 pt] |
| Unread dot | 8 pt `Color.blue`, `overlay(alignment: .leading)` offset x -13, so it sits in the leading inset 5 pt before the avatar [gap 5.5] (`CHANGELOG.md:1080`) |
| Separator | bottom edge of every row, including the last of a section [visible under the last bot], tint `Color.primary.opacity(0.12)`; drawn from the text's leading edge [x ≈ 79 pt from the window edge] to ≈16 pt before the column edge |
| Selection | system sidebar selection: in the screenshots a neutral lighter rounded rectangle inset ≈7 pt from the column's left, ≈10 pt from its right, radius ≈5-6 pt (measured; system drawn) |
| Section header | system sidebar header: ≈11 pt bold, secondary, ≈11 pt from the column's left (measured) |
| Accessibility | combined element; label "Unread, <title>, <preview>" or "<title>, <preview>"; value = runtime help |

**Timestamp rule.** Today: time only, `formatted(date: .omitted, time: .shortened)` ("8:02 AM"); any other day: `formatted(date: .abbreviated, time: .omitted)` ("Sep 20, 2026"), always with the year, never "Yesterday" or a weekday (`Sources/Noodle/SidebarView.swift:201-207`). The value is the conversation's `updatedAt`, which a sent or received message sets.

**Preview rule.** Last message body, tables removed ("Sent a table" if only a table), Markdown converted to plain text; "No messages yet" when empty (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:2189-2192`, `Shared/HubLink/Sources/HubLink/MessageTable.swift:54-59`).

**Runtime dot state machine.** Per bot phase `offline | starting | ready | working | failed`; a conversation's status is `working` if any shown participant works, else `failed` if any failed, else `ready` if all are ready, else `idle` (`Sources/Noodle/Components.swift:63-91`). Colours: working `.blue`, failed `.red`, ready `.green`, idle `.gray` (so `starting` and `offline` show grey). A bot on a joined Hub reports the Hub's phase while connected, otherwise `offline`. Tooltip text, one line per participant: "<Name>: <runtime detail>", or for Hub bots "<Name>: Working on <Hub>" / "<Name>: Runs on <Hub>", plus " (not connected)" (`Sources/Noodle/Components.swift:93-102`).

**Unread state.** A conversation id set, persisted by the repository, not a count of messages (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:76-78,604-608`). Only new agent-authored messages add a conversation, and only if it is not being viewed at that moment (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:1934-1941,2129-2148`). "Viewed" means the app is active and some registered window showing that conversation is visible, not minimised and not occluded (`Sources/Noodle/ConversationWindow.swift:226-232`). Read is triggered by: selecting it (`Sources/Noodle/SidebarView.swift:49-51`); the app becoming active with it visible; its window becoming key or changing occlusion; any mouse, key, scroll or gesture event inside a window showing it ("Input in this window is direct evidence of reading", `Sources/Noodle/ConversationWindow.swift:309-352`); tapping the chat, the composer gaining focus, typing a draft (`Sources/Noodle/ChatView.swift:43-52`, `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:94-97`); archiving it; and reading on another device unless a bot wrote since (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:1567-1574`). The Dock badge is the number of unread conversations, cleared at zero (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:1521-1525`). There are no other attention badges on rows; failure shows as the red runtime dot plus a Kick item in the context menu (pending-approval indicators were removed, `CHANGELOG.md:946`).

**Search.** `.searchable(text:, placement: .sidebar, prompt: "Search")` with `.controlSize(.large)` (`Sources/Noodle/SidebarView.swift:36-38`) [measured: capsule ≈294 × 27.5 pt, 7 pt from the left, top at ≈58.5 pt]. Matching is live, case- and diacritic-insensitive (`localizedCaseInsensitiveContains`) on: the conversation title, its public description, any participant's name, and the body of every message in the conversation (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:477-493`). It filters within the current space and excludes archived conversations; Pinned is filtered too. ⌘F (Conversation → Search Conversations) focuses the field through a global notification (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:151-153`, `Sources/Noodle/SidebarView.swift:59-61`).

**Empty states.** No conversations at all: an empty list (no overlay), with the detail showing the first-bot button if there are no bots. Conversations exist but none in the current view and no search text: `ContentUnavailableView("No Bots", systemImage: "square.stack")` ("A space with nothing in it yet"). Search with no match: `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)` (system copy, which reads 'No Results for "…"' with a spelling hint; inferred from the system API) (`Sources/Noodle/SidebarView.swift:39-48`).

**Selection and keyboard.** Single selection bound to `store.selectedConversationID`. Up/Down move the selection natively, and focus stays in the list while the chat switches (`CHANGELOG.md:1223`). Tab with a selection, no modifiers and the search field not focused moves focus to the composer; Shift-Tab in the composer returns to the list (`Sources/Noodle/ConversationListKeyboardNavigation.swift:5-22`, `Sources/Noodle/ScrollableChatComposer.swift:123-133`). Switching conversations dissolves the transcript over 0.16 s ease-out; a new switch replaces the running transition, so rapid arrowing renders only the latest; no dissolve under Reduce Motion or during a live resize (`Sources/Noodle/ConversationTransition.swift:61-79`).

**Context menu** (exact order, `Sources/Noodle/SidebarView.swift:77-138`):

1. Open in New Window
2. Float on Top
3. Pin / Unpin
4. Spaces ▸ (a checkbox per custom space, a divider if any, then "New Space…", which creates a space containing this conversation)
5. —
6. Group: Edit Group…, Change Background…. Direct: Edit Bot… (hidden for someone else's Hub bot), Change Background…, then, if the bot runs on this Mac: —, Show Activity, Show Usage, Show Workspace in Finder, —, Kick (only when the phase is `failed`; disabled while access is changing), New Session (disabled while access is changing)
7. —, Archive Group / Archive Bot (Archive Bot hidden for someone else's Hub bot)

Kick shows an alert titled by the request (default "Recover Bot") with "Open Harness Settings" (authentication failures), the confirm button, "New Session" when offered, and Cancel (`Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/AgentKickConfirmation.swift:6-39`). New Session asks "Start a new session for <Name>?" / "<Name> will start with a fresh context. Its workspace, memory and messages are kept." with New Session and Cancel (`Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/ConversationRuntimeSettings.swift:46-67`). Both alerts hang off the list, not the menu, "so closing a context menu cannot dismiss the alert".

**Drag and drop.** The only drop target is the whole split view: dropping files anywhere in the main window, sidebar included, attaches them to the selected conversation and draws a 2 pt accent-coloured rounded rectangle (radius 15, inset 5) while targeted (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:442-459`).

**Spaces.** A space is a filter over the sidebar: All (default), This Mac (only with a Hub joined), each joined Hub, and user-made spaces (iCloud-synced). The chosen space is persisted in `UserDefaults` "Noodle.space"; pins belong to the space they were made in; a bot or group created while a custom space is shown joins it (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:61-75,350-475`). The space is chosen only from the menu bar Spaces menu or ⌘1-⌘9; nothing in the window shows which space is active (verified: `SidebarView` and `ChatView` have no space UI). Deleting a space asks "Delete <name>?" / "Its bots and groups stay in All." with Cancel as the default button (`Sources/Noodle/ConversationCommands.swift:195-202`).

### 2.5 Multi-window model

Every conversation can be shown in the main window and, independently, in at most one extra place: a normal separate window or a floating panel, never both (`Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:41-72`).

| From → To | Trigger | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| none → separate window | Open in New Window | `present(id)`: if a separate window exists, raise it and focus its composer; else open `WindowGroup` value `id` (`Sources/Noodle/ConversationWindow.swift:261-268`) |
| floating → separate | Open in New Window | "How a window is opened decides its mode": ends floating, closes the panel, presents the window (`Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:56-61`) |
| none or separate → floating | Float on Top, or a pick in Choose Conversation | closes the separate window and shrinks its frame towards its top-right corner to min(420, w) × min(560, h); with no window and no saved frame, lands 420 × 560 centred on the pointer, clamped to that screen's visible frame; otherwise the saved frame (`Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:43-54,203-212`) |
| separate or floating → main | Show in Main Window (`pip.exit`) | select in main, raise or reopen main first "so the app never passes through having no window", then close the panel and window (`Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:63-71`) |
| floating → none | close the panel | ends floating mode (except during Quit) (`Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:140-145`) |

Floating panel behaviour: level `.floating`, `collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary]`, `hidesOnDeactivate = false`, non-activating so typing in it does not bring Noodle's other windows forward, can become key and main, minimum 380 × 360 enforced by the delegate because the hosted SwiftUI view resets the window minimum (`Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:134-201`). Because a panel is not a SwiftUI scene, menu shortcuts do not reach it, so the panel itself runs ⇧⌘D and ⇧⌘C (`Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:154-179`, `Sources/Noodle/ConversationCommands.swift:44-60`). New panels opened from the same spot step 28 pt right and 28 pt down until no open panel's top-left corner is within 20 pt, at most 12 steps, and at the screen edge shift left by 28 × the number of panels (`Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:214-225`). Settings → Conversation → "Keep one floating conversation" (off by default) closes the open float and gives the next one its exact frame (`Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:21-22,100-107`). The floating set is persisted in `UserDefaults` "Noodle.floatingConversations.v1" and restored as panels at launch.

**Choose Conversation** (`Sources/Noodle/AgentPicker.swift`). A borderless, non-activating panel at `.modalPanel` level that joins all Spaces and full-screen apps, appears without AppKit's pop-in animation, and closes when it loses key (click elsewhere). It is toggled by a Carbon global hot key registered from the "Choose Conversation" binding (default ⌃⌥Space), unregistered while a shortcut is being recorded, and is also opened by Conversation → Choose Conversation…. Layout constants (`Sources/Noodle/AgentPicker.swift:47-76`):

| Constant | Value |
|---|---|
| width | 560 |
| columns | 4 |
| tile height / grid spacing | 104 / 10 |
| visible rows | 1-3; more rows scroll (scrolling disabled when everything fits, so it cannot rubber-band) |
| padding / search field height / section spacing | 18 / 24 / 14 |
| panel height | 18 + 24 + 14 + 1 (divider) + 14 + grid + 18, grid = rows × 104 + (rows - 1) × 10 + 4 |
| position | top edge at 72 % of the visible screen height measured from the bottom (28 % from the top), centred on the screen under the pointer; height fixed when it opens so filtering never resizes it |
| background | `.regularMaterial`, radius 22 continuous |

Search field: plain, 18 pt, "Search", focused on open. Tile: `VStack(spacing: 8)`, avatar 56, title 12.5 pt medium, one line, tail truncation; an 8 pt blue unread dot before the name (`HStack(spacing: 5)`); a floating badge `pip.fill` 10 pt semibold white on an accent circle (padding 4) offset (6, -4) at the avatar's top-trailing corner; tile background accent 28 % when selected, otherwise primary 4 %, radius 14 continuous, horizontal padding 6 (`Sources/Noodle/AgentPicker.swift:363-402`). Items are every non-archived conversation, ignoring the current space and sidebar search; floating ones first, then by last activity (`Sources/Noodle/AgentPicker.swift:20-32`). Keys: arrows move by 1 or 4 and never wrap; Return or keypad Enter picks; Escape closes; ⇧⌘C picks and calls the bot (only if no call is running); ⇧⌘D picks and starts a voice message once the panel's composer has mounted; typing filters and resets the selection to the first tile. Empty: "No Conversations". A pick opens the conversation as a floating panel.

**Activity windows.** One per bot, titled "<Name> - Activity" (kept in sync on rename, closed when the bot disappears), 760 × 500, min 440 × 260, centred, not minimisable or zoomable, closed by the close button, Escape or ⌘W ("Close Activity (Esc or ⌘W)"). Content: selectable 12 pt monospaced text with 12 pt insets, re-rendered at most every 0.2 s; "No activity yet" 13 pt secondary when empty; a 34 pt glass "Follow Latest" button (`arrow.down` 13 semibold), 16 pt from the bottom, fades in over 0.15 s when the newest output is out of view; context menu Copy, Copy All, Select All, —, Follow Latest, Clear (`Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/AgentActivityWindow.swift:5-288`).

**Usage, Settings, Hub panels.** Usage is a single window (860 × 680) removed from automatic menu commands and opened from the app menu with the bot filter cleared, or from Show Usage with it set (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:180-187`, `Sources/Noodle/UsageWindow.swift:5-19`). Settings is the system Settings scene, 740 wide, top-anchored resize, tab changes animated ease-in-out 0.22 s (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleSettingsView.swift:35-106,214-219`). Hub live-view panels are keyed by link, 1100 × 760 centred and clamped to the screen, dark content, ⌘W closes, "Escape belongs to what is shown" (`Sources/Noodle/HubSurfaceWindow.swift:18-101`).

**Error alert.** A single store `errorMessage` is shown as an alert titled "Noodle" with OK, only in the key window, so several open windows never stack duplicate alerts (`Sources/Noodle/ConversationWindow.swift:146-160`).

**Wordmark animation** (`Shared/Brand/Sources/NoodleBrand/WordmarkWelcome.swift:31-105`, `Shared/Brand/Sources/NoodleBrand/Wordmark.swift`). The word "noodle" is seven pen strokes in a 3819 × 851 design box (`viewBox="0 119 3819 851"`), pen width 128 design units, round caps and joins, stroked in `.primary`. Width `min(windowWidth × 0.34, 360)` (360 at the default size, so 80.2 pt tall, stroke ≈12.1 pt). A lead-in swirl rises from below the bottom edge, curls once (radius 4 × pen) and runs into the "n"; its tail follows the pen so only the word remains. Timing: 0.55 s pause, then the whole stroke written with ease-in-out over 3.4 s; at 4.05 s it lifts by itself (`continuesItself: true`) with `spring(duration: 0.7, bounce: 0.1)` to half scale; the lifted word is centred together with the content below it: centre = `max(24, (H - liftedHeight - 32 - nextHeight) / 2) + liftedHeight / 2`, gap 32; the content enters with opacity plus a 24 pt upward offset, and the lift spring is retargeted once the content's height is measured. With Reduce Motion everything appears at once. (The non-auto variant instead fades in a borderedProminent large "Continue" from 12 pt below over 0.5 s at 4.05 s, 16 % of the height from the bottom.) Closing the window during the welcome asks "Leave the welcome?" / "You can come back to it from Help > Welcome." with Leave and Cancel; leaving counts as Not Now (`Sources/Noodle/WelcomeView.swift:30-85`).

### 2.8 Notifications and system integration

**Notifications** (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleNotifications.swift`, `Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:259-295`). Authorisation for alert, sound and badge is requested at launch. One notification per new bot message, only when `!NSApp.isActive` or no window is visible and un-minimised; otherwise the received sound plays in the app instead (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:2158-2179`, `Sources/Noodle/MessageReceivedSound.swift:20-22`). Content: title = bot name; subtitle = group name for group chats; body = message text with tables removed (Markdown is not stripped here, unlike the sidebar); sound = the chosen system sound (default "Blow", copied to `~/Library/Sounds` because notifications only find sounds there); attachment = the bot avatar rendered at 128 pt plus 8 pt padding at 2x as PNG; identifier = message id. A separate sign-in notification, "<Harness> needs you to sign in again." (fallback "The harness"), is shown even while Noodle is in front, one per bot (identifier `sign-in-<botID>` replaces the previous one). Clicking a message notification activates Noodle, stores a viewport anchored on that message (or the bottom if it is the latest) and posts a reveal, then raises the window already showing the conversation (separate or floating before main), or selects it in the main window and shows or reopens that window, which also covers a launch from the notification; clicking a sign-in notification opens Settings → Harness (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleNotifications.swift:153-170`). No categories, actions or text-input reply exist anywhere in the repository (no `UNNotificationCategory` or `UNTextInputNotificationAction`).

**App Intents / Shortcuts** (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleIntents.swift`). One intent, "Send to Agent": parameters "Agent or Group" ("Who should receive the message?") and "Message" ("What would you like to send?"), summary "Send <Message> to <Agent or Group>", runs in the background, replies "Sent to <name>."; errors "Enter a message to send." and "That Noodle conversation is no longer available.". Entities list non-archived conversations newest first, subtitle "Agent" or "Group", image `person.crop.circle` or `person.3.fill`. App Shortcut phrases include "Send to <conversation> with <app>", "Message <conversation> with <app>" and "Tell <conversation> using <app>"; tile `paperplane.fill`, teal. Parameters are refreshed whenever bots or groups change.

**URL scheme and deep links.** Scheme `noodle` (development `noodle-dev`) (`Project.swift:154-167`, `Support/Info.plist:23-41`); all external events route to the single main window (`Sources/Noodle/ExternalEventPresentation.swift:5-16`). `noodle://join-hub?i=<base64url>` (a Hub invitation, valid 15 minutes, also the QR payload) selects Settings → Hub and opens Settings with the invitation waiting (`Shared/HubLink/Sources/HubLink/LinkProtocol.swift:1582-1633`, `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:865-871`, `Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:357-360`); `noodle://mcp/oauth/callback` completes a tool sign-in (`Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/MCPController.swift:183-196`); `noodle://shared` is an opaque wake-up from the share extension ("no text or file paths in URLs") that makes Noodle import pending shares, which it also polls every second (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:251-256`, `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:2218-2233`).

**Services and share extension.** Services → "Send to Agent…" accepts files, plain text or URLs from any app and opens a 460 × 360 titled panel (`Support/Info.plist:69-110`, `Sources/Noodle/NoodleServices.swift`). The share extension "Send to Noodle" accepts up to 100 files, images or movies, text, and up to 20 web URLs (`Support/ShareExtension-Info.plist:21-43`). Both show `ShareComposer` (`Sources/NoodleSharing/ShareComposer.swift:183-238`): 420 wide, padding 20, spacing 16; header `paperplane.fill` (tint) + "Send to Agent" headline; a "Send to" picker of bots and groups sorted by name (`person.crop.circle` / `person.3`), defaulting to the first; while loading "Preparing shared items…"; a preview box (max height 140, padding 10, `.quaternary` radius 8) of the text at 12 pt and `doc`-labelled file names; "Add an instruction (optional)" field of 3-5 lines; red error; Cancel (Escape) and Send/"Sending…" (Return). With no destinations: "Open Noodle and create a bot or group, then share again." Shared web pages stay links and are never downloaded.

**Updates.** Sparkle with a signed appcast, daily scheduled check, automatic checks on and automatic install off by default (`Support/Info.plist:127-146`). UI: "Check for Updates" in the app menu (disabled until Sparkle can check); Settings → Update with "Installed Version", an orange caption "Update available — <version>", one button titled "Check for Updates" or "Install Update…", and toggles "Automatically check for updates" and "Automatically download and install updates" (the second disabled unless allowed) (`Sources/Noodle/AppUpdater.swift:67-102`, `Shared/SettingsUI/Sources/NoodleSettingsUI/UpdateSettingsButton.swift`). Opening Settings probes silently so the Update tab can carry a badge.

**Settings tabs and badges.** General `gearshape`, Conversation `bubble.left.and.bubble.right`, Harness `terminal`, Bots `sparkles`, Groups `person.3`, Tools `puzzlepiece.extension`, Keybindings `keyboard`, Permissions `hand.raised`, Companions `square.stack.3d.up`, Hub `server.rack`, Update `arrow.triangle.2.circlepath` (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleSettingsView.swift:40-91`). Count badges on Harness (accounts needing attention plus failed bots that can be kicked), Tools (connections with errors), Permissions (refused), Companions (updates) and Update (1 when available) are custom views copying AppKit's toolbar badge: a red capsule 12 pt tall, at least 12 wide (text + 4), white 8 pt text, at the tab icon's top-trailing corner, click-through (`Shared/SettingsUI/Sources/NoodleSettingsUI/SettingsTabBadge.swift:92-140`).

**This Mac as a Hub.** Settings → Hub can turn this Mac into a personal Hub for the owner's other devices; while on it holds an idle-sleep assertion with the reason "Your devices can reach this Mac" (`Sources/Noodle/ThisMacHub.swift:48-80`). It has no shell UI of its own beyond the Spaces entries it enables.

### 2.9 Navigation and selection state, restoration

| State | Type | Persisted | Default / rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `selectedConversationID` | UUID? | no | kept across reloads while it exists; otherwise the first non-archived conversation, i.e. the most recently updated | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:79,613-617` |
| `searchText` | String | no | "" | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:80` |
| `space` | String? | `UserDefaults` "Noodle.space" | nil = All | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:61-64,379-382` |
| `columnVisibility` | split visibility | no | `.all` | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:329` |
| `showsWelcome`, `showsConnect` | Bool | dismissal flag only | mutually exclusive takeovers | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:105-107,318-343` |
| `creationSheet` | `.bot`/`.group`? | no | nil | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:35-45,103` |
| `agentBeingEdited`, `groupBeingEdited`, `backgroundBeingEdited` | item? | no | nil | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:109-111` |
| `spaceNaming`, `spaceBeingDeleted` | enum / item? | no | nil | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:71-75,112-113` |
| `selectedSettingsTab` | enum | no | `.general` | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:108` |
| `errorMessage` | String? | no | nil | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:115` |
| unread conversations | Set | repository | | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:76-78` |
| pins | ordered list | repository (All), the Hub (Hub space), the space (custom) | | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:463-538` |
| drafts | per conversation text and attachments | in memory only | kept while switching chats | `Sources/NoodleCore/ConversationDrafts.swift:5-28` |
| transcript viewport | per conversation | `scroll-positions.json` | | `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:224,1506-1515` |
| separate window frames | per conversation | `conversation-windows.json` | | `Sources/Noodle/ConversationWindowSession.swift` |
| floating set | Set | `UserDefaults` | | `Sources/Noodle/FloatingConversations.swift:9-38` |

Selection changes: creating a bot selects its direct chat; creating a group selects the group; the starter team selects "Team"; Show in Main Window and notification clicks select; archiving the selected conversation, or a Hub removing it, clears the selection (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:696-699,722-725,826-831,958,1185`).

Restoration. The main window always opens at launch, centred until the person moves it (then macOS restores its frame). Conversation windows opt out of system restoration and are restored by Noodle from `conversation-windows.json`, which is checkpointed on every move and resize (never while full screen), removed when a window is closed explicitly, kept when windows close because of Quit, and pruned when conversations are deleted; at launch each saved conversation reopens in id order, as a floating panel if it was floating, and its frame is constrained to the screen (`Sources/Noodle/ConversationWindow.swift:164-224`, `Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:233-236,346-356`). A second launch activates the running copy and exits (`Shared/LaunchChecks/Sources/NoodleLaunchChecks/AppInstance.swift:10-24`).

## 3. Web translation

**Routes.** `/c/:conversationId` (main shell; `?m=:messageId` reveals a message, used by notification clicks); `/` redirects to the most recent non-archived conversation, matching Noodle's launch rule; `/welcome` and `/connect` render takeovers inside the same shell route (or as `takeover` state); `/settings/:tab` with tabs `general | conversation | harness | bots | groups | tools | keybindings | permissions | companions | hub | update`; `/usage?bot=:id`; `/window/c/:id` a chrome-light route for separate windows and the floating fallback; `/share` for the share target; `/join-hub?i=…` hands the code to `/settings/hub`. Keep the space out of the URL (it is a persisted view filter), or use a `?space=` parameter if links must be shareable.

**Component boundaries.**

```
<AppShell>                    grid: [sidebar 280-380, default 326] [detail 1fr]; min 980 x 670 on desktop
  <Wallpaper/>                absolute inset 0, z 0, behind both columns; crossfade 350 ms; forces dark scheme
  <HeaderShade/>              absolute top, 64 px, z 1, pointer-events none
  <Sidebar>                   z 2, translucent
    <SidebarToolbar/>         [HideSidebar 37 px circle] gap 15 [CreateMenu 44 x 37 pill], right-aligned, height 52
    <SidebarSearch/>          28 px capsule, 7 px side inset
    <SpaceSwitcher/>          new on web: Noodle shows the space only in the menu bar
    <ConversationList>        role=listbox, sections Pinned / Bots / Groups
      <ConversationRow/> + <RowContextMenu/>
  <Detail>
    <DetailToolbar/>          [Info …] flex [CallControl] [SharedPopover]
    <ChatView/> | <EmptyDetail/> | <FirstBotPrompt/>
  <Sheets/> <Alerts/> <ConversationPicker/> <FloatingPanels/>
```

**State shape** (Zustand or similar; server state such as conversations, unread and pins in TanStack Query):

```ts
type ShellState = {
  selectedConversationId: string | null;          // from the route
  searchText: string;                             // transient
  space: string | null;                           // localStorage "noodle.space"; null = All
  sidebarVisible: boolean;                        // transient, default true
  takeover: 'none' | 'welcome' | 'connect';
  welcomeDismissed: boolean;                      // server or localStorage
  creationSheet: 'bot' | 'group' | null;
  editing: { kind: 'bot' | 'group' | 'background'; id: string } | null;
  spaceNaming: { kind: 'new'; adding?: string } | { kind: 'rename'; spaceId: string } | null;
  error: string | null;                           // render only in the focused window
  floating: string[];                             // localStorage, restore offer at launch
  keepOneFloat: boolean;
  windowFrames: Record<string, { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number }>;
};
// Derived: visible = conversations.filter(notArchived && inSpace); filtered = matches(title, description, member names, message text);
// pinned = pinOrder.map(id => filtered[id]); bots/groups = filtered minus pinned, sorted by updatedAt desc.
```

**CSS values.**

```css
.sidebar { background: rgb(0 0 0 / .24); backdrop-filter: blur(30px) saturate(1.4); } /* light: .04; blur is an approximation of the native sidebar material */
.row { box-sizing: border-box; height: 70px; padding: 2px 10px 2px 14px; display: flex; gap: 10px; align-items: center; position: relative; }
.row .unread { position: absolute; left: 1px; top: 50%; width: 8px; height: 8px; margin-top: -4px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--system-blue); }
.row .avatar { width: 42px; height: 42px; position: relative; flex: none; }
.row .status { position: absolute; right: 0; bottom: 0; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 50%;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--window-bg), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--window-bg); }        /* SwiftUI's centred 2 pt stroke */
.row .title { font: 600 13.5px/1.2 var(--font-sf); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }
.row .time { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--label-tertiary); margin-left: 4px; }
.row .preview { font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--label-secondary); display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden; }
.row::after { content: ""; position: absolute; bottom: 0; left: 66px; right: 6px; height: 1px;              /* every row, the last of a section too */
  background: color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 12%, transparent); }                                       /* 66 = 14 inset + 42 avatar + 10 gap; right measured */
.header-shade { position: absolute; inset: 0 0 auto; height: 64px; pointer-events: none; backdrop-filter: blur(20px);
  background: linear-gradient(rgb(0 0 0 / .24), rgb(0 0 0 / .10) 50%, transparent);           /* light: .06 / .03 */
  mask-image: linear-gradient(#000, rgb(0 0 0 / .88) 55%, transparent); }
.header-shade-wrap { filter: drop-shadow(0 5px 14px rgb(0 0 0 / .24)); }                        /* a box-shadow would be masked away */
.transcript { mask-image: linear-gradient(transparent 0, rgb(0 0 0 / .12) 28.8px, #000 64px); }
.detail { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-bg) 28%, transparent); }
```

Tokens: system blue `#007AFF` / `#0A84FF`, green `#34C759` / `#30D158`, red `#FF3B30` / `#FF453A`, gray `#8E8E93` (Apple's published light / dark values, not from this repository); secondary and tertiary labels roughly 50-55 % and 25 % of the label colour (inferred). Font stack `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", Inter, system-ui, sans-serif`. Glass toolbar buttons can be approximated with `backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(1.6)`, a 0.5 px light border and a soft shadow (inferred; Noodle uses the system's Liquid Glass and sets no values).

**Timing and motion.** Transcript switch: opacity cross-dissolve 160 ms ease-out, cancel and restart on each switch. Wallpaper: preload the next image, then 350 ms ease-in-out cross-fade; switching the colour scheme to dark for non-default wallpapers can use the View Transitions API for the 350 ms whole-window fade. Sheets: fit content, animate height with the top edge pinned (`noodleSheetSizing`, `Shared/SettingsUI/Sources/NoodleSettingsUI/SheetSizing.swift:5-66`). Wordmark: reuse `website/app.js:15-99`, which already writes the same SVG strokes on the web (it draws the swirl 1.6x faster and fades its first 35 % in, which the app does not); for the lift, Framer Motion's `{ type: "spring", duration: 0.7, bounce: 0.1 }` uses the same duration-and-bounce parameterisation as SwiftUI (close, not verified identical). Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` exactly where Noodle checks Reduce Motion.

**shadcn / Radix mapping.** Create → `DropdownMenu` with `DropdownMenuShortcut`; row menu → `ContextMenu` with a `ContextMenuSub` of `ContextMenuCheckboxItem`s for Spaces; Kick, New Session, Delete Space, "Leave the welcome?" → `AlertDialog` (Delete Space with Cancel focused); New/Rename Space → `Dialog` with one `Input`; New Bot (520), New Group (480), Edit Bot (520), Group Info (460), Background (520) → `Dialog` with a "Cancel · Title · Create/Save" header and `Tabs` rendered as a segmented control; Shared → `Popover` 340 wide; tooltips (`help:` strings, runtime help) → `Tooltip`; Settings → `Tabs` inside a page or large `Dialog`, badges as a 12 px red capsule with white 8 px text (consider 16 px for web legibility); sidebar width → a custom pixel-clamped resizer (react-resizable-panels works in percentages by default; pixel limits need extra handling, inferred). The picker grid needs its own keyboard model: cmdk only navigates linearly, while Noodle moves by ±1 and ±4 without wrapping.

**List keyboard model.** `role="listbox"` with `aria-activedescendant`, selection follows focus (switches the chat immediately), Tab moves to the composer only when something is selected and the search field is not focused, Shift-Tab from the composer returns to the list and re-opens a collapsed sidebar.

**Read tracking on the web.** Mark read on selection, on `visibilitychange` to visible plus `document.hasFocus()` while the conversation is shown, on any `pointerdown`, `keydown` or `wheel` in that window, on composer focus and on typing. Never mark read for a hidden tab or a minimised popup. Badge with `navigator.setAppBadge(unreadConversationCount)` in an installed PWA.

**Multiple windows.** Separate windows: `window.open('/window/c/' + id, 'noodle-c-' + id, 'popup,width=760,height=810')`, keep a handle per conversation and call `focus()` on reopen; persist `screenX`, `screenY`, `outerWidth`, `outerHeight` on `resize` and `pagehide`. Popups cannot be reopened automatically at load (blocked without a user gesture), so offer "Reopen windows" instead of Noodle's silent restore. Floating: the Document Picture-in-Picture API (`documentPictureInPicture.requestWindow({ width: 420, height: 560 })`, Chromium only) gives an always-on-top window that renders arbitrary React through a portal, but only one per page, which equals Noodle's "Keep one floating conversation" forced on, and the minimum size cannot be enforced; fall back to an in-page fixed panel (420 × 560, min 380 × 360, drag by header, blurred backdrop) in other browsers. Sync drafts, unread and selection between windows with `BroadcastChannel` or server push, since Noodle relies on one in-process store. A global ⌃⌥Space and floating over other apps' full-screen spaces are impossible from a page; they need a desktop wrapper (Electron `globalShortcut`, Tauri global-shortcut plugin).

**Shortcuts on the web.** Port the registry as data (`{ id, title, summary, default }`), store only overrides with `null` meaning disabled, validate against a reserved list, and render bindings in menus and tooltips from the same source. Browser-reserved combinations differ from macOS: Chrome does not deliver ⌘N, ⌘T, ⌘W and their Shift variants to pages, so New Bot ⌘N and New Group ⇧⌘N need web defaults; ⌘1-⌘9 may also be taken by tab switching (verify per browser). ⌘F can be intercepted with `preventDefault`, at the cost of the browser's find bar.

**Notifications, share, links.** Show a Web Notification only when `document.visibilityState !== 'visible' || !document.hasFocus()`; otherwise play the in-app sound. Use `tag: messageId`, and `tag: 'sign-in-' + botId` with `renotify: true` for sign-in prompts; the click handler in the service worker focuses an existing client showing the conversation, else opens `/c/:id?m=:messageId`. Strip Markdown from the body (Noodle does not). Share: a manifest `share_target` (`POST` multipart to `/share`, accepting text, url and files) feeding the same composer. Deep links: plain HTTPS routes; `navigator.registerProtocolHandler('web+noodle', '/open?u=%s')` only if a custom scheme is really needed (web schemes must start with `web+`). There is no web equivalent of App Intents; an authenticated `POST /api/conversations/:id/messages` covers the "Send to Agent" automation case.

**Phone widths.** Follow Noodle Mobile rather than shrinking the Mac layout: one list (pinned as a 3-column grid of circles, then rows), search, swipe to pin, a space menu as the title, a plain "…" More button, and the chat pushed on top (`Mobile/Sources/NoodleMobile/Chats.swift:960-1035`); the hero image shows relative times ("2 hr ago") and disclosure chevrons there.

## 4. Patterns worth copying, and pitfalls

Worth copying:
- The conversation is the only navigation unit; sections, pins and spaces are views over one sorted list, and one `selectedConversationID` drives the detail.
- The Create menu travels with the sidebar: in the sidebar's toolbar when it is open, in the window toolbar when it is hidden.
- A 64 pt header shade plus a 64 pt content fade let a transparent toolbar sit on any wallpaper; a non-default wallpaper forces dark chrome.
- Read state needs evidence of viewing (visible, focused, interacted with), not just being the selected row.
- Notifications only when the person is not looking; one replaceable sign-in notification per bot; clicking lands on the exact message in whichever window already shows it.
- One extra presentation per conversation (window or float), and "Show in Main Window" raises the main window before closing the other, so the app never has zero windows.
- The picker doubles as a switcher of open floats (floats first, badged) and lets Call and Voice shortcuts act on the highlighted tile.
- Shortcuts as validated data with reserved and conflict checks, explicit disable, per-command reset and live menu labels.
- First run is immediately useful: an account picker that installs and signs in by itself, then a ready-made three-bot team that introduces itself; "Not Now", a persistent empty-state button and Help → Welcome keep it recoverable.
- Errors render in the key window only; destructive confirmations default to Cancel; HUD panels share one frame component.

Pitfalls (in Noodle, or in porting it):
- The active space is invisible in the window; on the web there is no menu bar, so a visible switcher is required.
- File → New Group stays enabled with no bots and silently does nothing (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:145-148,528-532`).
- Usage ⇧⌘U is bindable in the model but has no row in Keybindings, so it cannot be changed or cleared from the UI.
- Dropping a file over any sidebar row attaches it to the selected conversation, not to the row under the pointer.
- ⌘F is a global notification heard only by the main window's sidebar; from a separate window it probably focuses a search field the person cannot see (inferred).
- Rows jump to the top without animation when bots reply; older dates always carry the year.
- The picker ignores the current space and the sidebar search.
- Notification bodies keep raw Markdown; there are no notification actions or inline reply to copy.
- The welcome gives nothing actionable for about 4 seconds while the wordmark writes; on the web add click-to-skip.
- Selection is not restored at launch (the most recent conversation is chosen); a route-based web app will restore it, which is an intentional difference to decide on.
- Window restoration, floating above other apps and a system-wide hot key do not exist for web pages; plan explicit fallbacks.
- The repository screenshots are stale for the toolbar (sliders instead of `ellipsis`); trust the code.

## 5. Open questions and inferences

- `.primaryAction` placement: the screenshots put the Edit Bot button at the leading edge of the detail toolbar, which matches macOS convention, but the code does not state it (inferred from screenshots).
- Toolbar band height, glass button sizes, selection radius and section header font are system-drawn; the values given are screenshot measurements (±1 pt), not code.
- Whether macOS autosaves the sidebar width between launches is not handled in code (inferred: system split-view behaviour).
- The floating panel's toolbar items (title, Call, Show in Main Window, Shared) presumably reach the `NSPanel` through `NSHostingView` scene bridging; `docs/usage.md:53-56` confirms the header and close button but the bridging itself is inferred.
- System menu items (View → Show/Hide Sidebar, Window list entries named after each conversation window's title) and the "No Results" copy of `ContentUnavailableView.search` are standard behaviour, not verified in this repository.
- The selection highlight is grey in all screenshots (list not focused or window inactive); its accent-coloured focused form is assumed from the system sidebar style.
- Exact system colour values (`windowBackgroundColor`, label colours) are Apple defaults and are inferred, as are the Chrome reserved-shortcut notes in §3.
- `docs/usage.md:69` and `CHANGELOG.md` call the settings tab both "Conversation" and "Chat"; the current label is "Conversation" (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleSettingsView.swift:50`).

doc:docs-internal/research/noodle/analys.content:
# Noodle: visual language and design tokens

Noodle (v0.50.0, commit `702339e`) has almost no custom design system. Its look comes from four decisions applied consistently across the suite. (1) Colour comes from the operating system: there is not one `.colorset` in any asset catalogue, the accent is the user's system accent, and every surface is a semantic system colour, a material or a black/white overlay at a small alpha. (2) Type is SF Pro at a set of dense custom macOS point sizes (12.5 pt message text, 13.5 pt semibold row titles, 11.5 pt metadata), with system text styles for secondary chrome. (3) Liquid Glass (`.glassEffect`) appears only on floating controls (composer, chips, the mobile menus) plus the native toolbar and sidebar. In-content surfaces use the classic `.ultraThinMaterial` / `.regularMaterial`. (4) A per-conversation wallpaper is the main expressive layer. Whenever one is set, the whole window is forced into dark appearance, and legibility comes from a fixed stack: a 25 % black dim, a 64 pt header shade, a 28 % canvas tint and translucent bubbles. The brand itself is small: a cream lowercase "n" with a noodle tail on a `#0088FF` tile, a single-stroke wordmark that writes itself on first launch, and a website palette of soft slate plus `#0088FF`. This document records the exact numbers so the look can be rebuilt on the web.

Permalink base for every citation: https://github.com/pdparchitect/noodle/blob/702339e3153025c9fe9582783caff7a19b48ff97/ (citations below are repo-relative `path:line`).

---

## 1. Scope

**Code read in full or in the relevant parts.**

- Components: `Sources/Noodle/Components.swift`, `Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/BotAvatar.swift`, `HarnessProviderIcon.swift`, `SettingsStatusLabel.swift`, `HarnessSettingsView.swift` (status rows), `Mobile/Sources/NoodleMobile/Appearance.swift`, `Mobile/Sources/NoodleMobile/Chats.swift` (rows, bubble, composer, avatars), `Mobile/Sources/NoodleMobile/MessageActions.swift`.
- Chat chrome (visual specs only): `Sources/Noodle/ChatView.swift`, `SidebarView.swift`, `NoodleApp.swift` (window, toolbar), `TranscriptScrollView.swift`, `LongMessageText.swift`, `ScrollableChatComposer.swift`, `ComposerFocusSurface.swift`, `ConversationTransition.swift`, `ConversationEffectsView.swift`, `ConversationWindow.swift`, `AgentPicker.swift`, `AgentProfileSheet.swift`, `Overlays.swift` (sheets, icon editor), `GroupMemberPicker.swift`, `ConnectView.swift`, `FirstBotPrompt.swift`, `AttachmentPreview.swift`, `AttachmentLayout.swift`, `MessageLinkPreview.swift`, `MessageTableView.swift`, `MessageContextMenu.swift`, `ComposerAttachmentMenu.swift`, `NoodleSettingsView.swift`, `FloatingConversations.swift`.
- Wallpaper and compositing: everything in `Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/NoodleWallpaper/{AnimatedWallpaper, ConversationBackgroundView, ConversationWindowCompositing, ConversationWindowHeaderShade, IconAppearance, IconEditorSheet, CompanionContentPanel}.swift` and `Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/NoodleWallpaperCore/{ConversationBackground, SystemWallpaper, BackgroundMedia}.swift`; `Sources/Noodle/ConversationBackgroundView.swift`.
- Brand: `Support/AppIcon.svg`, `AppSymbol.svg`, `AppWordmark.svg`, `AppIconTemplate.svg`, the `AppSymbol.svg` and `AppIcon.png` of Computer, Browser, Applet, Hub and Mobile, `website/assets/symbol-*.svg`, `harness-*.svg`, `Shared/Brand/Sources/NoodleBrand/{Wordmark, WordmarkWelcome}.swift`, `Sources/Noodle/ScenarioFilm.swift` (`NoodleWordmark`).
- Website: `website/styles.css` (all 197 lines), the head and hero of `website/index.html`, `website/app.js`.
- Companion visuals: `Browser/Sources/NoodleBrowser/{BrowserViews, BrowserIconView}.swift`, `Computer/Sources/NoodleComputer/NoodleComputerApp.swift` (rows, status), `Applet/Sources/NoodleApplet/App.swift` (library cards), `Hub/Sources/NoodleHub/{App, HubPairView}.swift`, `Shared/SettingsUI/Sources/NoodleSettingsUI/{SheetSizing, SettingsTabBadge}.swift`.
- Repo conventions read as data (they are Noodle's rules, not instructions here): `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills/ui-copy/SKILL.md`.

**Inventories.** These are grep counts over the 600 non-test Swift files (`*.swift` outside any `Tests/` folder): main app, Shared, Mobile and the four companion apps. A count is the number of occurrences in source, not the number of rendered instances.

**Screenshots viewed.** `.github/readme/hero.png`, `mobile.png`, `applets.png`; `website/assets/screenshot-chloe.png`, `screenshot-group-chat.png`, `screenshot-harness.png`, `screenshot-hub.png`, `screenshot-computer.png`, `screenshot-browser.png`, `screenshot-applet.png`, `mobile-chats.png`, `mobile-new-bot.png`, `mobile-new-tool.png`, `social-card.png`; `docs/images/games-mac.png`; the app icons of all five apps; cast avatars `Scenarios/cast/{chloe, alfred, kai, sonia, wren, mila, victor}.jpg`.

**External reference.** System colour values and the macOS/iOS text-style tables were checked against Apple's Human Interface Guidelines (Color and Typography pages, HIG 2025/26 edition). Values the HIG does not publish numerically, such as label and background colours, are marked "approx." and use the widely measured UIKit/AppKit values.

---

## 2. Findings

### 2.1 Design stance

- **No custom colour assets.** The only asset catalogue contents are app icons, harness logos (template SVGs) and tool icons (`Support/Assets.xcassets/*.imageset`, `Support/ToolIcons/*.icon`). No `AccentColor` is defined, so `Color.accentColor` is whatever the user picked in System Settings (default blue).
- **Two accents.** `Color.accentColor` (46 uses) drives anything that represents *you* or *selection*: outgoing bubbles, the send button, your reactions, selected tiles, the drop ring and edit badges. A hard-coded `.blue` (35 `foregroundStyle(.blue)` uses, plus `Color.blue` fills) drives fixed system affordances: sheet header Cancel/Create/Save text, the unread dot, `plus.circle.fill` add buttons and the "working" status. With the accent set to Graphite, bubbles turn grey but the unread dot and the sheet buttons stay blue.
- **Hierarchy over hue.** `foregroundStyle(.secondary)` appears 314 times, more than all other foreground colours combined. Status hues are used only for status: red 57, orange 30, green 3.
- **Wallpaper-first chrome.** The window is made transparent (`ConversationWindowCompositing.swift:5-17` sets `isOpaque = false`, `backgroundColor = .clear`) so the native glass sidebar and the transcript both sit over one wallpaper. This is the iMessage-for-agents look in the screenshots.
- **Copy conventions** (from `.agents/skills/ui-copy/SKILL.md`, data). Labels are functional with no persistent hint text. A trailing `…` (single character) appears only when more input follows. Row buttons use `.buttonStyle(.link)` (40 uses), and secondary row actions go in a `…` menu with the destructive action last.

#### 2.2.5 Light, dark and per-conversation tinting

- **Default canvas follows the system.** `systemCanvas` resolves `textBackgroundColor` in the *app's* appearance, not the window's (`ConversationBackgroundView.swift:120-126`). A window that turns dark for a wallpaper therefore keeps a light canvas under the fading-in wallpaper instead of flashing black.
- **Any non-default wallpaper forces dark.** `WallpaperWindowAppearance` sets `window.appearance = .darkAqua` whenever `!background.isDefault` (`ConversationBackgroundView.swift:40, 129-156`), including the toolbar and sidebar. The switch is a 0.35 s `easeInEaseOut` `CATransition` fade across the window frame, skipped under Reduce Motion. Wallpapers are treated as dark scenes, so text over them is always white.
- **No colour extraction.** Nothing samples the wallpaper to tint chrome. The only per-conversation change is the wallpaper itself; bubbles over it carry `black 0.22` or `accent 0.28`.
- **iOS does not force dark.** The mobile backdrop draws over `systemBackground` with the same 25 % black dim (`Appearance.swift:19-34`). Mobile bubbles stay opaque (`secondarySystemBackground` or accent).
- **Website.** `color-scheme: light dark` with a full dark token set (`styles.css:7-31`). Near-black symbol SVGs are flipped with `filter: invert(1) brightness(.96)` in dark mode (`styles.css:50-52`).

#### 2.7.2 Translations

SwiftUI curves: `easeInOut` = `cubic-bezier(.42, 0, .58, 1)` (the site's own comment, `app.js:73`), `easeOut` = `cubic-bezier(0, 0, .58, 1)`, `easeIn` = `cubic-bezier(.42, 0, 1, 1)`. A bare `.easeOut` lasts 0.35 s.

SwiftUI `spring(duration: d, bounce: b)` has response `d` and damping ratio `1 − b`. With mass 1, stiffness = (2π / d)² and damping = 4πζ / d. Motion's (framer-motion) `{ type: "spring", visualDuration: d, bounce: b }` follows the same perceptual model and is the closest drop-in.

| SwiftUI | Damping ratio ζ | Stiffness | Damping | Motion config |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.spring(duration: 0.25)` | 1.0 | 632 | 50.3 | `{visualDuration: .25, bounce: 0}` |
| `.snappy(duration: 0.2)` (bounce 0.15, approx.) | 0.85 | 987 | 53.4 | `{visualDuration: .2, bounce: .15}` |
| `.snappy(duration: 0.28)` | 0.85 | 504 | 38.2 | `{visualDuration: .28, bounce: .15}` |
| `.spring(duration: 0.35, bounce: 0.25)` | 0.75 | 322 | 26.9 | `{visualDuration: .35, bounce: .25}` |
| `.bouncy(duration: 0.4, extraBounce: 0.05)` (bounce 0.35, approx.) | 0.65 | 247 | 20.4 | `{visualDuration: .4, bounce: .35}` |
| `.spring(duration: 0.7, bounce: 0.1)` | 0.9 | 80.6 | 16.2 | `{visualDuration: .7, bounce: .1}` |
| `withAnimation {}` default (iOS 17+/macOS 14+; approx. response 0.55, ζ 1) | 1.0 | 130 | 22.8 | `{visualDuration: .55, bounce: 0}` |

#### 2.7.3 Reduced motion

It is honoured almost everywhere:

- The wallpaper crossfade becomes instant.
- The window appearance fade and the conversation dissolve are skipped.
- The wordmark appears already written.
- Confetti/fireworks become a still 40 pt emoji ("🎉" / "🎆", Noodle data) in a `regularMaterial` circle with 12 pt padding.
- Video wallpapers show their poster, and dynamic wallpapers stop advancing.
- Emoji hover scaling and the animated sheet resize are off.
- The tab and segmented-picker animations become `nil`.
- On the website: no write-on, no smooth scroll, no nav transition.

| `pencil` | `Pencil` | `trash` | `Trash2` |
| `arrow.triangle.2.circlepath` | `RefreshCw` | `text.alignleft` | `AlignLeft` [`TextAlignStart` in newest] |

Others: `slider.horizontal.3` to `SlidersHorizontal`; `pip.fill` to `PictureInPicture2`; `arrowshape.turn.up.left` to `Reply`; `chart.bar` to `ChartColumn`; `tablecells` to `Table`; `macwindow` to `AppWindowMac`; `face.smiling` to `Smile`; `hand.raised` to `Hand`; `lock` to `Lock`; `link` to `Link`; `pin` to `Pin`; `eye` / `eye.slash` to `Eye` / `EyeOff`; `wand.and.stars` to `WandSparkles`; `bolt.fill` to `Zap`; `checkmark.seal.fill` to `BadgeCheck`; `ladybug.fill` to `Bug`; `shippingbox.fill` to `Package`. `apple.logo` has no lucide equivalent (lucide's `Apple` is the fruit), so ship an SVG. Lucide draws 2 px strokes at 24 px; to approximate SF semibold glyphs at 15–18 px, use `strokeWidth={2.25}`. Verify names against the installed lucide-react version.

### 2.9 Avatars

- **Illustrated cast** (`Scenarios/cast/*.jpg`; scenario JSON references them as `"avatar": {"image": "cast/chloe.jpg"}`). Images are 512 × 512 baseline JPEGs: one flat, saturated background (blue `#2B8BE0`-like, orange, cream `#FBE9D7`-like, cyan, yellow, peach; inferred from viewing) and a centred head-and-shoulders character filling about 80 % of the frame. There are two sub-styles: a sticker cartoon with thick dark outlines and blush cheeks (Chloe with a clipboard, Alfred with a cloche, Mila with headset and gamepad, Wren at a laptop with a `</>` speech bubble, Victor in a `</>` T-shirt) and an outline-free flat vector (Kai, Sonia). A prop states the role. Users can use any picture: it is scaled to fit 512 px and stored as JPEG at quality 0.86 for bots or PNG ≤ 2 MB for browsers and computers (`IconAppearance.swift:96-106`, `Overlays.swift:733`).
- **Shape.** Always a circle (`clipShape(Circle())`) with the black 0.2 / r 3 / y 1 shadow on the Mac; no shadow on iOS.
- **Generated fallback.** A gradient (section 2.2.4) with a white SF Symbol at 0.38 × size semibold (iOS 0.45), default `sparkles`. People get initials at 0.36 × size semibold rounded (iOS 0.4).
- **Group avatars** (`Components.swift:28-60`, identical on iOS at `Chats.swift:2562-2597`):
  - One member: a `.quaternary` disc at 0.88 S offset (+0.06 S, +0.06 S) behind the bot at 0.86 S offset (−0.06 S, −0.06 S) with a 2 pt `windowBackgroundColor` ring.
  - Several members: a `.quaternary` disc at full size with up to three bots at 0.62 S, each ringed 2 pt, at offsets (−0.18 S, −0.14 S), (+0.18 S, −0.14 S) and (0, +0.19 S).
- **Fallback.** With no participants, `questionmark.circle.fill` in `.secondary`. Archived bots are shown with `.grayscale(1)` (`GroupMemberPicker.swift:52`).
- **Header use.** The 82 pt avatar and the 22 pt semibold name are the *first row of the transcript* and scroll away with it; there is no fixed conversation header. Groups add the goal (13 pt secondary, max 460) and member names (12.5 pt secondary) (`ChatView.swift:565-623`).

### 2.10 Brand

- **Symbol.** A lowercase "n" whose right leg runs down and curls out to the right in a short tail: the noodle. It is drawn as one round-capped stroke (pen 128 units) on a 1254-unit grid and filled as a path in the icons (`Support/AppSymbol.svg`; the wordmark's `n` is its centre line, `ScenarioFilm.swift:7-12`).
- **App icon family** (`Support/AppIconTemplate.svg`). Every app has a `#0088FF` tile whose squircle is hand-drawn (slightly wobbly edges, a different inset per app: Noodle 12–1242, Computer and Hub 36–1220, Applet 30–1224, Browser 52–1203). The cream glyph varies per app:

  | App | Glyph | Cream |
  |---|---|---|
  | Noodle | the bare "n" | `#FDF2D7` |
  | Computer | "n" inside a monitor on a stand | `#FCF7D9` |
  | Browser | "n" inside a globe with meridians | `#FCFBD8` |
  | Applet | "n" inside a window with two dots and a title bar | `#FDFBD6` |
  | Hub | "n" on a screen above a box with two dots | `#FCF7D9` |
  | Mobile | same as Noodle | `#FDF2D7` |

  Website versions recolour the glyphs to `#1D1D1F` with tight viewBoxes (`website/assets/symbol-*.svg`), shown at 22 px in the nav, 48 px above features and 44 px on download cards. The favicon is the 1024 px icon PNG.
- **Wordmark** (`Support/AppWordmark.svg`, `Wordmark.swift:16-27`). "noodle" as one pen stroke: `viewBox="0 119 3819 851"`, `stroke-width="128"`, round caps and joins, `fill="none"`. Seven strokes in writing order: `n`, `o`, `o`, the bowl of `d`, the `d` stem at x 2848, the `l` stem at x 3020, `e` ending open at the lower right. Baseline 906, x-height top 343, ascender top 183, letter gap 44. It is drawn in `currentColor` (`.primary` in the app, `#1D1D1F` on the site).
- **Write-on.** A swirl rises from the bottom edge, curls once and runs into the `n`; the pen writes the word in one `easeInOut` stroke of 3.4 s after 0.55 s, with the swirl drawn 1.6× faster and its tail following the pen in. The word width is `min(34 % of window width, 360 pt)`. "Continue" (`.borderedProminent`, `.large`) rises after 4.05 s; continuing lifts the word to 0.5 scale with `spring(0.7, bounce 0.1)` (`WordmarkWelcome.swift:31-105`, `website/app.js:15-99`).
- **Website palette** (`styles.css:7-31`):

  | Token | Light | Dark |
  |---|---|---|
  | `--bg` | `#fcfcfd` | `#131519` |
  | `--bg-alt` | `#f2f4f7` | `#1b1e24` |
  | `--raised` | `#e8ebf0` | `#252930` |
  | `--ink` | `#1c1e22` | `#f3f4f6` |
  | `--gray` | `#676c75` | `#a3a8b2` |
  | `--nav-bg` | `rgba(252,252,253,.8)` | `rgba(27,30,36,.8)` |
  | `--blue` / `--blue-hover` | `#0088ff` / `#0077e0` | same |

  `theme-color` is `#fcfcfd` / `#131519`. Content width is 1080 px with 22 px gutters. Pills use `border-radius: 980px`; shots 14 px (10 px on mobile); stages 28 px (16 px), on a launch-pad photo with an `#3b4a63` fallback; download cards 18 px; focus ring `2px solid var(--blue)`, offset 3 px, radius 6 px. Breakpoints are 1068, 900 and 734 px, matching apple.com.

---

## 3. Web translation

### 3.1 Tokens (CSS custom properties)

```css
:root {
  color-scheme: light dark;
  /* System palette, HIG 26 (light) */
  --sys-red:#FF383C; --sys-orange:#FF8D28; --sys-yellow:#FFCC00; --sys-green:#34C759;
  --sys-mint:#00C8B3; --sys-teal:#00C3D0; --sys-cyan:#00C0E8; --sys-blue:#0088FF;
  --sys-indigo:#6155F5; --sys-purple:#CB30E0; --sys-pink:#FF2D55; --sys-gray:#8E8E93;
  --accent: var(--sys-blue);            /* user-selectable; never a brand colour */
  --link: var(--sys-blue);              /* fixed blue: sheet buttons, unread dot */
  /* Labels (macOS, approx.) */
  --label: rgb(0 0 0 / .85); --label-2: rgb(0 0 0 / .50);
  --label-3: rgb(0 0 0 / .26); --label-4: rgb(0 0 0 / .10);
  /* Surfaces (macOS, approx.) */
  --window-bg:#ECECEC; --canvas:#FFFFFF; --control-bg:#FFFFFF; --sidebar-tint: rgb(0 0 0 / .04);
  --separator: rgb(0 0 0 / .12); --hover: rgb(0 0 0 / .08); --wash: rgb(0 0 0 / .04);
  --bubble-in:#E6E6E6; --bubble-out: var(--accent); --bubble-out-ink:#fff;
  /* Status */
  --status-working: var(--sys-blue); --status-ready: var(--sys-green);
  --status-failed: var(--sys-red); --status-idle: var(--sys-gray); --status-busy: var(--sys-orange);
  /* Avatar gradients */
  --grad-0: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sys-blue), var(--sys-cyan));
  --grad-1: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sys-purple), var(--sys-pink));
  --grad-2: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sys-orange), var(--sys-yellow));
  --grad-3: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sys-mint), var(--sys-teal));
  --grad-4: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sys-indigo), var(--sys-blue));
  --grad-5: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sys-pink), var(--sys-orange));
  /* Brand */
  --brand-blue:#0088FF; --brand-cream:#FDF2D7; --brand-ink:#1D1D1F;
  /* Type */
  --font-text: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", system-ui, "Inter", "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
  --font-display: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Display", system-ui, "Inter", sans-serif;
  --font-mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, "JetBrains Mono", monospace;
  /* Radii */
  --r-6:6px; --r-8:8px; --r-10:10px; --r-12:12px; --r-13:13px; --r-14:14px;
  --r-bubble:16px; --r-composer:18px; --r-panel:22px; --r-pill:9999px;
  /* Motion */
  --ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(.42,0,.58,1); --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0,0,.58,1); --ease-in: cubic-bezier(.42,0,1,1);
  --dur-select:120ms; --dur-reveal:150ms; --dur-dissolve:160ms; --dur-hover-scale:180ms;
  --dur-snappy:200ms; --dur-tab:220ms; --dur-step:250ms; --dur-wallpaper:350ms;
  --dur-frame:1000ms; --dur-write:3400ms; --delay-write:550ms;
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root:not([data-theme="light"]) {
    --sys-red:#FF4245; --sys-orange:#FF9230; --sys-yellow:#FFD600; --sys-green:#30D158;
    --sys-mint:#00DAC3; --sys-teal:#00D2E0; --sys-cyan:#3CD3FE; --sys-blue:#0091FF;
    --sys-indigo:#6D7CFF; --sys-purple:#DB34F2; --sys-pink:#FF375F;
    --label: rgb(255 255 255 / .85); --label-2: rgb(255 255 255 / .55);
    --label-3: rgb(255 255 255 / .25); --label-4: rgb(255 255 255 / .10);
    --window-bg:#323232; --canvas:#1E1E1E; --control-bg:#1E1E1E; --sidebar-tint: rgb(0 0 0 / .24);
    --separator: rgb(255 255 255 / .12); --hover: rgb(255 255 255 / .08); --wash: rgb(255 255 255 / .04);
    --bubble-in:#333333;
  }
}
/* A conversation with a wallpaper is always dark, whatever the system says. */
.conversation[data-wallpaper] { color-scheme: dark; /* apply the same dark overrides here */ }
```

Type scale, desktop and faithful to macOS: `--text-delivery: 9.5px`, `--text-caption: 10px/13px` (recommend 11 px on the web), `--text-meta: 11.5px`, `--text-small: 12px`, `--text-message: 12.5px/calc(1.2em + 2px)`, `--text-body: 13px/16px`, `--text-row-title: 13.5px` at 600, `--text-input: 14px`, `--text-title3: 15px/20px`, `--text-title2: 17px/22px`, `--text-conv-title: 22px` at 600, `--text-large: 26px/32px`. Touch scale, faithful to iOS: 11/13, 12/16, 13/18, 15/20, 16/21, 17/22 (body, message), headline 17/22 at 600, 20/25, 22/28, 28/34, 34/41. Use the desktop scale for `(pointer: fine)` layouts and the touch scale for `(pointer: coarse)`, as Noodle uses 12.5 pt messages on the Mac and 17 pt on iPhone. When falling back to Inter, apply the website's letter-spacing per size (17 px at −0.022em, 14 px at −0.016em, 12 px at −0.01em, 21 px at +0.011em) and `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` where Noodle uses `.monospacedDigit()`.

**Tailwind v4.** Expose the tokens through `@theme inline { --color-label: var(--label); --color-label-2: var(--label-2); --color-accent: var(--accent); --color-bubble-in: var(--bubble-in); --radius-bubble: var(--r-bubble); --radius-composer: var(--r-composer); --ease-apple: var(--ease-in-out); … }`. Keep Tailwind's 4 px spacing grid and add the odd values Noodle relies on as arbitrary values (`px-[13px] py-2`, `pb-[11px]`, `px-[15px]`), so the 2 pt half-steps are not lost.

### 3.2 Component recipes

**Avatar with gradient fallback and cut-out status dot**

```css
.avatar { width: var(--s); height: var(--s); border-radius: 50%; overflow: hidden;
  background: var(--grad, var(--grad-0)); box-shadow: 0 1px 6px rgb(0 0 0 / .2);
  display: grid; place-items: center; color: #fff; }
.avatar > svg { width: calc(var(--s) * .38); height: calc(var(--s) * .38); stroke-width: 2.25; }
.avatar > img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; }
/* ConversationStatusAvatar: the ring is a transparent gap, not a stroke */
.status-avatar { position: relative; width: var(--s); height: var(--s); --dot: 10px; --ring: 2px; }
.status-avatar > .avatar { -webkit-mask: radial-gradient(circle at calc(100% - var(--dot)/2) calc(100% - var(--dot)/2),
    transparent calc(var(--dot)/2 + var(--ring) - .5px), #000 calc(var(--dot)/2 + var(--ring))); }
.status-avatar > .dot { position: absolute; right: 0; bottom: 0; width: var(--dot); height: var(--dot);
  border-radius: 50%; background: var(--status-ready); }
```

The sidebar variant uses a stroked ring instead: `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--window-bg)` on a 10 px dot (12 px visible). Window titles use `--s: 20px; --dot: 7px; --ring: 1.5px`.

**Group avatar.** A container of size `S` with `background: var(--label-4)` and `border-radius: 50%`. Up to three children of `0.62S` with `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--window-bg)`, centred and translated by `(-0.18S, -0.14S)`, `(0.18S, -0.14S)` and `(0, 0.19S)`. A single member is a `0.88S` disc translated `(0.06S, 0.06S)` behind a `0.86S` avatar translated `(-0.06S, -0.06S)`.

**Sidebar row.** Height 66; padding `2px 10px 2px 14px`; gap 10; avatar 42 with a 10 px dot. Title 13.5/600, one line; timestamp 11.5 `--label-3` on the first baseline with a minimum gap of 4; preview 12.5 `--label-2` clamped to two lines. 1 px `--separator` under every row. Unread is an 8 px `--link` dot absolutely positioned 13 px left of the avatar. Section headers are "Pinned", "Bots", "Groups". The column is 280–380 (326 ideal) over `--sidebar-tint` and a translucent sidebar material.

**Message row and bubble (desktop).** Flex row aligned to the bottom, gap 8; bot avatar 27; a minimum 120 px empty gutter on the far side. The bubble has `padding: 8px 13px; border-radius: 16px; font: 12.5px/calc(1.2em + 2px)`. Bot: `background: var(--bubble-in); color: var(--label)`. You: `background: var(--accent); color: #fff`. Over a wallpaper, replace both with the material recipes in section 2.5.4. Rows are 10 px apart and each reserves 2 extra px on top. Under your last message, "Delivered" is 9.5 px `--label-3` with 5 px right padding, 3 px below the bubble. System messages are a centred pill: `font: 500 11.5px; color: var(--label-2); padding: 7px 12px; border-radius: 14px;` on ultra-thin material, with a `person.2.fill` icon and at least 80 px on each side. Real squircles need `corner-shape: squircle` (Chromium 139+) or an SVG mask; a plain radius is an acceptable fallback.

**Reaction badges.** Absolutely positioned at the bubble's top-right, `transform: translate(5px, -12px)`, siblings overlapping by `margin-left: -6px`. Each badge: `min-width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 9999px; padding-inline: 7px` (only when count > 1). Emoji 14 px, count `500 10px`. Background `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 25%, transparent)` for yours, else `color-mix(in srgb, var(--label-2) 15%, transparent)`, both over an opaque `var(--window-bg)`. Border `1.5px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--canvas) 85%, transparent)`. The reaction set, as Noodle data: ❤️ 👍 👎 😂 🎉 ❓ 👀 ⏳ ✅ 🙏 🔥 💡.

**Composer (desktop).** Pinned over the transcript bottom with `padding: 0 12px 11px`; a row gap of 8; chips 7 px above it. `+` button: 36 × 36 glass circle, glyph 15 px at medium weight. Field: `min-height: 36px; border-radius: 18px;` regular glass, text 14 px, padding `6px (27+14)px 6px 12px` (+31 px when the mic shows), growing to 6 lines. Placeholder "Message {name}". Send: a 23 px filled circle-arrow in `--accent` inside a 27 × 36 hit area, 7 px from the right edge; when empty, a 22 px outline in `--label-3`. Mic: 16 px in 27 × 36, gap 4. No focus ring (focus is implied by the caret). Fade the transcript bottom beneath it with a soft mask.

**Wallpaper stack.** A positioned layer under both columns: `object-fit: cover` image or video (muted, looping, paused under `prefers-reduced-motion`). Then a `rgb(0 0 0 / .25)` dim, the 64 px header shade, `color-scheme: dark` on the shell, a detail tint of `color-mix(in srgb, var(--canvas) 28%, transparent)`, and a transcript mask `linear-gradient(transparent 0, rgb(0 0 0/.12) 28.8px, #000 64px)`. On change, crossfade the new layer in over the old for 350 ms `var(--ease-in-out)` after the image has decoded, never through blank.

**Conversation switch.** Avoid animating the transcript tree. Snapshot-crossfade instead: a 160 ms `--ease-out` opacity dissolve of the outgoing frame, for example the View Transitions API with `::view-transition-old(root)` fade-out and no slide.

**Sheets.** Header: three columns, plain "Cancel" in `--link`, a centred title (13 px bold on desktop), a plain primary action in `--link` (or `--label-2` when disabled), padding 16, then a divider. Body padding 20–24. Widths: Bot editors 520, Group 460, most editors 480, Icon 440, Profile 320. Sheets grow from the top edge as content changes.

**Status label.** `font-size: 10px` (caption) with a leading icon, never wrapping. Green check "Signed in" / "Ready"; `--label-2` "Sign-in required"; orange triangle "Needs attention"; "Checking…" with an ellipsis-circle icon.

**Cards.** A, settings card: `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--label-2) 7.5%, transparent); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--label-2) 11%, transparent); border-radius: 12px`. B, well: `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--label-4) 35%, transparent); border-radius: 12px`. C, tile: `background: var(--wash); border-radius: 12px`. D, library card: `background: var(--control-bg); border: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0/.06); border-radius: 14px`.

**Quick switcher.** 560 wide on regular material, radius 22, padding 18, an 18 px search field, a 4-column grid of 104 px tiles (gap 10, radius 14, `--wash`; selected `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 28%, transparent)`), 56 px avatars, 12.5/500 titles.

---

## 4. Patterns worth copying, and pitfalls to avoid

**Copy**

- **Wallpaper implies dark.** Forcing the dark scheme whenever a wallpaper is set, plus a fixed 25 % dim, makes arbitrary user images safe without colour analysis. It also halves the token work: wallpaper surfaces need only dark values.
- **One legibility stack, shared by every app.** The header shade, top fade, canvas tint and material bubbles are shared code (`Shared/Wallpaper`) used identically by Noodle, Computer, Browser and Applet. Build the web equivalent once as a layout primitive.
- **Reserve layout for transient badges.** Every row keeps 12 pt of reaction clearance, so adding a reaction never shifts the transcript.
- **Cut, don't stroke, status rings over translucent content.** The `destinationOut` cut reads correctly over glass and wallpapers, where a `windowBackgroundColor` stroke would show as a grey ring.
- **Separate "you" colour from "system" colour.** Accent marks you and your selection; fixed blue marks links, unread state and add actions.
- **Glass only where controls float.** Composer, chips, menus and the toolbar are glass; content (bubbles, cards, pills) uses materials or plain fills. This keeps Liquid Glass legible and cheap.
- **Seeded gradient avatars.** Six gradients with the SF Symbol at 0.38 × size give every bot a recognisable default with no image, and stay on-palette in both themes.
- **Dense but tuned type.** The 12.5 / 13.5 / 11.5 pt trio carries the Mac chat. Copying it, rather than defaulting to 14/16 px, is what makes a web clone feel native on desktop.
- **Reduce Motion as a first-class branch.** Every motion has a defined still equivalent, including a still emoji for celebration effects.

**Avoid**

- **Do not hard-code the accent as brand blue.** Noodle follows the system accent and the screenshots show it grey; offer an accent setting and make `--accent` the single source.
- **Do not put glass on content.** Translucent bubbles appear only over a wallpaper. Without one, bubbles are opaque (`#E6E6E6` / `#333333` or accent).
- **Do not re-run a wallpaper's colour into the chrome.** Noodle deliberately does not; it would compete with the per-conversation image and break contrast.
- **Do not animate the whole transcript on switch** (layout thrash, mirrored text). Dissolve a rendered frame instead.
- **Do not trust macOS caption sizes literally on the web.** 10 px captions (`.caption`, 203 uses) are legible in SF with macOS rendering but too small in many browser and font fallbacks; bump them to 11 px.
- **Do not assume an `n` icon can be a font glyph.** The symbol and wordmark are custom geometry; use the SVG paths, and on the web the stroked wordmark path with `stroke-width: 128` in its own viewBox.
- **Do not copy the outdated website screenshots blindly.** They show a `slider.horizontal.3` toolbar button where the current code has `ellipsis` (Edit Bot) and `square.stack` (Shared).

---

## 5. Open questions and inferences

- **Accent in the marketing screenshots** (inferred). Grey user bubbles and send arrows in `hero.png` / `screenshot-chloe.png` imply the Graphite accent; `games-mac.png` shows a green send circle (accent or older build). The code always uses `Color.accentColor`.
- **Toolbar drift** (inferred). The `slider.horizontal.3` toolbar icon in the website screenshots predates the current `ellipsis` + `square.stack` items (`NoodleApp.swift:473-492`); `games-mac.png` already shows the newer pair.
- **System label and background hex values** are the widely measured AppKit/UIKit values; Apple publishes them only as names. Treat them as approx. In macOS 26 the default `controlAccentColor` is assumed to equal the HIG 26 blue `#0088FF` / `#0091FF`.
- **Material and glass CSS** in section 2.5.4 are visual approximations; neither Apple materials nor Liquid Glass (refraction, specular edge, adaptive tint) have a CSS equivalent. Tune against screenshots in both themes.
- **Sidebar section headers and the search field** use system styling (`.listStyle(.sidebar)`, `.searchable(placement: .sidebar)` at `.controlSize(.large)`). Their exact metrics, roughly an 11 pt semibold secondary header and a 30 pt capsule search field, are inferred from screenshots, not set in code.
- **Spring presets.** The base bounces of `.snappy` (0.15) and `.bouncy` (0.3), and the default `withAnimation` spring (response about 0.55, ζ 1), are from Apple's documented presets as remembered, not re-verified here.
- **Mobile timestamps and bubble colour over wallpapers.** iOS keeps opaque bubbles and does not force dark (`Appearance.swift:19-34`, `Chats.swift:1955-1975`). Whether this divergence from the Mac is intentional is not stated in code.
- **Cast background colours** (`#2B8BE0`-like blue, `#FBE9D7`-like cream) were estimated by eye from the JPEGs, not sampled.

doc:docs-internal/research/noodle/analys.content:
# Noodle conversation surface: header, transcript, bubbles, composer and effects

Noodle's conversation pane is a SwiftUI `LazyVStack` transcript inside a native `ScrollView`, drawn over a window-wide wallpaper, with a Liquid Glass composer overlaid at the bottom and a 64 pt fade under a transparent toolbar. Messages are 16 pt-radius continuous rounded rectangles (they read as capsules at one line) with 12.5 pt text: translucent material over a wallpaper, solid fills otherwise. On the Mac every bot message carries its own 27 pt avatar at the bottom-left; there are no sender names, no run grouping, no timestamps, no day separators and no typing or streaming indicator (the iOS client does group runs). Markdown is inline-only with whitespace preserved; tables are cut out into their own sortable bubbles. Reactions are a fixed set of 12 emoji plus the system picker, hung 12 pt above the first bubble's top-right corner, and every row reserves that clearance so reacting never moves anything. The composer is a native `NSTextView` that grows to six lines; Return sends and `@` opens a native menu of bot names. Bots can fire confetti or fireworks, which play as a 4 s canvas overlay. Exact values with citations follow.

Permalink base for every citation below: https://github.com/pdparchitect/noodle/blob/702339e3153025c9fe9582783caff7a19b48ff97/

## 1. Scope
