### 2.2 Header

Noodle has no fixed conversation header bar. Identity is carried by (a) toolbar items and (b) a "conversation start" hero that is the first row of the transcript and scrolls away with it.

**Main window toolbar** (`NoodleApp.swift:461-495`): leading, the sidebar toggle and a Create menu (`plus`; items "New Bot" `person.crop.circle.badge.plus`, "New Group" `person.3.fill`) live in the sidebar's section while it is open (`NoodleApp.swift:369-399`). In the detail column: a `primaryAction` button with symbol `ellipsis`, labelled "Edit Bot" for a direct chat with your own (not shared) bot or "Group Info" for a group; then a flexible spacer; the Call control (`phone`, help "Call {name}") when the bot takes calls; and "Shared" (`square.stack`, help "Shared Computers, Browsers and Noodlets") when the chat has companion links. No title appears in the main window.

**Separate window toolbar** (`ConversationWindow.swift:68-143`): principal item = `ConversationStatusAvatar` 20 pt with a 7 pt status dot and 1.5 pt cut-out ring, 7 pt gap, then the name in `.headline` (13 pt bold), one line, tail truncation; then the Call control, "Show in Main Window" (`pip.exit`), a "Conversation Info" menu (`ellipsis`) holding "Edit Bot…" or "Edit Group…", "Change Background…", a divider and "Float on Top", and "Shared". During a call the Call button becomes `phone.fill` (green once connected) + `00:00` timer in monospaced digits ("--:--" while connecting) + Mute (`mic.fill`/`mic.slash.fill`) + End Call (`phone.down.fill`, red), spacing 10, each icon 18 pt wide so the toolbar never shifts (`VoiceCallToolbar.swift:6-48`).

**Shared popover** (`AttachmentPreview.swift:105-205`): 340 pt wide, height `min(count x 70 + 12, 460)`; rows 68 pt tall with an 84x54 preview clipped to radius 6, title (2 lines) and a caption "Browser", "Computer", "Noodlet" or "Noodlet unavailable"; hover fill primary at 0.08 opacity, radius 8; padding 6.

**Conversation start hero** (`ChatView.swift:565-623`), shown only when the oldest message is loaded (`ChatView.swift:526-530`), centred, `VStack` spacing 12, 14 pt bottom padding:

| Element | Direct chat | Group |
|---|---|---|
| Avatar | `BotAvatar` 82 pt, a button opening the bot's profile; context menu "Show Activity" if the bot runs on this Mac | composite group avatar 82 pt, button opening the group profile |
| Name | 22 pt semibold, 1 line, tail truncation | same |
| Goal / description | none | `publicDescription`, 13 pt, secondary, centred, max width 460 |
| Members | none | shown members' names joined by ", ", 12.5 pt, secondary, centred |

**Group avatar geometry** (`Components.swift:6-61`), as fractions of `size`: with 2+ members, a base circle filled `.quaternary` at full size, then up to the first 3 members at 0.62 x size, each stroked 2 pt in `windowBackgroundColor`, offset (-0.18, -0.14), (+0.18, -0.14), (0, +0.19); later ones draw on top, so the third sits in front at the bottom. For 82 pt: avatars 50.8 pt at (-14.8, -11.5), (14.8, -11.5), (0, 15.6). With one member: a `.quaternary` circle 0.88 x size offset (+0.06, +0.06) behind the avatar at 0.86 x size offset (-0.06, -0.06) with the same 2 pt stroke. "Shown" members drop archived bots unless all are archived (`NoodleStore.swift:644-649`).

**BotAvatar** (`BotAvatar.swift:11-28`, `IconAppearance.swift:24-70`): a circle holding either a custom image (`scaledToFill`) or a linear gradient top-leading to bottom-trailing from six pairs ([blue, cyan], [purple, pink], [orange, yellow], [mint, teal], [indigo, blue], [pink, orange]; index = seed mod 6) with a white SF Symbol at 0.38 x size, semibold (default `sparkles`). Shadow black 0.2, radius 3, y 1.

**Status dot** (`Components.swift:63-130`): one status per conversation: any member working = blue, else any failed = red, else all ready = green, else grey (offline and idle are grey). The dot sits at the avatar's bottom-trailing corner; a ring is cut out of the picture (opaque circle of dot + 2 x ring, offset by the ring width, `blendMode(.destinationOut)` inside a `compositingGroup`), so it reads on any background. Tooltip lists "{Name}: {runtime detail}" per member, or "Working on {Hub}" / "Runs on {Hub}" (+ " (not connected)") for Hub bots (`Components.swift:93-102`). Sidebar rows use a 10 pt dot with a 2 pt `windowBackgroundColor` stroke on a 42 pt avatar instead (`SidebarView.swift:146-158`).

**Shading** (`ConversationWindowHeaderShade.swift`): the shade is a 64 pt `ultraThinMaterial` rectangle with a black overlay gradient (dark mode 0.24 at 0, 0.10 at 50%, clear at 100%; light mode 0.06, 0.03, clear), masked by black 1.0 at 0, 0.88 at 55%, clear at 100%, plus a shadow black 0.24 (dark) or 0.06 (light), radius 14, y 5; it ignores the top safe area and is not hit-testable. The transcript itself is masked by `ConversationContentTopFade`, so message pixels fade to nothing as they pass under the toolbar (this is why the back two avatars of the group hero look washed out in `screenshot-group-chat.png`: they sit inside the 64 pt band).

### 2.3 Wallpaper and appearance

`ConversationWallpaper` (`Shared/Wallpaper/.../ConversationBackgroundView.swift:8-63`) decodes the next image or video poster off the main thread, then crossfades layers with `.easeInOut(duration: 0.35)` (none under Reduce Motion), so switching never flashes the default canvas. Under the layers is the default canvas in the *system* appearance (`textBackgroundColor`). Presets (`:108-115`): sunset, ocean, forest, dusk, each a 3-colour linear gradient top-leading to bottom-trailing plus an ellipse of colour 2 at 0.5 opacity, 1.4 x width by 1.1 x height, rotated -35 degrees, offset x +0.35 x width, blurred 50. Any non-default background adds a black 0.25 scrim (`:92`) and forces the window to dark appearance with a 0.35 s ease-in-out window crossfade (`:129-156`, `CHANGELOG.md:336`: "A conversation with a wallpaper keeps its window dark"). Video and multi-frame HEIC wallpapers loop muted and pause when hidden or under Reduce Motion (`CHANGELOG.md:1198`). The background editor sheet previews two sample bubbles, "Make this space your own." and "Looks good!", in `regularMaterial` capsules over a 210 pt preview with radius 16 (`Sources/Noodle/ConversationBackgroundView.swift:46-54`).

### 2.4 Transcript layout

**Container** (`TranscriptScrollView.swift:74-88`): `ScrollView` > `LazyVStack(spacing: 10)`, horizontal padding 15, top padding 30, then a clear bottom spacer of `composerHeight + 20` that doubles as the scroll target `.bottom`. The scroll indicator's bottom margin is `composerHeight + 8`. Composer height is measured live and includes the pending-attachment strip and the 11 pt bottom padding (`ChatView.swift:168-175`). There is no maximum content width.

**Row** (`Components.swift:214-322`): each message is one `VStack(spacing: 0)` with top padding `12 - 10 = 2`, so with the 10 pt row gap every row has exactly 12 pt above it for a reaction badge, reacted or not (`Components.swift:209-228`, `CHANGELOG.md:509`). Inside, an `HStack(alignment: .bottom, spacing: 8)`:

```
bot:   |15| avatar 27 |8| content (VStack leading,  spacing 3) |8| spacer >= 120 |15|
user:  |15| spacer >= 120 |8| content (VStack trailing, spacing 3)               |15|
```

So the widest bot content is `W - 193` and the widest user content `W - 158`, where W is the detail column width (the Chloe screenshot's bot bubbles wrap at about 723 pt in a ~924 pt column, matching `W - 193` = 731 minus wrap slack).

Content stack, top to bottom with 3 pt gaps (`Components.swift:276-311`): the text segments (one bubble per prose stretch or table), the link preview card (2.11), the attachment group (2.17), and, for the user only, the delivery label (2.8).

**Avatars, names and runs.** Every bot message shows its own 27 pt avatar, bottom-aligned with the last element of that message (`Components.swift:255-274`). It is a button opening the bot's profile (help = bot name, accessibility "Show {name}'s profile", context menu "Show Activity"). There is no run grouping, no sender name label in groups and no avatar spacer logic: in a group you tell speakers apart only by avatar (confirmed in both screenshots). User messages have no avatar.

**Timestamps and day separators:** none. `createdAt` is never rendered in the transcript, not even as a tooltip (`Components.swift`, `ChatView.swift`); the sidebar row is the only place a time shows.

**Alignment:** user right, bot left, system centred. Attachments of user messages align to the trailing edge too (`Components.swift:295`).

**The iOS client differs** (`Mobile/Sources/NoodleMobile/Chats.swift:516-534, 1488-1509, 1931-1981`) and is closer to iMessage: in groups the bot's name (caption, secondary, 12 pt leading inset) heads the first message of each run, the 28 pt avatar sits beside the *last* message of a run, other bot messages keep a 28 pt spacer so the run lines up; row gap 6, reaction overhang 16, side spacers 48; delivery only under your latest message or one that failed. For the web, the iOS run rules are the better model (see section 4).

### 2.6 Markdown, segments and long messages

**Inline only.** `MessageMarkdownCache.render` parses with `interpretedSyntax: .inlineOnlyPreservingWhitespace` and `failurePolicy: .returnPartiallyParsedIfPossible`, then strips any link whose scheme is not `http`, `https` or `mailto` (`MessageMarkdownCache.swift:58-73`). Supported: bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code and links, as SwiftUI `Text` renders them (code spans in a monospaced font, links in the accent colour: SwiftUI defaults, inferred). Block syntax is not interpreted: headings, list markers, quotes and code fences show as typed, with the original line breaks and blank lines. The screenshots show exactly this: "- Renewed the car insurance…" keeps its hyphen, "1. **A framed print…**" keeps "1." with the bold rendered, and "**Handled overnight**" is a bold line, not a heading.

**Segments.** `MessageSegment.split` (`Shared/HubLink/.../MessageTable.swift:8-49`) cuts a body at GitHub-style pipe tables (header row whose cell count equals the alignment row's, alignment cells of dashes with optional colons, following rows that contain `|`), ignoring tables inside ``` fences; prose between tables is trimmed of leading and trailing newlines. A body that merely looked like it might hold a table is kept byte-for-byte. Each segment is its own bubble; reactions hang on the first segment, whether text or table (`Components.swift:277-284`). Notification and sidebar previews drop tables ("Sent a table" if nothing else remains, `:54-59`).

**Caching.** Rendered text and segments are cached in `NSCache`s of 1,000 entries keyed by message ID (segments re-checked against the body) (`MessageMarkdownCache.swift:26-56`).

**Long messages** (`LongMessageText.swift:6-62`): a segment is "long" when its source exceeds 1,200 characters or 12 lines (13th line). Long text is clamped to 8 lines and followed (spacing 8) by a "Read more" button: `Label` with `text.alignleft`, 11.5 pt semibold, 2 pt vertical padding, accessibility "Read full message". It opens a popover (arrow at bottom) sized `min(600, screen width - 80)` x `min(540, screen height - 100)`: header "Message" (`.headline`), a copy button (`doc.on.doc`, help "Copy message", copies the raw body) and close (`xmark`, Escape), 16 pt padding, divider, then the text at 14 pt with +4 line spacing, 18 pt padding, selectable.

### 2.7 Message tables

A table is a bubble of its own (`MessageTableView.swift`, `MessageTable.swift`; `CHANGELOG.md:40`):

- Grid: no outer spacing, 4 pt horizontal padding; header band `Color.primary` at 0.06 opacity behind the whole header row; dividers at 0.6 opacity between rows (`MessageTableView.swift:57-94`).
- Header cell: 11.5 pt semibold, `.secondary` unless it is the sorted column (`.primary`), max width 260, padding 9 x 5, a sort chevron (`chevron.up` / `chevron.down`, 8 pt bold) always laid out but at opacity 0 unless active so widths do not jump; leading for normal columns, trailing for right-aligned ones. Help/accessibility "Sort by {name}", value "Ascending"/"Descending" (`:104-136`).
- Body cell: 12.5 pt with monospaced digits, up to 3 lines, max width 260, padding 9 x 5, selectable (`:76-86`).
- Alignment: from the Markdown colons; automatic columns go trailing when every non-empty cell parses as a number after stripping ` $€£%+×x` and thousands commas (`MessageTable.swift:82-89, 130-134`).
- Sorting: header click cycles ascending, descending, original order, animated `.snappy(duration: 0.2)`; numbers sort before text, text in Finder order (`localizedStandardCompare`); sort is view state, never stored (`MessageTable.swift:99-111, 183-186`).
- Width: a table that fits hugs its columns; a wider one fills the bubble and scrolls horizontally inside it (no indicators, bounce only when needed) (`MessageTableView.swift:17-36`).
- Folding: when there are more than 8 rows (6 shown + at least 3 hidden), the first 6 rows show, then a divider and a full-width button "{n} more rows" (`tablecells`, 11.5 pt semibold, padding 13 x 7) that opens a reader popover: header "Table" (`.headline`) + "{n} rows" (secondary) + the actions menu + close (Escape), 16 pt padding, then the whole grid scrolling both ways with 12 pt padding, `min(600, screen - 80)` x `min(540, screen - 100)` (`MessageTableView.swift:37-52, 166-193`).
- Hover: an `ellipsis.circle.fill` menu (14 pt, hierarchical rendering, 4 pt from the top-right corner) with "Copy as CSV" and "Save as CSV…" (save panel defaulting to "Table.csv"); CSV is RFC 4180 from the plain text of cells as currently sorted (`MessageTableView.swift:24-27, 139-164`, `MessageTable.swift:114-122`, `AttachmentDrag.swift:116-130`).

### 2.8 Delivery status

Every user message, not just the latest, has a 9.5 pt `.tertiary` label under it, 5 pt in from the trailing edge (`Components.swift:305-310, 522-529`): "Sent" (`.queued`, set when you send, `WorkspaceRepository.swift:1407-1432`) then "Delivered" once any recipient's harness fetches it from its inbox (`WorkspaceRepository.swift:1249-1260`; "In a group it is delivered once any member fetches it", `CHANGELOG.md:556`). "Saved" and "Not delivered" map `.saved` and `.failed`, which the Mac runtime does not produce today (only scenarios use them, `Scenario.swift:529`; inferred legacy). There are no read receipts and no failure affordance on the Mac (iOS shows a red `exclamationmark.circle` menu for unsent messages, `Chats.swift:1944-1953`).

**System notices** (`Components.swift:239-250`): centred `Label(body, systemImage: "person.2.fill")`, 11.5 pt medium, secondary, multiline centred, padding 12 x 7, `ultraThinMaterial` in a radius-14 rounded rectangle, at least 80 pt from each side. The only producer is a group edit, which writes one notice combining sentences such as "Kira was added to the group.", "Kira and Mara were removed from the group.", "The group description was updated: {text}" or "The group description was cleared." **Voice call card** (`VoiceCallToolbar.swift:77-115`): centred with at least 60 pt each side; `phone` (secondary) or `phone.fill` (green, live) at 15 pt, "Voice call with {bot}" 12.5 pt medium, then a live timer or the duration ("1 min, 4 sec" style) 11 pt secondary; padding 14 x 9, `ultraThinMaterial`, radius 14. What was said follows as **call blocks** placed after the last message sent before each line (`:198-216`): `waveform` 12 pt semibold + up to 2 one-line previews ("You  …" / "{bot}  …", speaker 11.5 pt semibold secondary, text 12.5 pt), "{n} lines" 10.5 pt tertiary, max width 380, padding 14 x 8, radius 12, clicking opens a 340x300 transcript popover (`:126-196`).

**Voice messages** (`VoiceMessagePlayer.swift:158-207`): a 270 pt card in `regularMaterial`, radius 16, padding 12 x 7: play/pause 28x32, a 60-bar waveform 28 pt tall (accent up to the playhead, secondary 0.6 after; click to seek), `m:ss` in caption monospaced digits. A voice-only message (body "Voice message") shows no text bubble (`Components.swift:376-379`).

### 2.10 Reactions

**Who and what.** Reactions belong to the message, not to a bubble. The user can add any number of different emoji (each toggles independently, `NoodleStore.swift:1979-1990`); bots react through the Messenger CLI, and every reaction change wakes all the conversation's bots except the one who reacted (`NoodleStore.swift:1959-1968`). Any single emoji is valid (`MessageReaction.isValidEmoji`, `Models.swift:166-170`).

**Quick set** (two rows of six, `MessageContextMenu.swift:48`): ❤️ 👍 👎 😂 🎉 ❓ / 👀 ⏳ ✅ 🙏 🔥 💡, followed by "More Emoji…" (`face.smiling`) which opens the system Character Viewer and accepts the first valid emoji typed into a hidden 1x1 text view (`:121-170`).

**Picker UI, inside the right-click menu** (`:172-270`): each row is a custom menu-item view 258 x 42 with buttons 38 x 36 at x = 9 + 40i, y = 3, emoji 22 pt, borderless. An emoji you already used gets an accent background at 0.25 opacity with corner radius 8 and tooltip "Remove your {emoji} reaction" (else "React {emoji}"). Hover scales only the glyph to 1.12 over 0.18 s ease-in-out, reversing from the current scale, skipped under Reduce Motion. Choosing closes the menu and toggles.

**Badges** (`Components.swift:381-520`):

- Placement: overlay at the top-trailing corner of the first text or table segment, or of the attachment group when the message has no text bubble; offset x +5, y -12, so a badge hangs 12 pt above the bubble and 5 pt past its trailing edge, for user and bot messages alike.
- Order: one badge per distinct emoji in order of first use; count shown when more than one person reacted.
- Stacking: `HStack(spacing: -6)` (overlapping); if that does not fit, a `LazyVGrid` of adaptive columns (min 48, spacing 4, max width 280).
- Badge: emoji 14 pt; count 10 pt medium with 4 pt gap; horizontal padding 7 only when counted; min 28 x 28 capsule; fill accent 0.25 if it includes yours, else `.secondary` 0.15, layered over an opaque `windowBackgroundColor` capsule so overlaps stay distinct; 1.5 pt inner border of `textBackgroundColor` at 0.85.
- Tooltip "{emoji} — {names}. Click to see who reacted." where names are "You", the bot's name, or "Noodle" for system.
- Click opens a 260 pt popover (padding 20, spacing 16, arrow at bottom): the emoji at 26 pt and the names at 13 pt centred; if one is yours, a divider then "Change Reaction…" (which swaps in a "Change Reaction" caption over a 6-column grid of the 12 quick emoji at 22 pt in 36 x 36 cells, spacing 10; choosing replaces yours, adding the new one before removing the old, `NoodleStore.swift:2064-2075`) and "Remove My Reaction".
- Animation: none. Badges appear in place; the reserved 12 pt clearance means rows never move (`CHANGELOG.md:509`, test `testAddingAReactionDoesNotResizeItsTranscriptRow`).

### 2.11 Link previews

**Which link** (`Components.swift:157-181`, `MessageLink.swift`): the first public web URL in the message, from Markdown link runs first, then `NSDataDetector`; http/https only, at most 2,048 characters, no credentials, host not `localhost`, `*.localhost`, `*.local`, IPv6 literals or private, link-local, CGNAT, benchmark or multicast IPv4 ranges. It is skipped when an attachment already links the same URL (`Components.swift:286-290`). Detection results are cached by body text (1,000 entries).

**Card** (`MessageLinkPreview.swift:30-173`): 280 x 220, clipped to radius 14 (continuous), `regularMaterial` background, 1 pt stroke white 0.12. Top: 280 x 158 image area over black 0.28; the image `scaledToFill`, top-leading, fades in over 0.15 s ease-out; while loading a small spinner; failed or imageless: `link` (or `map` for Apple Maps links) at 26 pt light, secondary; YouTube adds a centred `play.fill` 22 pt semibold white on a black 0.7 circle with 14 pt padding. Bottom: padding 11 x 9, title 12 pt semibold, 2 lines (Maps title, else page title, else host); site 10.5 pt secondary, 1 line, host without `www.` ("Apple Maps" for Maps), spacing 4. Accessibility "Open link: {title}" / "Open in Maps: {title}".

**Loading states:** nothing is fetched until the card has been on screen 300 ms (`fetchDelay`); one 10 s deadline covers metadata and image; every outcome stops the spinner; failures are cached for the launch so redraws do not retry; successes are kept on disk for 7 days (title + PNG) and in an `NSCache` of 128; images are downscaled to cover the card at 2x (560 x 316) before caching (`:218-376`). Apple Maps links render a MapKit snapshot instead (route line white 6 pt under system blue 3.5 pt, pins 12 pt, `:486-564`).

**Opening:** the card is a plain button that calls `openURL`; the chat intercepts web links and opens them in Quick Look via a temporary `.webloc` bookmark unless "Preview web links" is off or Command, Option or Shift is held, in which case the browser opens (`ChatView.swift:212-219`, `MessageLinkPreview.swift:175-197`, `NoodleSettingsView.swift:205-208`).

### 2.12 Context menus

### 2.13 Working, typing and streaming indicators

There are none in the transcript. Messages arrive whole: bots post through the Messenger CLI, the store re-reads each conversation's `messages.json` once a second off the main thread when its modification date or size changes (`NoodleStore.swift:1824-1971, 2218-2233`), and rows appear without animation (see 2.19). A bot's activity shows only as (a) the blue status dot on its sidebar row and, in separate or floating windows, on the 20 pt title avatar, with the runtime detail in the tooltip, and (b) its floating Activity log window ("Show Activity"), which carries tool calls and streamed output (`docs/usage.md:72-87`). No partial output ever renders in a bubble.

### 2.14 Scrolling, paging, restoration and performance

**Positioning rules** (`TranscriptScrollView.swift`):

- Anchors: initial offset at the bottom if the saved viewport was at the bottom, else top; size changes anchor to the bottom while following the latest message, else to the top; alignment top (`:98-100`).
- "At bottom" means within 2 pt of the maximum offset, or the content fits (`TranscriptScrollMetrics.swift:8-16`).
- Restore on open: after one `Task.yield`, scroll to the bottom sentinel or to the saved message ID anchored at the top, unless the user already scrolled (`:101-111`). A saved message that no longer exists, or a non-finite offset, falls back to the bottom (`TranscriptPositions.swift:15-21`).
- Following: when the user *ends* a scroll gesture, "follows latest" becomes "is at bottom" and the reading position (top visible row's message ID, offset, at-bottom flag) is saved per conversation to a JSON file (`:138-153`, `TranscriptPositions.swift:26-61`). Saves also happen on disappear and on quit, never from teardown geometry (`:180-196`).
- New last message: if it is yours, always follow and jump to the bottom; if a bot's, jump only when already following and not mid-gesture (`:154-167`). Scrolled up, nothing happens: there is no jump-to-latest button and no "new messages" pill (the Activity window has one, `CHANGELOG.md:449`; the chat does not).
- Window resize while reading history re-anchors the reading message at the top, only on viewport size changes, never from content geometry, to avoid feedback loops (`:89-97`, `:135-136`).
- A notification click posts `revealTranscriptMessage`; the transcript loads history back to that message if needed and scrolls to it (or to the bottom if it is the latest) (`ChatView.swift:557-561`, `TranscriptScrollView.swift:168-179`).

**Paging** (`ChatView.swift:486-562`): a conversation opens on its newest 100 messages, or from the saved reading message if that is older. Reaching the top shows a small spinner row (8 pt vertical padding) whose appearance loads the previous 100; rows keep their place by ID. The first shown message is pinned, so new replies extend the list rather than pushing old rows out under the reader. The start hero appears only once the first message is loaded.

**Performance techniques** (the reasons behind the code):

- Lazy virtualization (`LazyVStack`), and each row's body is one plain `VStack` because a bare `if/else` or a `.transition` at the row's root makes the lazy stack build every row up front (`Components.swift:216-219`).
- The draft is read only inside the composer's own subviews, so typing re-evaluates the composer and never the transcript (`ChatView.swift:381-382`, test `testTypingInTheComposerDoesNotReevaluateTranscriptRows`).
- Markdown, segment and link-detection caches (2.6, 2.11); thumbnails and link previews load only for visible rows (`onScrollVisibilityChange(threshold: 0.01)`, `Components.swift:315-317`) and reserve their final size before loading (`AttachmentPreview.swift:522-541`, `CHANGELOG.md:918`).
- Scroll geometry is written to a plain class rather than SwiftUI state, so scrolling publishes nothing per pixel (`TranscriptScrollView.swift:21-26`); `ScrollPosition` is never written from geometry callbacks.
- Transcript loading and change detection run off the main thread (`NoodleStore.swift:1838-1860`).

**On AppKit:** there is no AppKit table view; `MessageTableView` is the Markdown table bubble. The transcript is pure SwiftUI. AppKit appears where SwiftUI fell short: the composer (`NSTextView` in an `NSScrollView`, for trackpad scrolling of long drafts while unfocused, separate measurement layout, input-method composition, undo, spelling, custom paste and drop), the right-click menu (a hit-test-filtered `NSView` + `NSMenu` with custom emoji rows), the `@` menu and + menu (`NSMenu` for native keyboard navigation and type-to-select), the conversation dissolve (`NSHostingView` + `CATransition`), the composer padding click target, Quick Look (`QLPreviewPanel`), and the floating backdrop (`NSVisualEffectView`).

### 2.15 Composer

**Anatomy** (`ChatView.swift:189-306, 374-377, 408-484`): footer padding 12 pt horizontal, 11 pt bottom. A `VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 7)` holds the pending attachment strip (only when non-empty) above the control row. The control row is an `HStack(alignment: .bottom, spacing: 8)` inside a `GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 8)`:

| Part | Values |
|---|---|
| + button | 36 x 36, `plus` 15 pt medium, `.primary`, `.glassEffect(.regular.interactive(), in: Circle())`, help "Add Attachment"; opens the attachment menu |
| Field | `.glassEffect(.regular)` in a continuous rounded rectangle of radius 18 (= 36/2), min height 36; capsule at one line, rounded rectangle when taller |
| Editor | `NSTextView`, 14 pt system, `labelColor`, no insets, 12 pt leading padding, 6 pt vertical padding, trailing padding 27 + 14 + 31 = 72 pt (with mic) |
| Placeholder | "Message {title}" (e.g. "Message Chloe", "Message Launch week") in `placeholderTextColor`, drawn at the editor origin; when unavailable the reason replaces it |
| Mic | `mic` 16 pt in a 27 x 36 frame, help "Record Voice Message" plus shortcut (⇧⌘D) |
| Send, empty draft and no attachments | `arrow.up.circle` 22 pt `.tertiary`, not a button |
| Send, enabled | `arrow.up.circle.fill` 23 pt accent, 27 x 36, help "Send Message" |
| Mic-send spacing | 4 pt; 7 pt from the field's trailing edge |

**Growth:** the editor's height is measured on a separate layout manager sharing the text storage (so SwiftUI's speculative width probes never reflow the live editor), from `ceil(defaultLineHeight)` for 14 pt (17 pt), between 1 and 6 lines; an empty draft and a one-line draft are the same height so the transcript never jumps on the first keystroke (`ScrollableChatComposer.swift:142-205`, `CHANGELOG.md:1224`). Beyond six lines it scrolls with an auto-hiding overlay scroller and the caret is kept visible (`:96-102`). Max field height therefore about 6 x 17 + 12 = 114 pt (computed, inferred).

**Keys** (`ScrollableChatComposer.swift:123-138`, `ComposerNameCompletion.swift:62-70`): Return or Enter sends (unless input-method text is marked); Shift+Return and Option+Return insert a newline; Shift+Tab leaves the composer and focuses the selected sidebar row; Control+V pastes attachments. Writing Tools are disabled; spelling, grammar and autocorrection are on (`:159-178`).

**Paste** (`ScrollableChatComposer.swift:212-250`, `NoodleStore.swift:1633-1692`): attachments first: file URLs; PNG data ("Pasted Image.png"); TIFF ("Pasted Image.tiff"); then text longer than 1,200 characters or 12 lines becomes a "Pasted Text.txt" attachment and leaves the draft alone; otherwise text pastes as plain text (rich text is stripped). With focus elsewhere in the chat, ⌘V with files, images, PDFs, movies, audio or archives still attaches (`ChatView.swift:137-139`).

**Drop:** file URLs dropped on the editor attach; dropping anywhere on the window imports files, images, PDFs, movies, audio, archives, web URLs (downloaded) or raw data into the draft with the 2 pt accent ring (`ConversationWindow.swift:55-67`, `AttachmentTransfer.swift:40-60`).

**Focus:** clicks in the field's padding focus the editor (an `NSView` target that ignores the text area and the bottom-right 65 x 36 controls region, `ComposerFocusSurface.swift:42-56`). The composer focuses when a separate window opens or is raised, after a profile sheet closes, and after an annotation is saved; switching conversations swaps the draft and clears undo history (`ChatView.swift:149-157`, `ScrollableChatComposer.swift:48-63`). Focusing or typing marks the conversation read (`NoodleStore.swift:94-97`).

**Disabled states** (`NoodleStore.swift:652-661`, `ChatView.swift:274`): the whole row is disabled and the placeholder reads "This group is archived", "Every bot in this group is archived" or "{Name} is archived". The editor becomes non-editable and paste and drop are switched off.

**Drafts:** text and pending attachments are kept per conversation for the app session and cleared on send; an attachments-only send gets the body "Sent {n} attachment(s)" (`NoodleStore.swift:1452-1480`).

**Pending attachment strip** (`ChatView.swift:383-406, 625-687`): horizontal scroll without indicators, chips spaced 7, leading inset 44 (36 + 8, aligned with the field). Chip: height 28, max width 260, caption font (10 pt), `glassEffect(.regular, in: Capsule())`, 9 pt leading and 5 pt trailing padding; type symbol in system blue in a 14 pt slot (`photo.fill`, `doc.richtext.fill`, `waveform`, `film.fill`, `doc.fill`, `text.bubble.fill` for annotations, `globe`, `desktopcomputer`), the filename or the annotation's comment on one line, then `xmark.circle.fill` (secondary, help "Remove Attachment"). Clicking previews; the chip can be dragged out.

**Voice recording** replaces the field (not the + button) with a 36 pt glass row of radius 18: discard (`xmark`, Escape, "Discard Recording (Escape)"), a 6 pt red dot, a live waveform 22 pt tall (2.5 pt bars every 5 pt), elapsed time, stop (`stop.fill`), send (`arrow.up.circle.fill` 23 pt blue, Return, "Send Voice Message (Return)"), with "Finishing transcription…", "Reconnecting microphone…", "No sound from {mic}" and "Retry Transcription" / "Send Audio Only" states (`VoiceMessageComposer.swift:26-94`).

### 2.16 @ name completion

**Trigger** (`AgentNameCompletion.swift:8-27`): no selection, and the nearest `@` before the caret is at the start or follows whitespace or one of `( [ { , :`; the query is at most 64 characters of letters, digits, space, apostrophe, hyphen, underscore or period, with no newline. The replaced range runs from `@` through any letters, digits, `-` or `_` right after the caret.

**Menu** (`ComposerNameCompletion.swift:84-189`): a native `NSMenu`, scheduled on the next run loop after each edit or selection change; minimum width 360 with descriptions, 220 without; positioned with its bottom 4 pt above the `@` glyph, left-aligned to it (AppKit keeps it on screen). Entries: bots whose name contains the query (case-insensitive), the conversation's participants first, then by name in Finder order; in groups a separator splits members from other bots; then, after a separator, people the bots are shared with on a Noodle Hub (`person.crop.circle`). Bot items show a 16 pt avatar image and "{Name}  {description}" with the description in secondary colour, whitespace collapsed and cut at 72 characters + "…" (full description in the tooltip); Settings > Conversation can hide descriptions ("Show descriptions in the @ name menu"). It works in direct chats too.

**Selection:** Return or click inserts the plain name (no token, no styling) followed by a space if at the end of the text, as one undo step. Escape dismisses; the same request does not reopen until the query or range changes. Mentions are not a delivery primitive: bots see plain text (`AgentNameCompletion.swift:3`).

### 2.18 Chat effects

**Trigger and rules** (`ConversationEffects.swift:39-92`, `MessengerDocumentation.swift:118-127, 198-200`, `docs/chat-effects.md`): a bot runs `messenger --effect confetti|fireworks --conversation <uuid>`; confetti is for "an everyday win, such as a task finished or tests passing", fireworks for "a rare, major milestone, such as a release shipped". An effect is not a message: it does not wake bots, mark unread or reorder chats. It must come from a participant, at most one per conversation every 2 s, and expires 30 s after queuing. The queue keeps at most 32 events from the last 5 minutes.

**Playback** (`ConversationEffectsView.swift:34-84`): an overlay over the whole chat (clipped, not hit-testable, hidden from accessibility). While the chat is visible (app active, window visible, key, not minimised, no sheet) it polls every 250 ms and atomically claims the newest live effect, consuming all others so reopening never replays. It plays for 4 s, then clears; switching conversations stops it. A development-only Conversation > Play Effect menu previews each kind (`ConversationCommands.swift:120-130`). Reduce Motion replaces either effect with a still badge: the glyph 🎉 or 🎆 at 40 pt with 12 pt padding in a `regularMaterial` circle, centred.

**Confetti** (`:112-144`), 60 fps `TimelineView` + `Canvas`, deterministic from the effect ID: 120 pieces in pink, orange, yellow, mint, cyan, purple; even pieces launch from the left edge, odd from the right, at 72% height; start stagger up to 0.45 s; velocity x (0.18 to 0.63) x width inward, y -(0.48 to 0.84) x height; gravity term 0.35 x height x t²; life 3.8 s, fading over the last 0.8 s; spin (3 to 11) rad/s; each piece a rounded rectangle (radius 1) 5 to 10 wide and 6 x flutter tall, flutter = 0.3 + 0.7 x |cos(7t + 6 x phase)|.

**Fireworks** (`:146-226`): 8 rockets launched evenly over 1.8 s, additive blending (`plusLighter`). Each rises 0.7 s from the bottom edge (x at 15% to 85%) to an apex at 14% to 44% height with ease-out `1 - (1 - p)^2.2` and a 10-dot trail (radius 2.2 shrinking 0.18 per dot, warm white hue 0.11, saturation 0.5). The burst flashes a white radial gradient of radius 30 + 500t for 0.18 s, then 64 sparks per rocket at random angles: reach = min(width, height) x (0.20 to 0.34), distance = reach x speed (0.35 to 1.0) x (1 - e^(-3.2t)), plus 0.07 x height x t² drop; life 1.4 s x (0.7 to 1.0); fade 1 - (t/life)³; flicker after 60% of life at 0.55 + 0.45 sin(40t + i); every 7th spark white, the rest the rocket's hue ± 0.04 at saturation 0.85; drawn as 5 tapering streak segments of 0.035 s each, width (3.4 - 0.55k) x (0.6 + 0.4 x speed), round caps.

### 3.1 Component boundaries

```

  <Wallpaper/>                       // fixed, inset-0, behind both columns; crossfade
  <HeaderShade/>                     // absolute top-0 h-16 full width, pointer-events-none
  <Sidebar/>
  <ConversationPane conversationId>  // keyed transition surface (3.13)
    <ChatVeil/>                      // bg token, see 3.3
    <Transcript>                     // scroller, masked top fade; virtualised rows (3.4)
      <ConversationStart/>           // hero, only when the oldest message is loaded
      <LoadEarlierSentinel/>
      <MessageRow message/>          // memoised by id + revision; NOT subscribed to the draft
        <BotAvatarButton/> <Segments/> <LinkPreviewCard/> <AttachmentGroup/> <DeliveryLabel/>
        <ReactionBadges/>            // absolutely positioned on the first bubble
        <MessageContextMenu/>        // Radix ContextMenu wrapping each bubble/attachment
      <BottomSpacer height={composerHeight + 20}/>
    </Transcript>
    <Composer/>                      // absolute bottom; reports its height via ResizeObserver
      <PendingAttachmentStrip/> <PlusMenu/> <ComposerField/> <MentionMenu/> <VoiceRecorder/>
    <EffectsCanvas/>                 // absolute inset-0, pointer-events-none
    <DropRing/>
```

Keep the draft in a store slice that only `<Composer>` subscribes to (the user's codebase rule: slice selectors, never whole-store reads), so typing never re-renders rows; Noodle proves this with a render probe test, and the web equivalent is React Profiler showing zero `MessageRow` commits while typing.

### 3.2 State

```ts
type Author = { kind: 'user' } | { kind: 'agent'; agentId: string } | { kind: 'system' };
type Delivery = 'queued' | 'delivered' | 'failed';           // labels: Sent, Delivered, Not delivered
type Reaction = { id: string; author: Author; emoji: string; createdAt: string };
type Message = { id: string; conversationId: string; author: Author; body: string;
  createdAt: string; delivery: Delivery; attachmentIds?: string[]; reactions?: Reaction[] };
type Viewport = { isAtBottom: boolean; messageId?: string; offset: number };   // persisted per conversation
type Draft = { text: string; attachments: PendingAttachment[] };              // per conversation, session-scoped
type TranscriptLocal = { firstShownId?: string; followsLatest: boolean;
  userScrolling: boolean; userHasScrolled: boolean; restored: boolean };
type Effect = { id: string; conversationId: string; kind: 'confetti' | 'fireworks'; expiresAt: string };
```

Messages should arrive by push (WebSocket event per message and per reaction change) rather than Noodle's 1 s file poll.

.dark {
  --accent: #0a84ff; --bubble-in: #333333; --bubble-in-ink: #ffffff;            /* white 0.20 */
  --chat-veil: color-mix(in srgb, #1e1e1e 28%, transparent);
  --delivery-ink: color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 25%, transparent);
}
[data-wallpaper] {                     /* also force the .dark token set, as Noodle forces dark */
  --bubble-in: color-mix(in srgb, #000000 22%, transparent);
  --bubble-out: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 28%, transparent);
  --bubble-material: blur(20px) saturate(160%);   /* ultraThinMaterial approximation (inferred) */
}
```

### 3.4 Transcript scrolling and virtualisation

Mirror Noodle's bounded model rather than an infinite virtual list: render the newest 100 messages (or from the saved reading message), and prepend 100 when a top sentinel intersects (`IntersectionObserver`). Give each row `content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: auto 72px` so off-screen rows skip layout and paint while staying in the DOM (find-in-page and selection keep working). If conversations reach thousands of rows, `react-virtuoso` (`firstItemIndex` for prepends, `followOutput`, `atBottomStateChange`) is the closest off-the-shelf match; TanStack Virtual needs manual prepend anchoring.

Rules to port exactly:

1. `isAtBottom = scrollHeight - clientHeight <= 2 || scrollTop >= scrollHeight - clientHeight - 2`.
2. Track `userScrolling` from `wheel`, `touchstart`/`touchmove`, `pointerdown` on the scrollbar and keyboard scrolling; end it on `scrollend` (with a 150 ms debounce fallback where `scrollend` is missing). On end: `followsLatest = isAtBottom`; save `{isAtBottom, messageId: topVisibleRowId, offset}`.
3. On a new last message: if `author.kind === 'user'`, set `followsLatest = true`; then if following and not `userScrolling`, scroll the bottom spacer into view (`block: 'end'`).
4. On prepend: capture `scrollHeight` and `scrollTop` in `useLayoutEffect` before and after, then restore `scrollTop += newHeight - oldHeight` (do not rely on `overflow-anchor`, whose Safari support is uncertain; inferred). Never let content growth while reading change what is at the top.
5. On container resize (`ResizeObserver` on the scroller only, never on content): if following, pin to the bottom; else scroll the saved top message back to the top edge.
6. On open: after the first layout, scroll to the bottom or to the saved `messageId` with `block: 'start'`; fall back to the bottom if that message is gone.
7. Bottom spacer height `composerHeight + 20`; scrollbar margin via `scroll-padding-bottom` or by sizing the scroller's padding.
8. Top fade: `mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent 0, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.12) 28.8px, #000 64px);` on the scroller (64 px band, 45% stop). Bottom soft edge (Noodle's `.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.soft)`): a pseudo-element strip of height `composerHeight + 16px` with `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)` masked from opaque at the bottom to transparent at the top (inferred approximation).
9. Add what Noodle lacks: a "Jump to latest" pill when not following and a message arrives (see section 4).

### 3.5 Row and bubble CSS

```css
.msg-list { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--chat-row-gap);
  padding: var(--chat-top-pad) var(--chat-gutter-x) 0; }
.msg-row  { padding-top: var(--chat-row-clear); display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: var(--avatar-gap); }
.msg-row[data-author=user] { justify-content: flex-end; padding-left: var(--bubble-side-min); }
.msg-row[data-author=agent] { padding-right: var(--bubble-side-min); }
.msg-content { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--content-gap); min-width: 0; }
.msg-row[data-author=user] .msg-content { align-items: flex-end; }
.bubble { position: relative; border-radius: var(--bubble-radius);
  padding: var(--bubble-pad-y) var(--bubble-pad-x);
  font: 400 var(--bubble-font)/var(--bubble-line) system-ui, -apple-system, "SF Pro Text", sans-serif;
  white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; user-select: text; }
.bubble[data-author=user]  { background: var(--bubble-out); color: var(--bubble-out-ink); }
.bubble[data-author=agent] { background: var(--bubble-in);  color: var(--bubble-in-ink); }
[data-wallpaper] .bubble { backdrop-filter: var(--bubble-material); }
.bubble.long { display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 8; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden; }
.delivery { font-size: 9.5px; color: var(--delivery-ink); padding-right: 5px; }
.system-notice { margin-inline: 80px; align-self: center; padding: 7px 12px; border-radius: 14px;
  font: 500 11.5px/1.3 system-ui; /* + person.2.fill equivalent (lucide Users) */ }
```

`white-space: pre-wrap` reproduces "inline-only, preserving whitespace". For Markdown, parse inline syntax only (for example `marked.parseInline` or `markdown-it` with block rules disabled) and sanitise links to `http`, `https`, `mailto`; split tables out first with a port of `MessageSegment.split` (fence-aware, header/alignment count match). Whether to go further and render real lists and headings is a product decision: Noodle deliberately keeps agent prose looking like chat.

The 12.5 px message size is small for the web; keep the ratios (14 px composer, 12.5 px body, 9.5 px status) but consider scaling the set to 14/15.5/11 if readability tests demand it.

### 3.6 Reactions

- Badge row: `position: absolute; top: -12px; right: -5px; display: flex;` children `margin-left: -6px` (first excluded); wrap into a grid (`grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(48px, 1fr)); gap: 4px; max-width: 280px`) when the row would overflow the bubble width.
- Badge: `min-width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 9999px; padding-inline: 7px` (only when counted); emoji 14 px; count 10 px/500; `background: linear-gradient(var(--reaction-mine), var(--reaction-mine)), var(--window-bg); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--reaction-ring)` with `--reaction-ring` = text background at 85%.
- Badge click: shadcn `Popover` (260 px, padding 20, gap 16) with the 26 px emoji, names, and, when one is yours, "Change Reaction…" (6-column grid of 36 px cells, gap 10) and "Remove My Reaction".
- Reserve the 12 px clearance on every row (3.5) so reactions never move rows.
- Accessibility gap in Noodle: reacting needs a right-click. On the web, also expose React through keyboard (Shift+F10 / ContextMenu key opens the Radix menu on a focused bubble) and a hover/focus-visible "Add reaction" button; Radix `ContextMenu` already opens on long-press for touch.

### 3.7 Context menu

shadcn `ContextMenu` around each bubble and each attachment. First item: a non-menuitem group rendering two rows of six 38 x 36 emoji buttons (22 px glyph, 8 px radius selected background `--reaction-mine`, `transform: scale(1.12)` on hover with `transition: transform 180ms ease-in-out`, disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`); then "More Emoji…" opening an emoji-picker popover anchored to the bubble; then the table in 2.12 with lucide icons (Copy, Table, Download, AlignLeft, Eye, FolderOpen, Image, CircleUser, Laptop, MonitorPlay, Smile). "Use as Background" and "Use as Icon" go through shadcn `AlertDialog` with the same titles and messages. Copy should copy the right-clicked segment rather than the whole body (Noodle copies the whole raw body, a small pitfall).

### 3.8 Composer

- Layout: `fixed`/`absolute` bottom, `padding: 0 12px 11px`; row `display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: 8px`; + button 36 px circle; field `min-height: 36px; border-radius: 18px` with glass: `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--surface) 55%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(24px) saturate(180%); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--glass-edge), 0 1px 3px var(--glass-shadow)` (Liquid Glass approximation, inferred).
- Editor: `<textarea rows=1>` 14 px / 17 px, padding `6px 72px 6px 12px` (72 = send 27 + 14 + mic 31). Auto-size by setting `height = clamp(17, scrollHeight - 12, 6 x 17) + 12` (or `field-sizing: content` plus `max-height`, where supported); empty and one-line drafts must be the same height.
- Keys: Enter sends unless `e.shiftKey || e.altKey || e.nativeEvent.isComposing || e.keyCode === 229`; Shift+Tab focuses the sidebar row; while the mention menu is open, Up/Down/Enter/Tab/Escape go to the menu.
- Send control: outline arrow-up circle at 22 px in tertiary ink when the draft is blank and has no attachments (not focusable), filled 23 px accent otherwise (`aria-label="Send message"`).
- Paste: `onPaste` takes `clipboardData.files` as attachments; text over 1,200 characters or 12 lines becomes `new File([text], 'Pasted Text.txt', { type: 'text/plain' })` and leaves the draft alone; other text falls through as plain text.
- Drop: a window-level dropzone (`dragenter`/`dragover` with `dataTransfer.types.includes('Files')`) shows the ring (`inset: 5px; border: 2px solid var(--accent); border-radius: 15px`), and drops add to the pending strip, never send.
- Pending strip: `overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none; gap: 7px; padding-left: 44px`; chips `height: 28px; max-width: 260px; padding: 0 5px 0 9px; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 10px` (consider 11 to 12 px on the web).
- Disabled: `disabled` on the whole row, with the reason as placeholder.
- Draft persistence: per conversation in memory (Noodle keeps drafts for the session only); `localStorage` is acceptable for unsent text as a per-viewer convenience.
- Focus on open, after closing a dialog opened from the chat, and after saving an annotation; mark read on focus and on input.

### 3.9 @ mention completion

Port `AgentNameCompletion.request` verbatim (preceding character must be start, whitespace or `([{,:`; query at most 64 of `[\p{L}\p{N} '\-_.]`; replacement extends over trailing `[\p{L}\p{N}\-_]`). Render a shadcn `Command` inside a Radix `Popover` anchored to a virtual element at the `@` glyph (compute with a mirror div of the textarea), placed above with a 4 px gap, min width 360 (descriptions on) or 220. Rows: 16 px avatar, name, then the description in muted ink cut at 72 characters + "…"; participants first, a separator before other bots in groups, then a separator and people. Insert plain text plus a trailing space at the end; treat it as one undo step (`document.execCommand('insertText')` keeps native undo in a textarea; inferred browser behaviour). Remember a dismissed request until the query or range changes.

### 3.10 Attachments and previews

- Wrap layout: `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; justify-content: flex-end` for user rows. Image previews are sized before load from server-provided width and height: `scale = min(300 / w, 240 / h)`, `width = max(120, w x scale)`, `height = max(120, h x scale)`, `aspect-ratio` set, `border-radius: 13px`, placeholder tint black 12%, `loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"`, thumbnails at 2x (max 1,040 px).
- Stack mode: absolute positioning per the plan in 2.17 (advance `min(72, 0.42 w)`, stagger 12, width capped 220).
- Selection: `transform: scale(1.01); box-shadow: 0 0 7px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent); transition: 120ms ease-out`. Click opens; Space opens the focused one; ⌘/⌥/⇧-click opens the raw file in a new tab.
- Preview: a Radix `Dialog` lightbox paging (Left/Right) through the message's plain files only; Escape closes.
- Drag out: `draggable` with `DownloadURL` (`{mime}:{filename}:{absoluteUrl}`, Chromium) and `text/uri-list`. Because the codebase requires a pointer-operable non-drag equivalent for any functional drag, keep "Save…" and "Copy" in the context menu as that path, sharing one helper.

### 3.11 Link previews

Unfurl on the server (Open Graph / oEmbed), never from the browser: only `http(s)` URLs up to 2,048 characters, no userinfo, and hosts that pass a port of `isPublicHost` (plus DNS-resolution checks against private ranges, which Noodle does not need because it never fetches server-side). Cache results 7 days, failures briefly; return `{ title, site, imageUrl }` with the image resized to 560 x 316. On the client, request only after the card has been 300 ms in view (`IntersectionObserver` + timer), keep a 10 s overall deadline, show the 280 x 220 card from 2.11 with a spinner, and fall back to a link icon. Skip the preview when an attachment already carries the same URL.

### 3.12 Effects

Port both canvases to a single `<canvas>` overlay (`position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none`) driven by `requestAnimationFrame` for 4,000 ms, scaled by `devicePixelRatio`, with `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'` for fireworks. Seed a small PRNG (for example mulberry32) from the effect ID so every viewer sees the same show. Play only when `document.visibilityState === 'visible' && document.hasFocus()`, the conversation is open and no modal is up; dedupe by effect ID, drop after `expiresAt` (30 s), enforce the 2 s per-conversation rate limit on the server. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, show the still badge (40 px glyph, 12 px padding, material circle, centred) for the same 4 s.

### 3.13 Transitions

Use the View Transitions API for the 160 ms conversation dissolve, which cross-fades rendered snapshots the way Noodle's `CATransition` does (no fade to blank): set `view-transition-name: transcript` on the pane, call `document.startViewTransition(() => flushSync(() => select(id)))` (React's `<ViewTransition>` is an alternative where available; inferred), and style `::view-transition-old(transcript), ::view-transition-new(transcript) { animation-duration: 160ms; animation-timing-function: ease-out; }`. Skip when reduced motion is requested or during window resizes. Wallpaper: preload with `img.decode()` (or the video poster), then cross-fade two stacked layers over 350 ms ease-in-out; when switching to a wallpapered conversation, switch the token set to dark in the same transition.

### 3.14 Sound, read state and status

Play the received sound only when the tab is focused and no system notification is shown; otherwise let the Notification API carry it (browsers need a prior user gesture to unlock audio). Mark read on focus, pointer, key and scroll input inside the pane and on composer focus or input. Status dot: draw the avatar with a CSS mask that cuts the ring (`mask: radial-gradient(circle at calc(100% - var(--dot)/2) calc(100% - var(--dot)/2), transparent calc(var(--dot)/2 + var(--ring)), #000 calc(var(--dot)/2 + var(--ring) + 0.5px))`) and place the coloured dot over it (20/7/1.5 px in a title, 42/10/2 px in a list).

## 4. Patterns worth copying, and pitfalls to avoid

**Copy:**

1. Reserve the reaction overhang on every row (12 px = row gap 10 + 2) so reacting never moves the transcript.
2. Size every media preview from metadata before it loads; load only what is visible, after a short dwell.
3. Keep the draft out of the transcript's render path; prove it with a render count.
4. Anchor scrolling by message identity; never feed geometry back into scroll commands; save the reading position only at gesture end, on hide and on quit.
5. Open long conversations on the newest page and pin the first shown row so new messages extend rather than shift the list.
6. Meaningful delivery states: Sent until an agent actually fetches the message, then Delivered.
7. Long pastes become a "Pasted Text.txt" attachment; long messages clamp to 8 lines with a reader.
8. Tables as their own sortable, foldable bubble with CSV copy and save; numeric columns right-aligned automatically.
9. Effects as an ephemeral, rate-limited, expiring side channel that never creates a message, plays once, only in the foreground, with a still Reduce Motion fallback.
10. Make the whole surface dark while a wallpaper is set, add a 25% scrim, a 28% veil, and translucent bubbles; crossfade wallpapers only after decoding.
11. One click selects and opens an attachment; Space opens the selected one; modifier keys bypass the previewer.
12. Composer heights identical for empty and one-line drafts; six-line cap; Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks; IME-safe.
13. Link previews only for public hosts, with failures cached so redraws never retry.

**Avoid (or improve on):**

1. Files-only messages on the Mac show a synthetic "Sent 2 attachments" text bubble above the files; the iOS client hides it (`Chats.swift:2065-2069`). Hide synthetic bodies.
2. The Mac shows "Delivered" under every user message; iOS shows it only under the latest and under failures. Prefer iOS.
3. The Mac shows an avatar on every bot message and no names in groups, so a run of one bot's messages is visually noisy and speakers are identified only by face. Use the iOS run rules: name above the first message of a run, avatar beside the last, a spacer on the others.
4. No timestamps or day separators anywhere in the transcript; add hover or focus timestamps and day dividers.
5. No in-transcript working indicator for agents that may work for minutes; at least mirror the status dot in the header and consider a "{Name} is working…" row driven by agent status (and, where agents stream, a streaming bubble).
6. No jump-to-latest affordance or unread divider when scrolled up.
7. Copy on a table or a segment copies the whole raw message body.
8. No maximum bubble width: on wide windows bubbles span `W - 193` (about 730 px in the screenshot); cap prose at roughly 680 to 720 px for readability.
9. Reactions are reachable only by right-click (no keyboard path, no hover button).
10. Row insertion transitions are declared but effectively disabled; if the web adds them, keep them off the virtualised list's measurement path and respect reduced motion.
11. Message text at 12.5 px and chips at 10 px are below typical web body sizes.

## 5. Open questions and inferences

- The exact look of `ultraThinMaterial`, `regularMaterial` and Liquid Glass (`.glassEffect(.regular)`) cannot be read from code; the CSS blur and tint values in 3.3 and 3.8 are approximations, as are the macOS semantic colour values (`windowBackgroundColor`, `textBackgroundColor`, tertiary and placeholder label colours).
- The screenshots appear to use the Graphite accent and an older build (sliders toolbar glyph, reaction on the image); the code values were preferred wherever they disagree.
- Whether row insertion ever animates: the transcript strips animations and no update is animated, so rows most likely appear instantly (inferred).
- Inline code and link styling inside bubbles follow SwiftUI `Text` defaults (monospaced code, accent links); not verified in a screenshot.
- The composer's maximum height (about 114 pt) is computed from a 17 pt line for 14 pt SF, not measured.
- The + menu's on-screen position depends on AppKit's placement of `popUp(positioning:at:in:)` near the window bottom (anchored 5 pt from the button's top-left corner); exact placement unverified.
- `.saved` and `.failed` delivery states appear to be legacy or scenario-only on the Mac; whether a Hub path still produces them was not traced.
- The measured gap between a text bubble and its image in the Chloe screenshot (about 6 pt) differs from the code's 3 pt; likely transparent padding inside the image asset or an older build (inferred).

doc:docs-internal/research/noodle/analys.content:
# Noodle rich media around chat: voice messages, voice calls, annotations, screen capture and noodlets

Noodle (macOS app 0.50.0) keeps five rich-media features inside the conversation instead of in separate screens. **Voice messages** replace the composer pill with a recording bar (live scrolling waveform, on-device transcription) and are sent as an audio attachment that carries its own transcript, duration and 100-point waveform. **Voice calls** (Codex bots only) run over WebRTC in a hidden web view, are controlled from the window toolbar, and leave a "Voice call with X" card plus compact transcript blocks interleaved with whatever was typed during the call. **Annotations** are started only from the keyboard or menu bar (⇧⌘A for selected text, ⇧⌘R for a region) on conversation text, a frozen picture of the conversation window, attachment and web-link previews, live captures, Hub live views and noodlets. Each is saved as a durable draft attachment, either plain text or a PNG with an orange mark, plus structured metadata, and goes out with the next message. **Screen capture** is a floating panel with a thumbnail picker, a 10 fps live preview and freeze-and-annotate. **Noodlets** are small HTML apps that bots build in the Noodle Applet companion and share as `noodlet://UUID` link cards that open live. None of the repo's screenshots shows recording, a call, an annotation editor or the capture panel, so their appearance below comes from code. Only the noodlet card and the composer microphone button appear in screenshots.

Permalink base for every citation: https://github.com/pdparchitect/noodle/blob/702339e3153025c9fe9582783caff7a19b48ff97/

## 1. Scope

**Read in full** (`Sources/Noodle/` unless noted):

| File | Lines | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `VoiceRecorder.swift` | 477 | Recorder phases, capture, metering, transcription, draft persistence, audio sink |
| `VoiceMessageComposer.swift` | 139 | Recording bar that replaces the composer |
| `VoiceMessagePlayer.swift` | 229 | Live and saved waveforms, playback model, in-chat player, transcript sheet |
| `VoiceCaptureRecovery.swift` | 162 | Microphone start verification, Core Audio deadline queue |
| `VoiceInputDevice.swift` | 91 | Microphone enumeration and selection |
| `VoiceCall.swift` + `Sources/NoodleCore/VoiceCall.swift` | 352 + 120 | Call routing, controller, WebRTC media, voice previews; call data model, bot instructions, harness voices |
| `VoiceCallToolbar.swift` | 217 | Toolbar control, timer, call card, transcript blocks, placement |
| `AnnotationPopover.swift`, `AnnotationPreview.swift`, `AnnotationContent.swift`, `AnnotationCommands.swift` | 370, 246, 79, 14 | Region canvas, comment popover, review window, marked-PNG export, command state |
| `ConversationAnnotation.swift`, `ConversationAnnotationContent.swift` | 321, 32 | Conversation text and window-region annotation, save transaction |
| `NoodletAnnotation.swift`, `NoodletAttachmentCard.swift` | 168, 73 | In-place noodlet annotation, noodlet card |
| `ScreenCapturePreview.swift`, `ScreenCaptureModel.swift`, `CaptureAttachment.swift`, `ScreenCaptureService.swift` | 456, 193, 44, 318 | Capture panel, picker, live preview, canvas, phases, saving, ScreenCaptureKit service |
| `AttachmentPreviewController.swift` | 751 | Quick Look owner, attachment and link annotation, comment save and dismissal |
| `Sources/NoodleCore/AttachmentAnnotation.swift`, `VoiceMessage.swift`, `KeyboardShortcuts.swift` | 89, 25, 157 | Annotation data shape, voice metadata, default shortcuts |
| `Shared/HubLink/Sources/HubLink/LinkCall.swift` | 232 | The WebRTC call page (JavaScript), call wire types |
| `ConversationEffectsView.swift` | 237 | Chat effects (adjacent, section 2.6) |
| Docs: `docs/voice-messages.md`, `docs/attachment-annotations.md`, `docs/chat-effects.md`, `docs/usage.md` (relevant parts), `Applet/README.md` | | Behaviour as documented |

**Consulted for specific facts:** `ChatView.swift` (composer, mic button, chips, capture entry), `ComposerAttachmentMenu.swift`, `Components.swift` (bubble integration), `MessageContextMenu.swift`, `AttachmentPreview.swift` (cards, Shared popover, companion opening), `ConversationCommands.swift`, `KeyboardBindings.swift`, `NoodleStore.swift` (send, save, call routing), `WorkspaceRepository.swift` (call card record), `HubSurfaceWindow.swift`, `LongMessageText.swift`, `NoodleSettingsView.swift`, `PermissionsSettingsView.swift`, `AgentConfigurationFields.swift` (voice chooser), `NoodleApp.swift`, `ConversationWindow.swift`, `Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/AgentActivityWindow.swift` (`AnnotationPreviewFrame`), `Applet/Protocol/Sources/AppletBridge/{NoodletLink,BuildIdentity,Protocol}.swift`, `Applet/Protocol/Sources/NoodletFormat/Manifest.swift`, `Sources/NoodleCore/MessengerDocumentation.swift`, `CHANGELOG.md`. `Support/VoicePreviews/` was listed (contents in 2.4). Mobile counterparts, for comparison only: `Mobile/Sources/NoodleMobile/{VoiceMessages,Calls,Noodlets}.swift`, `Chats.swift` (placement lines).

**Screenshots viewed:**

| Screenshot | Relevant content |
|---|---|
| `docs/images/games-mac.png` | A noodlet card in a group chat: black thumbnail centred in the card, "Bubble Buddies" bold title, "Noodlet · Click to open" caption, near-invisible card fill over the wallpaper. Cropped and enlarged to confirm. |
| `.github/readme/hero.png`, `website/assets/screenshot-chloe.png`, `screenshot-group-chat.png` | Composer at rest: glass "+" circle, input pill with `mic` glyph left of the send circle. No recording or call state. |
| `website/assets/screenshot-harness.png` | Settings tab bar (General, Conversation, Harness, ...), which confirms the microphone picker sits under **Conversation**. |
| `.github/readme/applets.png`, `website/assets/screenshot-applet.png`, `docs/images/games-iphone.png`, `.github/readme/mobile.png` | Noodlets running in Noodle Applet and on iPhone (context only). |

Font note: SwiftUI text styles on macOS resolve (per Apple's HIG, not the repo) to `.caption` 10 pt, `.callout` 12 pt, `.body` 13 pt, `.headline` 13 pt bold, `.title3` 15 pt. Explicit `.system(size:)` values are quoted as written. 1 pt = 1 CSS px at 1x.

## 2. Findings

### 2.1 Noodlets

**What a noodlet is.** "Each one is a noodlet: a small creation your bots write and you open like an app. In Finder a noodlet looks like a single document" (`Applet/README.md:3-5`). On disk it is a package folder with the extension `.noodlet` (`.noodlet-dev` for development builds) containing a `noodlet.json` manifest (`Applet/Protocol/Sources/AppletBridge/BuildIdentity.swift:16-19`, `Sources/NoodleRuntime/NoodletPreviewAccess.swift:15-18`). Manifest fields: `version`, `title`, `runtime` (default `"html"`), `entry` (default `"index.html"`), `summary`, `symbol`, `window`, `permissions` (`microphone`, `camera`, `speech-recognition`, `screen-capture`, `local-network`), `category` (games, productivity, utilities, developer, data, creativity, media, writing, learning, lifestyle), `controls` (gamepad keys), `layout` (desktop, phone, adaptive), `runs` (device, hub), `theme`, `display` (browser, standalone, fullscreen), `orientation`, `backgroundColor` (hex only) (`Applet/Protocol/Sources/NoodletFormat/Manifest.swift:4-28, 58-69`). Today they are HTML only ("Bots no longer write noodlets in Swift", `CHANGELOG.md:226`). Games are noodlets too (`docs/gaming.md:22-23`).

**How one is created.** The person never creates one in Noodle. A bot builds it with its applet tool ("Build, run, inspect, interact with, capture and share HTML noodlets in Noodle Applet: small utilities, games, interactive websites, prototypes, examples and demos", `Applet/Protocol/Sources/AppletBridge/AppletGuidance.swift:7`), receives `url` = `noodlet://<uuid>`, and posts it with `messenger --send --attach noodlet://UUID` (`Sources/NoodleCore/MessengerDocumentation.swift:177, 244`). The attachment stores `url`, `originalFilename` "Noodlet.webloc" and no `card` (`MessengerDocumentation.swift:227-236`). It points at the package on this Mac rather than copying it, so deleting the package makes the card "Noodlet unavailable". Links are validated strictly: only `scheme://<lowercase uuid>` with no user, port, path, query or fragment, scheme `noodlet`, `noodlet-dev` or `noodlet-local` (`NoodletLink.swift:12-26`). A tool may ask Noodle to post one with media type `application/vnd.noodle.noodlet-link` (`NoodletLink.swift:4-5`).

**Card anatomy** (`NoodletAttachmentCard.swift:15-42`, confirmed in `games-mac.png`):

| Part | Spec |
|---|---|
| Container | VStack, leading, spacing 10; padding 12; idealWidth and maxWidth 304; fill `.quaternary` at 35% in RoundedRectangle radius 13 (`:16, :27-29`) |
| Thumbnail | Full width, height 150, `scaledToFit`, so it is letterboxed, never cropped (`:17-22`) |
| Placeholder | `square.grid.2x2` at 42 pt, secondary, while loading; `questionmark.square.dashed` when unavailable (`:19-20`) |
| Title | `.headline`, 1 line; "Noodlet" until the real title loads (`:11, :23`) |
| Caption | "Noodlet · Click to open" or "Noodlet unavailable", `.caption`, secondary (`:24-25`) |
| Selection | Shared attachment behaviour: scale 1.01 and an accent glow (accent at 55%, radius 7), easeOut 0.12 s; hit shape RoundedRectangle 13 (`AttachmentPreview.swift:267-273`) |
| Tooltip | "Click or press Space to open in Noodle Applet" (`AttachmentPreview.swift:308-313`) |

Loading starts only when the card scrolls into view (`.task(id: shouldLoad)`). Noodle asks Applet for the preview image (PNG of 4 MiB or less), else reads `preview.png` from the package, else asks Quick Look for a 560×300 thumbnail (`NoodletAttachmentCard.swift:50-61`, `NoodletPreviewAccess.swift:17`). Results are cached per URL so the Shared popover matches the card, and at most two preview requests run at once, the rest queued ("leave room for bots", `NoodletAttachmentCard.swift:44-47, 63-72`).

**Opening.** A click or Space calls `showPreview`, which sends companion links to `store.openCompanion` instead of Quick Look (`ChatView.swift:308-319`).
- A **local** noodlet opens live in Noodle Applet with full interaction and saved data, or Applet brings its existing window forward. Noodle passes along the person's current Annotate Region and Add Annotation bindings (`AttachmentPreview.swift:83-101`). Failures land in the app's error display.
- A **Hub** noodlet opens in a floating panel, 1100×760 (min 480×340), in the dark preview frame with kind label "Noodlet" and close hint "Close Noodlet (⌘W)". A link-style header button ("Run on Hub" or "Run on This Mac", 11 pt medium) switches where it runs, and Noodle remembers the choice per noodlet (`HubSurfaceWindow.swift:34-62, 156-212`). A Hub noodlet that declares the microphone, camera or local network asks once with an Allow alert (`HubSurfaceWindow.swift:281-288`). Its context menu adds "Open on This Mac" (`laptopcomputer`) and "Open on Hub" (`play.display`) (`MessageContextMenu.swift:61-62`; `Components.swift:424-429`).
- Noodlets, browsers, computers, voice messages and annotations never join Quick Look's paging gallery (`AttachmentPreview.swift:27-28`). In Stack layout they sit side by side above stacked files (`CHANGELOG.md:216`).

**Shared popover.** A toolbar button `Label("Shared", systemImage: "square.stack")` (help "Shared Computers, Browsers and Noodlets") appears once anything has been shared. It opens a popover 340 wide and `min(count × 70 + 12, 460)` tall. Rows are 70 tall: an 84×54 preview (radius 6, continuous), a title of up to 2 lines, and a caption with the kind ("Noodlet", "Browser", "Computer") or "Noodlet unavailable". Hover shows a primary-8% fill at radius 8. Rows are newest first, one per companion (`AttachmentPreview.swift:53-57, 105-205`).

**Annotating a noodlet in place** (`NoodletAnnotation.swift`). Opening passes an `AppletAnnotation` {Noodle's bundle id, notification name, region and selection shortcuts with modifier bits command 1, shift 2, option 4, control 8} (`Applet/Protocol/Sources/AppletBridge/Protocol.swift:32-60`; `NoodletAnnotation.swift:53-63`). When the person presses either shortcut in the Applet window, Applet posts the distributed notification `<bundle id>.annotate-noodlet.region` or `.selection` with the session id. Noodle accepts it only for sessions it opened (`:22-24, 41-51, 62`). For a region, Noodle requests a screenshot artifact and reads it in chunks. For a selection, it evaluates `return { selection: String(getSelection() ?? ''), text: (document.body?.innerText ?? '').slice(0, 200000) };` in the page (`:81-108`). An empty selection or an off-screen noodlet beeps (`:70-78`). Noodle then lays a borderless floating window carrying the picture exactly over the page, adds a "shield" window at black 1% alpha over the rest of the Applet window ("All but invisible, as clicks go through what is fully clear"), activates itself, and runs the standard annotation editor. When the editor closes, it removes the overlay and re-activates the previously frontmost app (`:115-162`). Sources are named "Noodlet — <title>.png" or ".txt" (`:140-145`), and only one capture runs at a time (`:30, :66-68`).

**Mobile** runs noodlets on the phone or streams them from the Hub, with TV and game-controller modes, and has no annotation (`Mobile/Sources/NoodleMobile/Noodlets.swift:49-238`).

### 2.2 Annotations

**What can be annotated:**

| Surface | Text (⇧⌘A) | Region (⇧⌘R) | Source saved with the note | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Conversation transcript (main, separate and floating windows) | Selected text inside one message | Frozen picture of the whole Noodle window, marked inside its content area | "Message — <title>.txt" (`Conversation: <uuid>\nMessage: <uuid>\n\n<body>`) or "Conversation — <title>.png" | `ConversationAnnotation.swift:217-312` |
| "Read more" message reader popover | Yes | Yes (its window) | Same | `LongMessageText.swift:64-115` |
| Attachment in Noodle's Quick Look preview | Selected text, captured by copy; images start region selection; no selection means "Whole attachment" | Frozen capture of the preview window | None: the attachment already exists | `AttachmentPreviewController.swift:449-590` |
| Web link previewed in Quick Look | Yes | Yes | Link source, saved only together with the note | `AttachmentPreviewController.swift:184-201`; `CHANGELOG.md:287` |
| Live screen or window capture | Both shortcuts freeze the frame | Yes, with an inline comment editor | "Capture — <title>.png" | `ScreenCapturePreview.swift:148-160` |
| Hub live view (browser, computer) or Hub noodlet panel | Conversation controller | Yes | "Live View — …" or "Noodlet — <title>.png" | `HubSurfaceWindow.swift:47-51` |
| Noodlet open in Applet | Selected page text | Screenshot laid over the page | "Noodlet — <title>.txt" or ".png" | `NoodletAnnotation.swift` |

Not annotatable: a message without a text selection (there is no whole-message note), voice messages, and annotations themselves (they open in their own review window, `AttachmentPreviewController.swift:170-176`).

**Entry is keyboard-only, plus the menu bar.** Default bindings: "Add Annotation" ⇧⌘A, "Annotate Region" ⇧⌘R, "Save Annotation Comment" ⌘↩. All can be remapped in Settings → Keybindings (`Sources/NoodleCore/KeyboardShortcuts.swift:60-107`). Labels render modifiers in the order ⌃⌥⇧⌘ (`:19-31`), so the UI reads "⇧⌘A" even though the docs write ⌘⇧A. The Conversation menu has "Add Annotation…" and "Annotate Region…", enabled only while the key chat can annotate (`ConversationCommands.swift:104-109`). Nothing on screen offers an annotate button: the Preview menu was removed (`CHANGELOG.md:942`), and so were the Annotate buttons on Hub live views, Hub noodlets and the capture picker (`CHANGELOG.md:59`). `docs/attachment-annotations.md:22` still mentions "Preview → Add Annotation", which is stale. Key repeats never re-trigger a shortcut.

**Gating** (`ConversationAnnotation.swift:156-164`): the window is visible and key, with no visible key child window such as a popover. There must be a conversation and a save handler, no operation in flight, no pending note, no modal window and no sheet. A local monitor sees keyDown and leftMouseDown. Mouse-down records which message's passive marker view lies under the pointer, which is how the source message is identified even when quotes repeat. Escape cancels while busy (`:85-104, 143-146, 194-215`). Switching conversation, closing the window, or moving or resizing it during a region gesture cancels (`ChatView.swift:140-148`; `ConversationAnnotation.swift:175-192`).

**Text flow** (`ConversationAnnotation.swift:217-268`). It requires a recorded message in this conversation, and the first responder must not be an editable text view, so the composer never triggers it. Otherwise the system beeps. Noodle snapshots every pasteboard item and type, sends `copy:` through the responder chain, polls `changeCount` every 25 ms up to 20 times (500 ms), reads the string, and restores the original pasteboard. The quote must be non-blank and contained in that message's rendered Markdown text, or Noodle beeps. In Quick Look the same technique fails with "The clipboard changed while preparing the selection. Try adding the annotation again." (`AttachmentPreviewController.swift:500-548, 597`).

**Region flow** (`ConversationAnnotation.swift:270-312`, `AnnotationPopover.swift:6-47, 235-351`). ScreenCaptureKit's `SCShareableContent.currentProcess` captures Noodle's own window at backing scale, with no cursor, no shadow and no child windows. No Screen Recording permission is needed (`docs/attachment-annotations.md:51-52`). If the window frame changed meanwhile, the gesture is abandoned. Errors show the alert "Conversation couldn’t be captured". The frozen image is drawn at the window's own coordinates and clipped to the content area, so the window appears to stop in place while its toolbar and rounded silhouette stay real (`AnnotationPopover.swift:8-15`). The canvas:
- shows a crosshair cursor, repaired every run-loop turn because Quick Look fights over it (`:199-233, 303-312`), swallows scroll so the selection cannot drift (`:300`), and accepts the first click (`:248`);
- has a hint pill: HUD material, radius 15, height 30, width = text + 26, text "Drag to select · Esc to cancel" at 12 pt medium. It sits 16 pt right of and 14 pt below the pointer, flips to the left or above near edges, keeps 8 pt margins, hides once dragging starts, and never takes hits (`:252-263, 287-299, 353-356`);
- in a conversation, dims everything outside the selection with black at 15% (even-odd fill). Quick Look previews are not dimmed (`:315-320`);
- draws the selection with systemOrange at 14% fill and a 3 pt systemOrange stroke (`:321-324`);
- clamps the drag to the canvas. On mouse-up, anything smaller than 4×4 becomes a 16×16 marker centred on the mouse-down point ("click a point"). The rectangle is normalised to fractions of the image rect with a bottom-left origin, and the comment popover opens at the mouse-up point (`:326-349`).

**Comment popover** (`AnnotationPopover.swift:49-136`, AppKit `NSPopover`):

| Reference box | Height 60, radius 10, fill = label colour at 4.5%, insets 11; line 1 at 12 pt medium, up to 2 lines, tail-truncated: the quote (newlines turned into spaces), "Selected image region", or "Whole attachment · no selected text"; line 2 is the source filename at 11 pt, secondary (`:90-104`; `AttachmentPreviewController.swift:546`) |
