# Noodle companion apps, Surface and website: UI analysis

Noodle ships four companion Mac apps that give agents somewhere to work: **Computer** (Linux VMs, and an experimental "Local Mac" account), **Browser** (signed-in WebKit browsers), **Applet** (runs the small HTML apps, "noodlets", that bots build) and **Hub** (a menu-bar server that lends harnesses to invited people). All four follow one strict family template. Computer, Browser and Applet each have a single library window built as a `NavigationSplitView` over a wallpaper with native sidebar glass; Computer and Browser list their items as 42 pt gradient icons carrying a status dot, and Applet shows a card grid. Computer's and Browser's detail content sits in an inset rounded panel whose bottom edge is aligned with the floating sidebar, they share a sheet header (Cancel, title, primary action), and each adds an optional menu bar extra and a tabbed Settings window ending in an Update tab. Companions reach the chat through one mechanism: a *companion link* (a custom URL naming a browser tab, a computer or a noodlet) plus a *LinkCard* holding a title, a detail line and a picture taken when the link was shared. Cards never show live state. Clicking a card opens the live resource in its companion app. For a Hub conversation, it opens a dark floating live-view panel streamed as H.264 by the shared **Surface** layer. Surface also defines a manifest-declared gamepad (up to two pads, eight buttons and a menu key) that each viewer maps to a hardware controller or draws as on-screen controls. The marketing website is one static Apple-style page with no build step. It defines 8 CSS colour tokens (6 of them redefined for dark mode) plus two font stacks and a wrap width, uses apple.com's type scale and breakpoints, stages product shots on a launch photograph, and writes the wordmark on with an animation that matches the apps' first-run screen.

## 1. Scope

Permalink base for every citation below: https://github.com/pdparchitect/noodle/blob/702339e3153025c9fe9582783caff7a19b48ff97/ (citations are repo-relative `path:line`).

**Files read in full.** These cover the companion apps and Surface, the main app's companion integration, the website, and the docs and Mobile files consulted:
- `Computer/README.md`, `Browser/README.md`, `Applet/README.md`, `Hub/README.md`, `docs/gaming.md`, `website/README.md`.
- Computer: `NoodleComputerApp.swift`, `ComputerAppearanceView.swift`, `ComputerFilesView.swift`, `ComputerFileSearchField.swift`, `ComputerTerminal.swift`, `LocalMacView.swift`, `LocalMacWindowPreview.swift`, `ComputerPreviewSnapshot.swift`, `StorageView.swift`, `ComputerMenu.swift`, `ComputerLibraryWindow.swift`, `ComputerImageUpdateButton.swift`, `DestructiveActionButton.swift`, `ComputerDesktop.swift` (protocol skimmed), `ComputerStore.swift` (phases), `ComputerUpdater.swift` (settings), `ComputerFileIcons.swift` (grid), `ComputerCore/ComputerAppearance.swift`, `ComputerCore/Resources/container-registry.json`, `Computer/Bridge/.../ComputerLink.swift`.
- Browser: `BrowserApp.swift`, `BrowserViews.swift`, `BrowserLiveView.swift`, `BrowserPointer.swift`, `BrowserRecordsView.swift`, `BrowserProfileEditor.swift`, `BrowserBackgroundSheet.swift`, `BrowserIconView.swift`, `BrowserMenu.swift`, `BrowserSettingsView.swift`, `BrowserPresentation.swift`, `BrowserTab.swift` (surface, snapshot, input), `BrowserWebMCP.swift` with `Resources/WebMCP.js` (skimmed), `BrowserProtocol/.../BrowserReference.swift`.
- Applet: `App.swift`, `Library.swift`, `WindowPresentation.swift`, `NoodletCast.swift`, `AppletSettingsView.swift`, `AppletBackgroundSheet.swift`, `Permissions.swift`, `Recording.swift` and `Runtime.swift` (skimmed), `Protocol/.../NoodletFormat/Manifest.swift`, `WindowOptions.swift`, `NoodletRuntime/Bridge.js`, `Grants.swift`, `AppletBridge/AppletGuidance.swift`, `NoodletLink.swift`, the two bundled example noodlets.
- Hub: `App.swift`, `HubPairView.swift`, `HubSettings.swift`, `HubAccessSettings.swift`, `HubBotsSettings.swift`, `HubActivityView.swift`, `HubLinkSettings.swift`; `Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/HubInvitationSheet.swift`, `HubLinkRows.swift`; `Shared/Brand/.../WordmarkWelcome.swift`, `Wordmark.swift`.
- Shared: `Shared/Surface/Sources/Surface/SurfaceView.swift`, `Surface.swift`, `Gamepad.swift`, `HardwareGamepad.swift`, `SurfacePacket.swift`; `SurfaceStreamer.swift`, `SurfaceEncoder.swift` and `SurfaceFlow.swift` (constants only); `Shared/HubLink/.../LinkSurface.swift`; `Shared/Wallpaper/.../CompanionContentPanel.swift`, `ConversationWindowHeaderShade.swift`, `ConversationWindowCompositing.swift`, `IconAppearance.swift`, `IconEditorSheet.swift`; `Shared/SettingsUI/.../CompanionAppVisibility.swift`, `SheetSizing.swift`, `UpdateSettingsButton.swift`.
- Main app: `Sources/Noodle/BrowserController.swift`, `ComputerController.swift`, `HubSurfaceWindow.swift`, `CompanionAssignmentPicker.swift`, `MessageLinkPreview.swift`, `AttachmentPreview.swift`, `NoodletAttachmentCard.swift`, `CompanionAppCommands.swift`, `NoodletAnnotation.swift` (header), `AgentProfileSheet.swift` (actions); `Sources/NoodleCore/CompanionLink.swift`, `ToolHostServices.swift`; `Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/CompanionApp.swift`, `CompanionAppsSettingsView.swift`, `AgentActivityWindow.swift` (`AnnotationPreviewFrame`).
- Website: `website/index.html`, `styles.css`, `app.js` (read as data, never run), `oauth/client.json`, `oauth/callback/index.html`; symbol SVG headers; app icon SVG headers.
- Mobile (for the controller menu only): `Mobile/Sources/NoodleMobile/ExternalScreen.swift`.

**Screenshots viewed:** `website/assets/screenshot-computer.png`, `screenshot-browser.png`, `screenshot-applet.png`, `screenshot-hub.png`, `applet-castle-road.png`, `applet-molecule-bench.png`, `applet-tiny-empires.png`, `social-card.png`, `stage-launch.jpg`, `favicon.png`; `.github/readme/applets.png`; `docs/images/games-mac.png`, `games-iphone.png`, `games-tv.png`.

**Version drift between screenshots and code.** The Computer and Browser screenshots show a sliders glyph for Edit, where current code uses `ellipsis` (`NoodleComputerApp.swift:722`, `BrowserViews.swift:231`). The Browser screenshot also places Create and a gear in the detail toolbar, while the code puts Create in the sidebar column. The Hub screenshot shows six tabs and push buttons ("Invite…", "Remove…", "Add User"), while the code has ten tabs and link-style buttons. Where they differ, this document treats the code as current and the screenshots as the earlier look.

## 2. Shared app-family conventions

### 2.1 Process and window model

| Aspect | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Single copy | `AppInstance.claim()` runs before SwiftUI builds the app | `Computer/Sources/NoodleComputer/NoodleComputerApp.swift:12-17`, `Browser/Sources/NoodleBrowser/BrowserApp.swift:29-34` |
| Library window | one `Window(id: "library")`, min 850 x 580; default 1080 x 720 (Computer, Applet) or 1180 x 780 (Browser) | `NoodleComputerApp.swift:23-34`, `BrowserApp.swift:45-55`, `Applet/Sources/NoodleApplet/App.swift:23-45` |
| Quiet start | `.defaultLaunchBehavior(.suppressed)` and `.restorationBehavior(.disabled)`. Noodle starts companions with a background URL and keeps them hidden; the library opens only on a person's launch | `NoodleComputerApp.swift:28-33, 207-243` |
| Toolbar | `.windowToolbarStyle(.unified(showsTitle: false))`; toolbar background hidden so the wallpaper shows through | `NoodleComputerApp.swift:34, 507` |
| Close vs quit | Closing the window keeps everything running. Quitting Computer stops its computers, with a 10 s hard deadline. Hub asks before quitting | `NoodleComputerApp.swift:252-271`, `Hub/Sources/NoodleHub/App.swift:114-133` |
| Dock and menu bar | "Show in Dock" on by default, "Show in Menu Bar" off. With both off, an "App Settings" gear (`gearshape`) appears at the trailing end of the toolbar | `Shared/SettingsUI/Sources/NoodleSettingsUI/CompanionAppVisibility.swift:46-47, 88-100, 155-180` |
| Menu bar menu | "Open Library", the items (computers, browsers, or pinned then up to 8 recent noodlets), "Settings…" ⌘,, "Quit Noodle X" ⌘Q; icon is `AppSymbol.svg` as a 24 x 24 template image | `Computer/Sources/NoodleComputer/ComputerMenu.swift:14-22`, `Applet/.../App.swift:91-114`, `CompanionAppVisibility.swift:102-123` |
| App menu | "About Noodle X", "Check for Updates" (after Settings), Help → "Noodle X Help" opens the GitHub repo | `NoodleComputerApp.swift:35-47` |

### 2.2 Library window anatomy (Computer, Browser, Applet)

From back to front:
1. **Transparent window.** `isOpaque = false` with a clear background, so the wallpaper and the native sidebar glass composite in one window (`Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/NoodleWallpaper/ConversationWindowCompositing.swift:4-17`). The code never calls `.glassEffect`; the glass is the macOS 26 split-view sidebar.
2. **Wallpaper.** Computer and Browser show the selected item's own background; Applet has one library background (`App.swift:396-402`). It is the same `ConversationWallpaper` the main app uses for conversations: presets `sunset`, `ocean`, `forest` and `dusk` (`Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/NoodleWallpaperCore/ConversationBackground.swift:5-7`), or an image, animated HEIC or muted looping video (`Computer/README.md:84-86`).
3. **Header shade.** A 64 pt band under the toolbar. It is `.ultraThinMaterial` overlaid with a black gradient at 0.24 → 0.10 → 0 in dark mode or 0.06 → 0.03 → 0 in light (stops 0, 0.5, 1), masked black → black 88 % at 55 % → clear. Its shadow is black 24 %/6 % with radius 14 and y 5 (`ConversationWindowHeaderShade.swift:26-52`). Scrolling content is masked with `ConversationContentTopFade`, which runs clear → white 12 % at 45 % → white over 64 pt (lines 7-22); Applet's card grid uses it (`App.swift:391`).
4. **Sidebar.** A `.sidebar` List with its scroll background hidden and a tint of black 24 % (dark) or 4 % (light). `.searchable(placement: .sidebar, prompt: "Search")`, `.controlSize(.large)`. Column widths are min 280, ideal 326, max 380 for Computer and Browser, and 220/260/340 for Applet (`NoodleComputerApp.swift:459-464`, `App.swift:358-362`).
5. **Content panel.** The detail view is clipped to a continuous rounded rectangle of radius 12 (11 + 1, inset by 1). Padding is leading 12 (8 when the sidebar is collapsed), trailing 8, top 4 and bottom 7 (`CompanionContentPanel.swift:3-16`). A Computer smoke test fails if the panel's bottom edge differs from the native sidebar glass's bottom edge by 0.01 pt or more (`ComputerSmokeTest.swift:121-137`). Browser fills its panel with `textBackgroundColor` at 76 % (`BrowserViews.swift:206`). Computer's Files view uses the terminal background colour at the terminal's opacity (`ComputerFilesView.swift:118`). Applet has no panel: its cards float on the wallpaper.
6. **Toolbar order.** While the sidebar is shown, the sidebar column's own toolbar section holds a flexible spacer, "Hide Sidebar" (`sidebar.leading`), a fixed spacer, then the primary create action (`plus`: "Create", or "Open Noodlet" in Applet). When the sidebar hides, the system toggle returns and Create moves to `.navigation` in the window toolbar (`NoodleComputerApp.swift:470-486, 508-512`; `BrowserViews.swift:83-100`; `App.swift:462-497`). Sidebar visibility persists under `ComputerSidebarVisible`, `BrowserSidebarVisible` and `AppletSidebarVisible`.
7. **Hub grouping.** Items that Noodle Hub keeps for its bots appear in a separate "Hub" section, with one DisclosureGroup per person (labelled with the `person` symbol) and unowned items after them (`NoodleComputerApp.swift:445-457`, `BrowserViews.swift:60-72`). Applet makes Hub the first row of its Categories section (`App.swift:448-461`).

### 2.3 Sidebar row (Computer and Browser)

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Row | height 66; insets 2 top and bottom, 10 leading and trailing; bottom separator visible, tint primary 12 % | `NoodleComputerApp.swift:572-576` |
| Icon | `IconBadge` 42 pt | `:558` |
| Status dot | 10 pt circle at the icon's bottom-trailing corner, 2 pt stroke in `windowBackgroundColor`; tooltip shows the state | `:559-561` |
| Title / subtitle | system 13.5 semibold; system 12.5 secondary; one line each | `:564-566` |
| Extra line | Computer: "Upgrade available", 11.5 orange | `:567-569` |
| Dot colours | Computer: running green; starting, stopping, upgrading and setup orange; failed red; stopped gray. Browser: ready green, paused orange | `:614-621`, `BrowserViews.swift:163-165` |
| Subtitles | Computer: template name ("Desktop", "Shell", "Local Mac"). Browser: "1 tab", "N tabs" or "Agents paused" | `BrowserViews.swift:169` |

### 2.4 Icons

`IconBadge` is shared by bots, browsers and computers. It is a circle holding either a custom image (fill) or an SF Symbol on one of six top-leading → bottom-trailing gradients: 0 blue→cyan, 1 purple→pink, 2 orange→yellow, 3 mint→teal, 4 indigo→blue, 5 pink→orange. The symbol is white semibold at 38 % of the size; initials are 36 % rounded semibold. The shadow is black 20 %, radius 3, y 1 (`Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/NoodleWallpaper/IconAppearance.swift:24-71`). Bots store any integer seed modulo 6; browsers and computers store a clamped index, and a new browser takes `count % 6` (`Browser/Sources/NoodleBrowser/BrowserProfileEditor.swift:22-24`).
- **Editor sheet** (440 wide). Header Cancel / title / Done. A 104 pt preview. An "Image" group with "Choose Image…" (file or Photos, plus camera for people), Image Playground, and "Use Symbol Instead" / "Using Symbol". A "Colour" group of six 34 pt swatches with a white bold check on the selected one. A "Symbol" group in six columns of 42 pt tiles, radius 10: the selected tile is filled with the accent colour and shows a white glyph, the others use secondary 14 % (`IconEditorSheet.swift:36-137`).
- **Symbol set** for computers and browsers: `desktopcomputer`, `terminal`, `shippingbox`, `server.rack`, `laptopcomputer`, `globe`, `sparkles`, `bolt.fill`, `brain.head.profile`, `hammer.fill`, `paintbrush.fill`, `gearshape.2.fill` (`ComputerAppearanceView.swift:43-44`). Images are scaled to 512 px and stored as PNG of at most 2 MB; sources may be up to 50 MB (`IconAppearance.swift:94-146`).
- **Edit affordance.** A 64 pt icon carrying a 21 pt `pencil.circle.fill` (palette white on accent) at its bottom-trailing corner, on a background-coloured circle (`ComputerAppearanceView.swift:23-38`).

### 2.5 Sheets, groups and destructive actions

- **Header.** Cancel (plain button, blue, ⎋), title in `.headline` centred between spacers, and the primary action (plain, blue, ↩, secondary colour while disabled). Padding 20, then a Divider, then a body padded 20 or 24 with 16-20 pt vertical spacing (`NoodleComputerApp.swift:824-848`).
- **Groups.** `Color.secondary.opacity(0.075)` in a 12 pt rounded rectangle with 12 pt padding. Navigation rows ("Background & Terminal", "Background") are a label plus a `chevron.right` caption, padded 12, on `quaternary.opacity(0.3)` with radius 10 (`ComputerAppearanceView.swift:88-101`).
- **Widths.** Edit and new computer 580; New Local Mac, Background & Terminal and browser background 520; browser editor 480; icon editor 440; main-app New Computer / New Browser 420; bookmark editor 380; creation progress 520. Sheets resize to fit their content; with animation they stay attached at the top edge (`Shared/SettingsUI/Sources/NoodleSettingsUI/SheetSizing.swift:5-67`).
- **In-sheet destructive button.** An AppKit push button with `hasDestructiveAction`, `bezelColor = .systemRed`, `tintProminence = .secondary` and a capsule shape. The code explains that SwiftUI's bordered style drops Tahoe's subdued red outside alerts (`DestructiveActionButton.swift:4-25`).
- **Confirmations.** Always an alert with a Cancel role and a destructive verb, and a message that states the consequence (section 3.7).

### 2.6 Settings windows

A `TabView` whose tab switches animate with `.easeInOut(duration: 0.22)`. Panes are 580 wide (680 in Hub), `Form` style `.grouped`, and the window resize is anchored to the top. A badge counts available updates on the "Update" tab. The **Update** pane shows "Installed Version", an orange "Update available — x.y" caption, a button reading "Check for Updates" or "Install Update…", and two toggles: "Automatically check for updates" and "Automatically download and install updates" (`ComputerUpdater.swift:63-133`, `UpdateSettingsButton.swift:20-22`). **General** always begins with "Show in Dock" (help "Show the app in the Dock and app switcher.") and "Show in Menu Bar".

### 2.7 Naming, brand and voice

- **Names.** "Noodle Computer", "Noodle Browser", "Noodle Applet", "Noodle Hub", "Noodle Mobile"; development builds add "Dev". Created from a bot's editor, a resource is named for the bot, as in "Chloe’s Computer" (`Sources/Noodle/CompanionAssignmentPicker.swift:17-21`). Defaults are "My Desktop", "My Shell", "My Local Mac", "Browser" and "Browser 2".
- **App icons.** A slightly hand-drawn squircle tile in `#0088ff` with a cream glyph: Noodle `#fdf2d7`, Computer and Hub `#fcf7d9`, Browser `#fcfbd8`, Applet `#fdfbd6` (`Support/AppIcon.svg`, `Computer/Support/AppIcon.svg`; viewed in `website/assets/favicon.png`). The tile blue is also the website's `--blue`.
- **Voice.** Short plain sentences that state the consequence ("Closing the window leaves the computer running."). British spelling ("colour", "licence"). Typographic quotes and apostrophes, and "…" on commands that open a dialog. States are plain words: "Ready", "Agents paused", "Needs attention", "Unavailable".

## 3. Noodle Computer

### 3.1 Anatomy

The sidebar section is "Computers", plus "Hub" when relevant. The Create menu (`plus`, help "Create Computer") offers "New Linux Container" (`desktopcomputer`, ⌘N) and "New Local Mac" (`person.crop.rectangle`) (`NoodleComputerApp.swift:432-440`). The empty detail reads **"Your own computers."** with `desktopcomputer` and "Create a computer to get started." (`:492-499`). The row context menu offers Edit Computer… (`slider.horizontal.3`), Change Background… (`photo`), Upgrade (`arrow.down.circle`, containers only), Start/Stop, and Delete Computer (`:580-595`).

The **detail toolbar** (`.primaryAction`, `:717-767`) holds:
- "Edit Computer" (`ellipsis`).
- A power button: `power` when running (Stop, with confirmation) or `play.fill` (Start). While busy it shows a mini spinner; a hidden `slider.horizontal.3` label keeps its width fixed (`:788-804`).
- A segmented "Computer View" picker of symbols only: `desktopcomputer`, `terminal`, `folder` (Desktop, Terminal, Files). A Shell computer offers only Terminal and Files. The picker is disabled unless the computer is running.
- For Local Mac, "Focus Window" (`macwindow.on.rectangle`) and "Open All Windows" (`rectangle.on.rectangle.angled`) (`LocalMacWindowPreview.swift:13-31`).

The screenshot shows the Local Mac desktop letterboxed on black inside the rounded panel, under a glass toolbar of grouped capsules.

| Phase | Label | Dot | Detail placeholder text |
|---|---|---|---|
| stopped | Stopped | gray | Shell: "Start this computer to open its terminal." Desktop: "Start this computer to open its screen." |
| starting | Starting… | orange | the label as the title; Shell: "Opening the terminal…" |
| running | Running | green | Desktop before the first frame: "Connecting to the desktop…" |
| stopping | Stopping… | orange | the label |
| updating | Upgrading… | orange | 240 pt progress bar, "Upgrading the computer image…", Cancel |
| setupRequired | Approval required / Setup required | orange | `lock.shield` with a setup action button |
| failed | Needs attention | red | the failure message |

Sources: `Computer/Sources/NoodleComputer/ComputerStore.swift:8-32`, `NoodleComputerApp.swift:633-708`.

### 3.2 Desktop, Terminal and Files

- **Desktop.** A `VZVirtualMachineView` showing the guest at a fixed 1920 x 1200 unless "Resize desktop with window" is on (`ComputerDesktop.swift:13`, `NoodleComputerApp.swift:973-993`). ⌘C/⌘V move text through the desktop helper and nothing is shared automatically; the guest sees the Mac clipboard only when someone pastes (`:995-1041`). The Local Mac view letterboxes on black, applies a 12 px Gaussian blur during a live window resize and fades back to sharp over 0.25 s (`LocalMacView.swift:254-269`). Before the first picture it overlays "Waiting for desktop…" or the issue text with a "Settings…" button; after that, issues show in a bottom bar with "Settings…" or "Dismiss" (`:84-115`).
- **Terminal.** SwiftTerm in the monospaced system font at 13 pt, inset 12 pt on every side, painted on one background layer. The default is white on black at 100 % opacity (`ComputerTerminal.swift:22, 172-188`; `ComputerCore/ComputerAppearance.swift:15-17`). On reconnect it prints "[Shell exited. Opening a new shell…]". The context menu adds "Interrupt Command" (⌃C) and "Clear Terminal" (⌘K): Clear Terminal clears scrollback but keeps the current input and leaves a full-screen app's screen alone (`ComputerTerminal.swift:49, 72-132`). | Action | Alert title | Message (verbatim) | Destructive button |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stop | Stop My Desktop? | This will end the computer’s running processes. Unsaved work may be lost. | Stop / Force Stop |
| Delete (container) | Move My Desktop to Trash? | The computer and its disks will be moved to the Trash. | Move to Trash |
| Delete (Local Mac) | Delete X and its account? | This permanently deletes the managed account and its home directory. Stop preserves them; Delete removes them. | Delete Account |
| Upgrade | Upgrade X? | Download the current image and keep your files and local changes. Files you changed take precedence over files in the new image. A running computer will stop during the upgrade and restart afterward. | Upgrade (default) |
| Clean caches | Remove the previewed caches and restart running computers? | Running computers will stop and restart. Unsaved work may be lost. Removed caches can be downloaded again. Computer disks and recovery copies will be preserved. | Clean Caches and Restart |

Sources: `NoodleComputerApp.swift:604-607, 959-971`, `ComputerImageUpdateButton.swift:17-25`, `StorageView.swift:92-99`.

**Two techniques worth knowing.**
- **Desktop protocol.** A guest helper serves the X screen over vsock port 5100 and sends only the tiles that changed. A frame request returns width, height and a tile count, followed by x, y, w, h and raw BGRA rows for each tile; the client keeps the canvas. Input requests cover pointer, scroll, key (as X keysyms), text, paste (opcode 6) and copy (opcode 7), with a 1 MiB clipboard limit (`ComputerDesktop.swift:51-160`).
- **Card snapshots.** A computer shared into chat gets a best-effort snapshot. It retries every 250 ms for up to 8 s, and rejects a frame unless at least 1/300 of a 128 x 96 downsample (ignoring the top 14 px and the borders) differs from the median colour by 48 or more, so loading screens never become thumbnails. It encodes PNG at 1440, 1080 or 720 px if that fits 512,000 bytes, and falls back to JPEG at quality 0.92 or 0.85 (`ComputerPreviewSnapshot.swift:6-80`).

### 4.2 Agent presence and human-first rules

- **Agent pointer.** The agent's pointer is drawn as a cyan target that is not the system cursor. The colour is calibrated RGB (0.02, 0.78, 0.96), about `#05C7F5`. The marker is:
  - a 20 pt ring filled with cyan at 15 % (65 % while pressed), stroked 4 pt white under 2 pt cyan;
  - a 5 pt cyan dot at the centre;
  - a diamond with a 5 pt half-diagonal centred at (+14, +11), cyan with a 2 pt white outline;
  - a shadow of black 50 %, blur 4, offset 1 pt down.

  After a click the pressed look lingers for 180 ms. The overlay is never hit-tested or exposed to accessibility, and it is burned into screenshots (`BrowserPointer.swift:64-70, 101-145`).
- **Person first.** Any click, scroll or key from a person in a tab resets the agent's pointer (`BrowserTab.swift:51-65`). Pause Agents stops new agent actions but does not undo ones already done. Browsers start muted, and muting also pauses video. Camera and microphone requests are always denied (`BrowserTab.swift:210`). Bots cannot drag or right-click (`Browser/README.md:85-89`).
- **WebMCP.** The page runtime exposes `document.modelContext` (also `navigator.modelContext`) and declarative tools written as `<form toolname tooldescription>` with optional `toolparamdescription` and `toolautosubmit`. Without `toolautosubmit` the form is left filled in for the person to submit. A `Permissions-Policy: tools=…` header is honoured (`BrowserWebMCP.swift:5-40`, `Resources/WebMCP.js:166-196, 357-361`).
- **Live view for remote watchers.** The tab chrome is drawn into the video itself: the tab strip plus a 36 pt navigation row with back, forward and reload icons (13 pt medium in 28 x 26 boxes) and an address capsule 26 tall on primary 8 % with radius 7, showing an accent caret and a 1.5 pt accent border while editing. Clicks on that strip are hit-tested against a rendered layout; elsewhere they reach the page. Typing into the address follows the "first key replaces, Return goes, Escape leaves" rule (`BrowserLiveView.swift:8-75, 123-203`). The default page viewport is 1280 x 800 (`BrowserTab.swift:43`).

### 5.2 Noodlet package, manifest and windows

A noodlet is a folder `Name.noodlet` holding `noodlet.json` plus HTML, CSS, JS and assets; no build step. Bots create it in their own workspace, and Applet discovers it there and runs it in place (`Library.swift:37-55, 231-271`).

| Manifest key | Values and rules (`Applet/Protocol/Sources/NoodletFormat/Manifest.swift`) |
|---|---|
| version, title, runtime, entry | 1; title 1-200 characters; `"html"`; an `.html` file |
| summary, symbol | card text; SF Symbol name |
| category | games, productivity, utilities, developer, data, creativity, media, writing, learning, lifestyle (`:60-63`) |
| permissions | microphone, camera, speech-recognition, screen-capture, local-network; asked once per noodlet before it starts |
| layout | desktop (default), phone, adaptive (preferred) |
| runs | device or hub; a noodlet with any permission always runs on the device |
| theme | system, light, dark |
| display | browser (scrolls and zooms), standalone (fits its view; no scroll, zoom or selection), fullscreen (recommended for games and canvas) |
| orientation | any, portrait, landscape |
| backgroundColor | hex `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`, shown until the page paints |
| controls | gamepad declaration (section 8.2) |
| window.type | standard, floating (stays above), preview (non-activating HUD utility panel) |
| window.background | opaque, translucent (HUD material behind the window), transparent |
| window.titlebar | true, false (content under the title bar, buttons kept), or "none" (no buttons; draw your own) |
| window.cornerRadius | 0-100, only with `titlebar: "none"` |
| window sizes | 120-4096 points; default 900 x 620; `resizable` defaults to true, `rememberFrame` to false (`WindowOptions.swift:60-91`) |

Every validation error tells the bot what to use instead, for example "Unknown category X. Use games, productivity, …" (`Manifest.swift:131-160`).

Windows take the manifest title. When the title bar is hidden, a native drag strip 30 pt tall starts after the traffic lights (x = 78, or 28 for a preview panel, or 0 with `titlebar: "none"`) (`WindowPresentation.swift:85-95`). Pages mark drag regions with the CSS custom property `--noodle-app-region: drag` or `no-drag`; buttons, links, inputs and editable content stay interactive (`Bridge.js:20-31`). When a bot rebuilds a noodlet, the new window opens exactly over the old one "so nothing jumps or flashes", and it takes keyboard focus only if the person was working in it (`WindowPresentation.swift:6-24`).

**Play on a TV** (`NoodletCast.swift`). Casting moves the window to the chosen screen, lifts its size limits and enters full screen. A fixed-size window is placed on a black stage, scaled up as far as it fits and centred, and focus is restored afterwards. "Bring Back to This Mac" undoes all of it. Displays are added with "Add TV or Display", which opens the Displays settings.

### 5.3 The page API and the agent tool

Applet injects a frozen `window.noodle` object (`Applet/Protocol/Sources/NoodletRuntime/Bridge.js:78-96`):
- `version: 1` and `features`.
- `fetch`: native HTTP outside CORS; 16 MiB request and response, eight concurrent requests, 120 s total timeout.
- `data.read`, `data.write`, `data.list`: files of up to 16 MiB in the noodlet's own data folder.
- `storage.get`, `storage.set`, `storage.list`: named JSON values.
- `secrets.get`, `secrets.set`, `secrets.delete`, `secrets.names`: kept in the Keychain, per noodlet.
- `window.close()`, `minimize()`, `zoom()`, `toggleFullScreen()`.

The bridge also forwards `console.*`, uncaught errors and unhandled rejections to durable logs (`:2-19`). A `__noodletControl` hook gives agents inspect, click, type, key, scroll, drag and step; inspect returns the page text up to 20,000 characters and up to 500 targetable elements as CSS selectors (`:97-113`). Recordings run at 30 fps with 48 kHz audio; the bitrate is 0.4 bits per pixel per frame, clamped to 2-12 Mbps (`Recording.swift:22-24, 60-63`).

The guidance bots receive sets several product rules (`AppletBridge/AppletGuidance.swift`):
- "present" sets the preview; bots must "present once the noodlet shows something worth seeing, past any loading screen" (`:78`).
- "Only the user brings a noodlet to the foreground", so foreground mode is refused to bots (`:237`).
- Headless runs use test data and an optional test clock that steps requestAnimationFrame at 60 Hz (`:46-51`).
- Games must declare keys, because Noodle on iPhone does not pass controllers to the standard Gamepad API (`:196-199`).

While a person watches a noodlet live, every agent control operation fails with "A person is using this noodlet right now. Try again when they're done." (`Runtime.swift:453-456`). Permission prompts read "“Title” would like to use the microphone and the camera." with Allow and "Don’t Allow"; a refusal reads "Permission was not given to use …" (`Grants.swift:41-52`, `Permissions.swift:59-93`).

### 7.2 Links, cards and the trust model

`CompanionLink` has three kinds (`Sources/NoodleCore/CompanionLink.swift:8-40`):
- a browser: `noodlebrowser://<browser>?tab=<tab>`;
- a computer: `noodlecomputer://<computer>?terminal=<terminal>&view=terminal` or `view=web`;
- a noodlet: `<scheme>://<id>`.

UUIDs are lowercase. "It carries no credentials or authority; whoever opens it decides whether it may" (`ComputerLink.swift:3-5`). The chat stores what the card shows as a `LinkCard`: "its label and the last picture taken, never live state".

| LinkCard field | Rule |
|---|---|
| title | at most 300 characters; the page title (or browser name) or the computer name |
| detail | the last 2,000 characters: the page URL, or the terminal's last output |
| image | JPEG or PNG snapshot from share time, at most 550,000 bytes |
| symbol, colour, icon | the resource's icon appearance; icon at most 65,536 bytes |
| capturedAt | whole seconds |

When a bot posts, the host checks that the browser or computer is assigned to that bot; strips the browser's description and owner before the card enters the chat; refuses every other `application/vnd.noodle.*` type ("Tools cannot post this kind of attachment."); and posts the card in a message from the bot (`ToolHostServices.swift:16-41`, `BrowserReference.swift:18-25`).

### 7.4 Opening, live panels and feedback

- **Locally, opening hands the link to the companion.**
  - Browser shows that browser and its original tab, if the tab still exists.
  - Computer selects and starts the computer, then switches to Desktop for `view=web` or to Terminal. The person gets the computer's normal screen, not the agent's own session (`NoodleComputerApp.swift:156-177`, `Computer/README.md:35-38`).
  - Applet opens the live noodlet or brings its window forward.
- **In a Hub conversation, links open a floating live panel** (`HubSurfaceWindow.swift:20-101`). It is 1100 x 760 by default and at least 480 x 340, with no window buttons and a transparent title bar. Its frame (`AnnotationPreviewFrame`) is HUD material in dark appearance with continuous radius 18 and a 1 pt white 22 % border. The header is 36 tall and holds an 18 pt `xmark.circle.fill` at x 10, the title in 13 pt semibold, and a kind label in 11 pt medium secondary ("Live" or "Noodlet") 14 pt from the trailing edge. The content inset has radius 13 and sits 5 pt in from the sides and bottom (`Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/AgentActivityWindow.swift:302-360`). ⌘W and the close button end the view; Escape goes to the content. For a noodlet, a link button in the header switches between "Run on Hub" and "Run on This Mac", and the choice is remembered per noodlet (`HubSurfaceWindow.swift:158-212`). Failure texts are "Join that Noodle Hub again to open this." and "The Hub could not show this." While the view is open the bots wait (`LinkSurface.swift:26-29`).
- **Feedback loop.** In a noodlet opened from a conversation, Applet passes on the person's Annotate Region (⇧⌘R) and Add Annotation (⇧⌘A) shortcuts. Noodle then marks up a picture of the noodlet, or quotes the selected text, into that conversation's draft (`Sources/Noodle/NoodletAnnotation.swift:5-9`, `docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md:13-14`). This is how "say so while you play" works.

## 8. Surface and gamepad

### 8.1 Live view protocol

Surface is the shared live-view layer that Noodle, Mobile and Hub use to show a companion's screen remotely.
- **Inputs.** `pointer` (move, down, drag or up; x, y; clickCount), `scroll` (x, y, dx, dy), `key` (enter, tab, escape, backspace, space and the four arrows), `text`, and `hold(key, pressed)` for games (`Shared/Surface/Sources/Surface/Surface.swift:4-16`).
- **Viewer to source.** `input`, `view(width, height)` in device pixels ("so video is never sent larger"), `keyFrame`, `rate`, `shown(sequence)` and `recover` (`:18-36`).
- **Video.** H.264 High (auto level) in real-time mode. The streamer defaults to 60 fps and a maximum pixel size of 1600 (`maxPixelSize`). A picture unchanged for more than 6 frames is not re-encoded and is polled every 100 ms. Key frames are sent only on request. Packets are AVCC NAL units carrying SPS and PPS on key frames, in a binary frame starting with format byte 1 so they can never be mistaken for JSON events (`SurfaceEncoder.swift:46-49, 131-159`; `SurfaceStreamer.swift:48-51`; `SurfacePacket.swift:1-40`).
- **Flow control.** Bitrate drops to what the link drains as soon as frames queue. A viewer that is too far behind skips to the next key frame (`SurfaceFlow.swift:1-40`).
- **Viewer.** An `AVSampleBufferDisplayLayer`, aspect-fitted on black. Pointer positions map into surface points through the fitted rectangle. Mouse wheels without precise deltas are scaled by 10. When the decoder cannot continue it asks for a key frame by itself (`SurfaceView.swift:46-178`).
- **Touch on iPhone.** A tap clicks, a one-finger drag scrolls, a long press then drag moves a held pointer, and a pinch zooms up to 8x around the fingers; a keyboard button toggles typing (`Surface.swift:56-130`).

### 8.2 Gamepad declaration, mapping and on-screen controls

The manifest `controls` object holds `pads` (at most two; each with left, right, up and down keys and an optional `stick`), `buttons` (at most eight, most important first, optional labels of 1-12 characters) and a `menu` key. Keys must be a-z, 0-9, or one of left, right, up, down, space, enter, tab, escape and backspace, and each key may be used once. The guidance example is `{"pads":[{"left":"left","right":"right","up":"up","down":"down"}],"buttons":[{"key":"space","label":"Jump"},{"key":"z","label":"Fire"}],"menu":"escape"}` (`Gamepad.swift:6-102`, `AppletGuidance.swift:182-199`).
- **Hardware mapping.** The d-pad and left stick drive pad 0, and the right stick drives pad 1. Buttons are assigned in thumb order: A, B, X, Y, left and right shoulders, left and right triggers. The controller's Menu button sends the menu key. Anything without room goes on screen. Releases are sent before presses, so a thumb sliding across never holds opposite directions at once (`HardwareGamepad.swift:146-163`, `Gamepad.swift:106-163`).
- **On-screen layout** (`Gamepad.swift:168-263`).
  - Margin 16, spacing 12.
  - Pad size: min(width, height) x 0.36, clamped to 120-170. Button size: pad x 0.42, clamped to 52-72.
  - The first pad sits bottom-left with the 64 x 44 menu capsule above it; the second pad sits bottom-right.
  - Buttons fill a grid of at most three columns, ordered by distance from the right thumb. Two buttons side by side sit on a slant, the main one raised by 0.45 x the button size.
  - Pads read eight directions with a still centre whose radius is 25 % of the pad's; a pad that has only one axis ignores the other. A stick's knob travels up to 50 % of the radius.
- **Visuals** (`Gamepad.swift:357-452`).
  - Every control has a black 25 % backing so its white reads over light and dark pages.
  - Buttons: a white fill at 20 % (45 % pressed), a 1.5 pt white 40 % stroke, and a 13 pt semibold label.
  - The d-pad is a cross with arms one third of its width, filled white 18 % (28 % while held). Its chevrons sit at 0.68 of the radius, at 0.28 of the radius in size, and brighten from 60 % to 100 % while held.
  - The menu button is a capsule with `line.3.horizontal`.
  - Haptics: a selection tick when a pad takes a new direction; a medium impact when a button goes down and a light one when it comes up.
- **Controller menu.** The View button (Create on PlayStation, − on Switch) opens a TV overlay of black 55 % with a horizontal row of cards. Cards are 300 x 180 with radius 16 on white 12 %, spaced 28 apart, with 60 pt horizontal and 40 pt vertical padding. The chosen card gets a 4 pt white stroke, scale 1.08 and a semibold title; the others are at 70 % opacity, animated easeOut 0.15. The row lists the conversation's other games and ends with "Close Game". Left and right move, A chooses, and B or View resumes. Opening the menu releases any key held in the game (`Mobile/Sources/NoodleMobile/ExternalScreen.swift:159-287`, `ControllerMenuTests.swift:43-74`).
- **Focus.** On a Mac a controller plays only the game in the key window, and held keys are released when that window resigns key (`HardwareGamepad.swift:62-75`, `ControllerFocusTests.swift:7-38`).
- **What this gives agents.** A bot that declares keys gets a working controller on a Mac, on-screen controls on iPhone (`docs/images/games-iphone.png` shows a cross pad, a two-way pad, round labelled buttons and a menu capsule, with Done and controller/keyboard toggles at the top), and TV play. The bot can test without a person present through headless sessions, a test clock, screenshots and recordings, and it is locked out while a person plays (`docs/gaming.md:46-48, 117-131`).

Once they scroll above the nav, `.show-cta` fades in the logo and the Download pill: opacity 0 → 1 and translateY(−4px) → 0 over 0.35 s ease, with pointer events off while hidden. Without IntersectionObserver both are simply shown.
- **Wordmark writing** (`app.js:20-99`, the same paths as `Shared/Brand/Sources/NoodleBrand/Wordmark.swift:7-26`).
  - The SVG has `viewBox="0 119 3819 851"` and a 128-unit stroke with round caps and joins (`index.html:48-56`).
  - The script prepends a "swirl" path that rises from the top of the hero screenshot (or the bottom of the viewport, if nearer), curls once at radius 4 x pen with Bézier circle constant 0.5523, and runs into the "n".
  - All paths are drawn as one pen line using `stroke-dasharray` and `stroke-dashoffset`. The swirl's visible body is at most 0.6 of its own length, so its tail is gone before the pen finishes, and it fades in over the first 35 % of its length with smoothstep.
  - The swirl is drawn 1.6x faster, and the time saved comes off the 3.4 s total; the delay is 550 ms.
  - Easing is SwiftUI's easeInOut, `cubic-bezier(.42, 0, .58, 1)`, solved by 24 bisection steps.
  - The animation is skipped under reduced motion, or when the wordmark is not fully in view on load (for example, returning to the page scrolled down).
- **OAuth support.** `oauth/client.json` is a client-ID metadata document (`client_id` is its own URL; public client with `token_endpoint_auth_method: "none"`; redirects `/oauth/callback/`, `/dev/` and `/mobile/`). The callback page scrubs the query from history and forwards to `noodle://mcp/oauth/callback`. Its text: "Returning to Noodle…", "If Noodle didn't open, Open Noodle.", "Nothing to return to Noodle."

Explicit Copy and Paste buttons, because browser clipboard access needs a gesture |
| LinkCard | the same schema: title ≤300, detail ≤2,000 (tail), snapshot JPEG ≤550 KB taken at share time, symbol, colour, capturedAt. Clicking opens the live view. A terminal card without a picture renders its last lines in 9 px monospace, bottom-left aligned |
| Gamepad | the Web Gamepad API standard mapping: buttons 0-3 → declared buttons 1-4, 4-7 → buttons 5-8, 9 (Start) → menu key, 8 (Back/View) → the app's game menu; d-pad 12-15 and axes 0/1 → pad 0, axes 2/3 → pad 1; synthesise `keydown`/`keyup` into the iframe via `postMessage`, releases first; only the focused panel plays; release everything on `blur`. On-screen controls use the layout algorithm in section 8.2 with pointer events |
| Website | Tailwind v4 `@theme` with the 8 colour tokens, with dark values for the 6 that change; `--font-display`/`--font-sans` stacks; `max-w-[1080px] w-[calc(100%-44px)]`; breakpoints 734, 900 and 1068 as custom screens; stage utilities copied as values |

## 11. Patterns worth copying, and pitfalls to avoid

**Copy:**
1. One link-plus-snapshot type for every live resource, with a strict "never live state" rule. It makes chat history cheap, safe to share and stable.
2. Authority stays in the host, not in the card. A bot may post only resources assigned to it; descriptions and owners are stripped before posting; tools cannot mint the product's own card types.
3. The person comes first. A visible agent pointer, any human input resetting it, Pause Agents, browsers muted by default, agent operations refused while a person watches, and bots never allowed to bring a window to the front.
4. Make the bot do the presentation work. "present once the noodlet shows something worth seeing" and the snapshot usefulness heuristic both keep blank loading screens out of chat.
5. Manifest-declared controls rendered differently per viewer: hardware, on-screen, TV menu.
6. Errors and validation messages that say what to do instead ("Use games, productivity, …").
7. A family template enforced by shared components and smoke tests, for example the panel and glass edge alignment test.
8. Rebuild in place without flashing, taking focus only from a person already using it.
9. One brand stroke shared by the website and the apps' first run (the wordmark paths and timing are identical).

**Avoid:**
1. Do not copy `stage-launch.jpg`. It is a third-party launch photograph with a visible organisation's water tower, and its licence is not stated in the repo.
2. Below 900 px the site hides every nav link and offers no menu. A web product should keep a menu at phone widths.
3. `website/README.md` says five sections still show placeholders, but `index.html` has none, and the `.shot-img` styles go unused. Prune stale design debt.
4. Don't rely on the shots as specifications. As listed in section 1, the Computer, Browser and Hub screenshots predate the code.
5. The SwiftUI apps lean on system colours and materials. A web build must define explicit tokens for both themes, including translucent sidebar and HUD surfaces, or results will vary by browser.
6. Inverting monochrome raster symbols in dark mode via `filter: invert(1)` works only for pure black glyphs. Prefer `currentColor` SVG on the web.
7. iPhone games had to declare keys because controllers do not reach WebKit's Gamepad API in Noodle. A web product inside third-party iframes faces similar permission gaps (the `gamepad` permissions policy), so keep the key-based contract.

## 12. Open questions and inferences

- The SwiftUI system colours behind the six IconBadge gradients resolve at runtime; the hex values in section 10 are Apple's published values and may differ slightly on macOS 26 (inferred).
- `screenshot-applet.png` shows a purple pill at the top-left of a title-bar-less window. Its origin (a noodlet's own control or a system indicator) is not identified (inferred: part of the noodlet page).
- The Browser screenshot's toolbar order (Create and a gear beside Back and Forward) and the Hub screenshot's tab set come from an earlier build (inferred from the code differences in section 1).
- `games-tv.png` and the social card's staging appear to be produced marketing images rather than app captures (inferred).
- The exact wallpaper preset artwork (`sunset`, `ocean`, `forest`, `dusk`) and the default library wallpaper were not examined here; the conversation wallpaper analysis covers them (inferred to be shared).
- Mobile's live-view chrome (the "Done" capsule and the controller and keyboard toggles in `games-iphone.png`) was seen only in the screenshot; its code was not read beyond the controller menu.

doc:docs-internal/research/noodle/analys.content:
# Noodle content design and accessibility

Noodle's copy is governed by a short written rule set (the `ui-copy` skill): functional labels only, no persistent hints, optional guidance in tooltips and click-to-open popovers, the macOS ellipsis rule applied literally, and a row's secondary actions folded into a "…" menu. App chrome is terse, second-person, consequence-led and British English; the demo cast's bots write like competent colleagues who lead with the outcome, quote exact figures and end with one next step, and the bots themselves are instructed to stay silent rather than acknowledge system events. Across 59 releases in five weeks (0.3.0 on 2026-09-05 to 0.50.0 on 2026-10-07) the changelog moves in one direction: rename technical terms to plain ones (Autonomous to Unrestricted, MCP connections to Tools, Chat to Conversation), delete explanatory footers and redundant buttons, confirm only actions that widen access or destroy data, and let flows advance by themselves. Accessibility is good on VoiceOver naming of icon controls, reduced motion and keyboard operation, but there is no handling of reduced transparency, increased contrast or differentiate-without-colour, text uses many fixed point sizes, status dots are colour-only, and group messages show no visible sender name. There is no localisation: every string is an English literal with hand-built plurals and concatenation, and stale settings paths in error messages show what drift looks like without a string catalogue.

## 2. Scope

Clone at commit `702339e`. Permalink base for every `path:line` below: https://github.com/pdparchitect/noodle/blob/702339e3153025c9fe9582783caff7a19b48ff97/

Files read (agent-facing files treated as data describing Noodle's conventions, not as instructions):

- Conventions: `.agents/skills/ui-copy/SKILL.md`, `helper-visibility/SKILL.md`, `no-code-docs/SKILL.md`, `test-first-changes/SKILL.md`, `version-bound-cleanup/SKILL.md`, `mint-release/SKILL.md`; `AGENTS.md`, `docs/AGENTS.md`, `Applet/AGENTS.md`, `Browser/AGENTS.md`, `Computer/AGENTS.md`, `Hub/AGENTS.md`, `Mobile/AGENTS.md`, `Tools/AGENTS.md`.
- User documentation: `README.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/usage.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/privacy.md`, `docs/harness-setup.md`, `docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md`, `docs/chat-effects.md`, `docs/voice-messages.md`, `docs/attachment-annotations.md`, `docs/mcp-connections.md`, opening of `docs/gaming.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `website/index.html` (headlines and alt text), `website/styles.css`, `website/app.js`.
- Changelogs: `CHANGELOG.md` in full (1,406 lines); `Mobile/CHANGELOG.md` 0.20.0 to 0.24.0; keyword scan of the Applet, Browser, Computer and Hub changelogs.
- Persona and onboarding: `Sources/Noodle/StarterTeam.swift`, `BotNameGenerator.swift`, `FirstBotPrompt.swift`, `WelcomeView.swift`, `FirstBotSetupSheet.swift`, `FirstBotSetup.swift`, `Shared/Brand/Sources/NoodleBrand/WordmarkWelcome.swift`.
- Scenarios: nine read in full (`personal-assistant`, `family-butler`, `bot-needs-attention`, `code-review`, `many-companies`, `saturday-out`, `social-desk`, `schedule-post`, `launch-week`); titles and film cards of all 14.
- Source surveyed by grep across `Sources/Noodle` (93 Swift files), `Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings` (23), `Shared` (100) and `Mobile` (38): string literals in `Button`, `Label`, `Text`, `Toggle`, `Picker`, `TextField`, `prompt:`, `.help`, `.alert`, `.confirmationDialog`, `.navigationTitle`, `Section`, `ContentUnavailableView`, error assignments; every accessibility modifier; localisation APIs. Targeted reads of `SidebarView`, `Components` (`MessageBubble`), `ChatView`, `Overlays` (bot and group editors), `BotsSettingsView`, `NoodleSettingsView`, `ConversationCommands`, `NoodleApp`, `MessageContextMenu`, `ConversationEffectsView`, `AgentConfigurationFields` (effort control), `KeyboardShortcuts`, `KeyboardBindings`, `AgentRuntimeCoordinator` (kick requests), `MessengerDocumentation`, `AgentTips`, `ConversationName`, `Models`, `Harnesses`, `Support/Info.plist`, `Mobile/Project.swift`, `Tests/NoodleAppTests/HiddenViewTests.swift`.
- Images viewed: `Scenarios/cast/chloe.jpg`, `alfred.jpg`, `kai.jpg`, `sol.jpg`, `wren.jpg`; `website/assets/screenshot-chloe.png`, `screenshot-group-chat.png`, `screenshot-harness.png` (the last shows the pre-0.23.0 Settings with Heartbeat and Sandbox tabs and bordered "Sign In…" buttons, so it is historical, not current UI).

Counts below come from grep over string literals. Strings assembled from variables are missed, so counts are floors.

## 3. Findings

### 3.1 Voice and tone

Noodle writes in four registers. They share second person, plain words and no hype inside the product; they differ in length and warmth.

| Register | Where | Characteristics | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| App chrome | Labels, menus, settings, dialogs, errors | Functional, terse, states consequences and what is kept, uncontracted, no "we", no apology | "Saving restarts the bot. Its workspace and history stay unchanged." (`Sources/Noodle/Overlays.swift:398`) |
| Bot messages | Scenario cast, starter-team backstories | Outcome first, exact figures, one clause of reasoning, one next step, no emoji in body text | "Found it. The thumbnail cache is rebuilt on the main thread at every launch…" (`Scenarios/code-review/scenario.json:38`) |
| User docs | `docs/`, READMEs | Task-led headings, imperative, bold UI names, `→` paths, limits stated plainly, nothing about code | "Turning unrestricted access off does not undo completed actions, stop apps the bot left running, or revoke macOS privacy permissions." (`docs/security.md:84-86`) |
| Marketing | Website, film cards, README hero | Short declarative headlines ending in a full stop, contractions allowed | "Private by default." (`website/index.html:171`); "Signed in, so they don't have to ask." (`website/index.html:121`) |

Principles for app chrome, each verified in source:

1. **Say what the control does and nothing more.** The rule: "Keep visible copy focused on functional labels and necessary status or error messages. Do not add persistent instructional hints, shortcut legends, or explanatory footer text unless explicitly requested. Put optional guidance in tooltips or documentation." (`.agents/skills/ui-copy/SKILL.md:8-14`). When nothing is selected the detail pane is simply blank; there is no "Select a conversation" text (`Sources/Noodle/NoodleApp.swift:417-424`).
2. **State the consequence, especially what survives.** "{name} will start with a fresh context. Its workspace, memory and messages are kept." (New Session confirmation, `Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/ConversationRuntimeSettings.swift:64`); "Bots that use {harness} stop working until it is installed again. Your sign-in is kept." (`Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/HarnessSettingsView.swift:397`); "Off by default. Changing this restarts the bot. Turning it off keeps those services connected to your account." (`Sources/NoodleRuntimeSettings/BotsSettingsView.swift:367`).
3. **Second person, with Noodle named in the third person; never "we", never sorry.** A grep for we, our, sorry, oops and whoops in UI literals returns nothing. Noodle speaks of itself by name: "Noodle needs Screen Recording access to preview your screens and windows. Capture adds only the image you choose to your draft." and, in the docs, "Noodle never makes up an answer or consent." (`docs/security.md:92`).
4. **Uncontracted and calm.** About 238 literals use "cannot", "does not", "could not" and similar; about 15 contract, mostly device errors ("The microphone isn’t responding…", "Attachment action couldn’t be completed"). Status words are never alarmist: "Needs attention", "Sign-in required", "Checking…".
5. **British English, with slips.** "Colour" section headers in the icon editors, "cancelled", "recognise", "licence" on the website; but "You can customize it afterward." in the tool catalogue and "Model details and license on Hugging Face" as a tooltip, and the docs write "summarizes" (`docs/harness-setup.md:244`). Scenario copy is consistently British (£, "diary", "Mum", "half term", "organises").
6. **Exclamation marks are almost absent.** The only ones are the sample outgoing bubble "Looks good!" in the background editor preview (`Sources/Noodle/ConversationBackgroundView.swift:51`) and the starter-team greeting, which is written in the user's voice (`Sources/Noodle/StarterTeam.swift:18`).

Principles for user documentation, from the conventions files: documentation outside the code "is for people using the apps, not for people reading the code"; a README "says what the app is, what it does for the person using it, and how to get and use it, in plain language", with no type names, formats, protocols or design reasoning; "read every sentence as someone who has never seen the code. Delete any sentence they would not need or understand." (`.agents/skills/no-code-docs/SKILL.md:8-12, 27-28`). Guides "Document what people can do, how to do it, and the limits they will meet" and carry no work logs or audits (`docs/AGENTS.md:7-16`). Every user-visible change gets an Unreleased changelog entry in the same change (`AGENTS.md:11-15`), and on Mobile a "What to Test" list, which "is all TestFlight testers see" (`Mobile/AGENTS.md:10-11`). The resulting docs use task headings ("Give an agent a job", "Float a conversation over other apps", "See what your bots spend"), bold UI names and plain statements of limits. (`helper-visibility` governs Dock policy and `test-first-changes` requires tests that need no account, model, network or timing; neither is about copy, but the second explains why controls are found by accessibility name in tests, 3.7.)

Principles for bot messages, from the scenarios (these are demo data, but they define the voice the product presents as normal):

- **Lead with the result in one or two words, then detail.** "Done, and it is in the diary." "Sorted:" "Found it." "Booked: Roast, in the Floral Hall above the market, a table for five at 12:45." (`Scenarios/saturday-out/scenario.json:64`). "Up. I will watch it for an hour and tell you if the question changes again." (`Scenarios/social-desk/scenario.json:65`).
- **Exact figures with units and the comparison that matters.** "B is winning, and clearly: **9.4% against 5.9%**. With a thousand visitors on each side, that is not noise." (`Scenarios/launch-week/scenario.json:86`); "Sol has the running total: **£612 of the £900**." (`Scenarios/family-butler/scenario.json:45`).
- **Bold for the one thing to notice; numbered lists for options, each option a bold name plus one sentence.** Chloe's two gift ideas and three Sunday ideas (`Scenarios/personal-assistant/scenario.json:36, 72`).
- **End with one decision or commitment.** "Tell me which and I will block the morning so nothing lands on it." "Shall I?" "Shall I also keep a quiet list of what each person is hoping for, so nobody ends up with three scarves?" (`Scenarios/family-butler/scenario.json:89`).
- **Judgement and restraint are shown, not claimed.** Echo held a post because a competitor was mid-outage: "a line about staying up for weeks would have read as a dig at them while people were still waiting to get back in. I have rewritten it without the comparison and it is ready when you are." (`Scenarios/social-desk/scenario.json:40`). Kira: "I honestly do not know which wins, so let's find out." (`Scenarios/launch-week/scenario.json:40`).
- **Teammates are named, not "the other agent".** "Sol has the running total…", "Noted from Alfred: Secret Santa is six gifts at £25." (`Scenarios/family-butler/scenario.json:92`).
- **No emoji in message bodies.** Emoji appear only as reactions (🙌 🎄 🚀 🚢 🙏 👍 🎉 😍 👏).
- **Persona shows in acknowledgements only.** Canned `autoReplies` per character: Alfred "Very good. Consider it done.", Wren "Pushed. The suite is green.", Echo "Held. I will tell you what happens.", Clara "Scheduled." (`Scenarios/*/scenario.json`, `autoReplies` fields).

### 3.2 Glossary

| UI term | Meaning to the person | Internal name | Usage and examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bot | The AI worker the person creates and talks to | `AgentRecord`, `agents` (`Sources/NoodleCore/Models.swift:5`) | The managed object everywhere in chrome: "New Bot", "Edit Bot…", "Archive Bot", sidebar section "Bots" (`Sources/Noodle/SidebarView.swift:22`) |
| Agent | The generic idea of an AI worker | Same `AgentRecord`; code says agent throughout | Marketing and system-wide entry points: "Meet your AI team", "Send to Agent" (Spotlight, Shortcuts, Services; `Sources/Noodle/NoodleIntents.swift:63`, `Support/Info.plist:75`), toggles "Wake idle agents" and "Keep Mac awake while agents work", activity window label "Agent Activity" |
| Group | A shared conversation with several bots | `BotConversation` with `kind == .group` (`Models.swift:58-63`) | "New Group", "Edit Group…", "Group Info", "Archive Group", sidebar "Groups" |
| Conversation, chat | Any thread; a bot's direct thread is its "direct conversation" | `BotConversation`, kind `.direct` | Menu and settings tab "Conversation"; docs also say chat ("Switching chats keeps each chat's unsent draft", `docs/usage.md:109`) |
| Team | The starter group made on first run | `StarterTeam.groupName = "Team"` (`Sources/Noodle/StarterTeam.swift:15`) | Description "Ask the team anything; the personal assistant brings in whoever fits." |
| Harness | The agent program behind a bot (Codex, Claude Code, Grok Build, Muse Code, FX, OpenCode, Antigravity, Apple Intelligence) | `HarnessProvider` (`Sources/NoodleCore/Harnesses.swift:4-41`) | Settings tab "Harness" (singular since 0.10.0); the welcome instead names the account and maker: "Codex" by OpenAI, "Claude" by Anthropic, "Muse" by Meta, "Grok" by xAI (`Sources/Noodle/FirstBotSetup.swift:20-38`) |
| Model, Effort | The model a harness runs and its reasoning effort | `HarnessModel`, `HarnessEffort`, `reasoningEffort` | Visible "Effort", value "Model default" when unset, `xhigh` shown as "Extra High" (`Harnesses.swift:68-72`); accessibility name "Reasoning Effort" |
| Profile (of a bot) | The card shown when an avatar is clicked: picture, name, description, status, actions | `AgentProfileSheet` | Actions Message, Edit, Call, Usage, Computer, Browser; "Close bot profile" |
| Profile (of a harness) | A separate sign-in account for a harness | `HarnessProfile` (`Sources/NoodleCore/HarnessProfiles.swift:6`) | "Profiles", "Add Profile…", "Sign In…"; the default is called "System". The same word means two unrelated things |
| Description | Public one-liner that other bots and @ menu see | `publicDescription` | "Visible to other bots in shared groups. The private backstory below is never included." (`Overlays.swift:651`) |
| Backstory | Private role and instructions | `backstory`, stored in `agent.json` | Placeholder "Describe who this bot is, its role, tone, or priorities…" (`Overlays.swift:671`) |
| Workspace | The bot's own folder | workspace directory | "Show Workspace in Finder" |
| Folders | Extra folders shared with a bot or group | `AgentFolder` | Access "Read & Write" or "Read Only"; placeholder "Describe what this folder is for…" |
| Status | One line a bot sets about itself, at most 60 characters | `AgentRecord.status`, `statusLimit = 60` (`Models.swift:18-21`) | Set by the bot with Messenger `--set-status`; shown on the profile and over pinned bots on iPhone |
| Status dot | Runtime state of a bot | `ConversationRuntimeStatus` colours (`Sources/Noodle/Components.swift:74-81`) | Blue working, green ready, red failed, grey idle; text only in tooltip and VoiceOver value |
| Restricted, Unrestricted | Whether a bot is sandboxed to its workspace | `isExtended`, `extendedAccess`; called "Autonomous" until 0.17.0 | Status labels are lowercase "restricted" and "unrestricted"; the column heading and toggle say "Unrestricted" |
| Apps | Account apps (ChatGPT apps, Claude.ai connectors) | `appsEnabled` | Lowercase orange status "apps"; heading "Apps" |
| Tools | Connected services and built-in tools | `MCPConnection`, `MCPSettingsView`, `ToolProviderKind` | Renamed from "MCP connections" in 0.10.0, but "Custom MCP…", "MCP Server URL" and "Custom MCP Server" remain |
| Computer, Browser | Companion-app resources assigned to a bot | Noodle Computer, Noodle Browser | Editor tabs "Computers", "Browsers"; a new one is named for the bot, "Chloe’s Computer" (`CHANGELOG.md:182`) |
| Noodlet | A small app or game a bot builds, run by Noodle Applet | noodlet package | Lowercase in prose; capitalised in headers ("Noodlet Permissions", "Hub Noodlets") |
| Noodle Hub, This Mac | An always-on Mac that runs bots and lends sign-ins; "This Mac" when your own Mac plays that role | `HubMirror`, pairing | "Let My Devices Reach This Mac", "Join", "Leave", "Invite", "Hub key", "Plan", "Users", "Devices" |
| Space | A filtered sidebar: All, This Mac, one per Hub, and custom spaces | `CustomSpace` (`Shared/HubLink/Sources/HubLink/CustomSpace.swift:5`) | Menu "Spaces", ⌘1 is All |
| Pin, Archive | Keep at top; put away without deleting | `pinned`, `archivedAt` | Sidebar header "Pinned" appears only while something is pinned |
| Kick | Recover a failed bot | `kick(agent:)`, `AgentKickRequest` | Jargon verb. The confirmation names it plainly: "Recover {name}?", "Retry Now", "Resume" (`Sources/NoodleRuntime/AgentRuntimeCoordinator.swift:61-93`) |
| New Session | Restart a bot with a fresh context, keeping workspace, memory and messages | `startNewSession` | Sidebar menu and Kick dialog |
| Heartbeat | Idle wake to check for follow-up work | `AgentWakeReason.heartbeat` | "Wake idle agents", "Wake after", "Last heartbeat", "No heartbeat yet" |
| Activity, Usage | Live runtime log; token and cost chart | `AgentActivityStore`; `Window("Usage")` | "Show Activity", "Show Usage", "No Usage" |
| Float on Top, Choose Conversation | Keep a chat above other apps; pick one from anywhere | floating windows | "Open in New Window", "Show in Main Window" |
| Capture, Annotation | Screen capture and commented quotes or regions | `AttachmentAnnotation` | "Add Annotation…", "Annotate Region…", by shortcut only |
| Effect | Confetti or fireworks a bot can play | `ConversationEffectKind` | Still badge under Reduce Motion |
| Delivery | Per-message status under your messages | `MessageDelivery` saved, queued, delivered, failed | Shown as "Saved", "Sent", "Delivered", "Not delivered" (`Components.swift:522-529`) |
| Message delivery | When a busy bot sees new messages | `MessageDelivery` setting | "Automatic", "Send immediately", "Queue" |
| Companions | The suite's other apps | `CompanionApp` | Tab "Companions"; some strings still say "Companion Apps" |
| Messenger | The bots' command-line messaging tool | `messenger` CLI | Not user chrome; appears in the changelog and in bot guidance |

### 3.3 Copy rules

| # | Rule | Compliant examples | Source and counter-examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Functional labels and necessary status or errors only; no persistent hints, shortcut legends or explanatory footers | Blank detail pane; capture picker without footer; companion list without footer | `ui-copy/SKILL.md:8-14`; removals at `CHANGELOG.md:594, 624, 791, 1060, 1162`. Exceptions remain: editor captions "You can rename this bot later without changing its workspace location." (`Overlays.swift:125`) and Settings footers |
| R2 | Optional guidance goes in a tooltip, or behind a clickable heading or status label that opens a popover | Settings > Bots column headings "Heartbeat", "Unrestricted", "Apps", "Archived" are plain buttons opening 360 pt popovers (`BotsSettingsView.swift:59-84, 236-259`); status labels open "what this allows" popovers (`BotsSettingsView.swift:296-304`) | Popover shape: headline, what it allows, the default, what turning it off does and does not undo (`BotsSettingsView.swift:323-330`) |
| R3 | End a label with "…" (one character, never three dots) only when the command needs more input before it runs | "Rename…", "Edit Bot…", "Change Background…", "New Space…", "Add Device…", "Sign In…", "Install Manually…", "Choose Conversation…", "Add Annotation…", "Save as CSV…", "Custom MCP…", "Install Update…" | `ui-copy/SKILL.md:19-33`; three-dot strings in UI literals: none found; 32 distinct ellipsis labels on the Mac. Apparent violations: "Join" opens a sheet to paste an invitation (`Sources/Noodle/HubSettingsView.swift:104-109`); Mobile uses "Create Image" and "Choose Photo" but keeps "Change Background…", "New Space…", "Rename Space…" |
| R4 | No ellipsis for confirmation-only, new-item, external and toggle commands | "New Bot", "New Group", "Remove", "Delete Bot", "Delete Space", "Invite" (its sheet only shows a code), "Check for Updates", "Open System Settings", "Wallpaper Settings" | `ui-copy/SKILL.md:25-33`; `CHANGELOG.md:338-342` |
| R5 | Row actions: keep main controls in the row; secondary actions and per-item switches go in the row's "…" menu, switches as checkmark items above a divider, destructive action last; row buttons use link style | Harness rows: "Profiles", "Update", "Remove", "Local Models", "Sign In" as links (`HarnessSettingsView.swift:367-409`); Hub user rows: "Invite" link plus actions menu (`HubSettingsView.swift:429-456`) | `ui-copy/SKILL.md:35-40`; `CHANGELOG.md:537` (links "without the trailing ellipsis, so the lists take less room") |
| R6 | Annotating is by shortcut only; no Annotate button anywhere; menu commands stay | Conversation menu "Add Annotation…", "Annotate Region…" (`ConversationCommands.swift:104-109`) | `ui-copy/SKILL.md:16-17`; `CHANGELOG.md:59` removed the remaining Annotate buttons |
| R7 | Title Case for commands, buttons, menu items, tabs, window and sheet titles, empty-state titles; sentence case for settings switches, captions, explanations, tooltips that are sentences, placeholders, status labels; lowercase for inline status tags | "Keep Mac awake while agents work", "Preview web links", "Wake idle agents"; tags "restricted", "unrestricted", "apps", "home", "tailscale", "internet" (`CHANGELOG.md:161`) | Drift: Mac "Preview web links" vs Mobile "Preview Web Links" (`NoodleSettingsView.swift:206`, `Mobile/Sources/NoodleMobile/HubScreens.swift:1072`); "Nothing archived" vs "Nothing Archived"; alert titles "Usage limit reached" vs "Delete Bot?" |
| R8 | Progress text: verb in "-ing" form plus "…"; bot activity details: "-ing" phrase without ellipsis or full stop | "Checking…", "Connecting to {hub}…", "Asking the router…", "Restarting runtime…", "Still trying…"; details "Starting Codex", "Codex ready", "Checking for new messages", "Heartbeat: checking for follow-up work" | `Sources/NoodleRuntime/*`; scenario details "Running the test suite", "Opening the shop's account in the browser" |
| R9 | Confirm only what destroys data or widens access; turning access off applies at once | "Allow Unrestricted Access for {name}?" with button "Allow Unrestricted Access" (`BotsSettingsView.swift:92-104, 269-279`) | `CHANGELOG.md:557` ("Turning either off still applies at once"), `593`, `1216`; ui-copy: "A confirmation is not more input" |
| R10 | Dialog anatomy: title is a question naming the object; message says what is lost, what is kept, side effects, and "This cannot be undone." when true; the confirming button repeats verb and noun; names in curly quotes | "Delete Bot?" / "“{name}”, its workspace, and its direct conversation will be permanently deleted. It will also be removed from every group. This cannot be undone." / "Delete Bot", "Cancel" (`Overlays.swift:469-483`, `Sources/Noodle/NoodleStore.swift:1313-1319`) | Delete Space makes Cancel the default button (`ConversationCommands.swift:195-202`) |
| R11 | Errors: who or what, what happened, what to do with the exact place to do it, then what is kept | "Grok Build's usage limit has been reached. Once usage is available again, right-click the bot and choose Kick to resume. Unfinished work is preserved." ### 3.6 Design philosophy in the changelog

Recurring directions, each visible across many releases:

1. **Plain names over technical or internal ones.** SuperBot became Noodle; MCP connections became Tools; Autonomous became Unrestricted; Security became Sandbox and then merged into Bots; Chat became Conversation; the Apple harness became "Apple Intelligence"; Help > Set Up a Bot… became Help > Welcome.
2. **Remove persistent explanation; offer it on demand.** Footers, notes and badges were deleted; explanations moved into popovers opened from headings and status labels.
3. **Fewer steps and controls.** Flows advance by themselves, pickers lost Done buttons, settings with good defaults were removed, buttons duplicated by menus were removed.
4. **Asymmetric confirmation.** Confirm widening access and removal; never confirm narrowing access.
5. **Platform conventions and Messages parity.** macOS ellipsis rule, link-style row buttons, AppKit destructive red, Messages-style unread dot and Dock badge, received sound, system appearance.
6. **Stable layout.** Messages must not jump when reactions land, composer heights must not change on the first character, progress text must not move.
7. **Honesty about state.** Delivery status made meaningful, failures explained with recovery steps, nothing invented on the user's behalf.
8. **Changelog voice itself changed.** Through 0.28.1 entries are mostly imperative commit-style ("Add…", "Fix a crash…", "Connect to a Noodle Hub…"); from 0.28.2 (2026-09-27) they describe what the person now sees ("The first launch opens on a welcome…", `CHANGELOG.md:378`; "Noodle follows the system's light or dark appearance instead of always being dark.", `:336`).
